title: Intelligent Diagnosis of Peripheral Pulmonary Lesions Based on Endobronchial Ultrasound Images Using Multi-modal Features.
abstract: Lung cancer is a leading cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide. For peripheral pulmonary lesions (PPLs) that cannot be definitively diagnosed by computed tomography (CT) or positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) imaging, endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial lung biopsy (EBUS-TBLB) for pathological examinations still carries a significant possibility of indefinite diagnosis. Endobronchial ultrasound (EBUS) serves as not only a valuable and widely used guidance technique but also a superior diagnostic technique for PPLs compared with CT or PET-CT, by enabling direct visualization of the structures within the lesion and the echo distributions outside the lesion. Aimed at classifying PPLs as benign or malignant, this study enrolled 313 patients for the final analysis. Multi-modal features including clinical, radiomic, and deep features were integrated and fed into an artificial neural network for feature selection, fusion, and prediction based on the long-axis diameter of PPLs measured on CT images with a threshold of 3 cm. To reduce manual effort and maximize the diagnostic performance of multi-modal features, we employed the particle swarm optimization algorithm to automatically optimize the combination of selected features and model structure. Our method achieves an average area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.981 (95% CI: 0.953-1.000), accuracy of 0.964, sensitivity of 0.963, specificity of 0.969, and F1-score of 0.976 on the independent test dataset after four-fold cross-validation. The outstanding diagnostic performance for PPLs based on EBUS images, with all the evaluation metrics exceeding 0.95, can provide a solid foundation for clinical decision-making, biopsy site selection, and follow-up observations.
authorString: Chen Z, Feng J, Wei X, Huang L, He Q, Li S, Zhong C, Luo J.

title: Compound Lens Design and Beamforming for Wide-Field Volumetric Imaging Using a Row-Column Array.
abstract: Row-column addressed (RCA) ultrasound arrays enable volumetric imaging with a significantly reduced channel count compared to fully addressed 2-D arrays; however, their field of view (FOV) is typically limited to the transducer footprint. Diverging acoustic lenses can extend the FOV, but accurate beamforming remains challenging when the lens's finite thickness and multilayer structure are not properly modeled. This work presents a compound acoustic lens design that simultaneously achieves a large FOV, reduced edge-wave artifacts, and acceptable sensitivity loss, together with a beamforming approach that accurately accounts for wave propagation through multilayer lens structures. The proposed approach combines ray tracing with a Normal Path (RT-NP) approximation and determines the optimal propagation path using a two-dimensional Newton-Raphson optimization, enabling accurate time-of-flight (TOF) estimation while significantly reducing computational complexity compared to conventional two-interface ray-tracing methods. The method is validated experimentally using a 128+128 Vermon RCA transducer operating at 6 MHz and equipped with a BiQuadratic compound lens composed of TPX and RTV-PTFE materials. Pressure-field measurements validate the predicted wavefront expansion, while simulations indicate an FOV expansion to approximately 54.5°, enabling imaging well beyond the transducer aperture while preserving high spatial resolution and image quality. Hydrophone and RF-data measurements demonstrate sub-wavelength TOF accuracy of the proposed beamformer. The proposed system achieves a penetration depth of 75 mm compared with 90 mm without the lens, with only minor degradation in spatial resolution. These results demonstrate that compound-lens RCA systems, combined with accurate and efficient beamforming, enable wide-field volumetric imaging of organ-scale structures while preserving the practical advantages of RCA arrays, with a theoretical volume rate of approximately 104 Hz, indicating the potential for real-time 3-D visualization.

title: Automated Volumetric ROI Selection for Ultrasound Attenuation-Based Assessment of Liver Steatosis.
abstract: Quantitative ultrasound (QUS) attenuation imaging is a promising low-cost approach for hepatic steatosis assessment, but current methods remain sensitive to operator-defined region-of-interest (ROI) selection and may not fully exploit volumetric acquisitions. We present an automated multi-plane attenuation-coefficient estimation (ACE) method for matrix-array ultrasound that defines and refines the attenuation ROI through learning-based liver masking, vessel exclusion, axial range detection, model-based Aline rejection, and robust plane aggregation. The method was tuned and tested in phantoms and subsequently evaluated against same-visit MRI proton-density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) in 35 subjects with 237 volumetric acquisitions. Subject-level ACE was defined as the median across repeated acquisitions, and repeatability was quantified using the within-subject coefficient of variation (CV). Subject-level ACE was associated with MRI-PDFF, yielding Pearson r = 0.8835 (95% CI, 0.8182-0.9349), Spearman ρ = 0.9135 (95% CI, 0.7926-0.9579), and R 2 = 0.7806. The mean within-subject CV was 3.24% (95% CI, 2.82-3.67%). AUCs were 0.958 (95% CI, 0.871-1.000) for distinguishing S1+ from S0 at MRI-PDFF ≥ 6% and 0.954 (95% CI, 0.878-1.000) for distinguishing S2+ from S0/S1 at MRI-PDFF ≥ 17%. These findings support the feasibility of an automated post-acquisition volumetric attenuation-imaging pipeline that reduces dependence on manual ROI selection for quantitative liver fat assessment.

title: Boiling Histotripsy with 1.1/3.3 MHz Dual-Frequency Inducing Long-Duration Anti-Tumor Immunity in Mice Breast Cancer.
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) has a poor prognosis and high risk of recurrence and metastasis. Histotripsy is an ultrasound-guided, non-invasive, non-thermal ablation method that mechanically lyses target tissues. A boiling histotripsy (DF-MS BH) technique combining 1.1/3.3 MHz superposition with a multi-stage ultrasound pulse scheme was proposed, aiming to enhance anti-tumor immune response by optimizing pulse dose and number of treatments. A custom-designed 1.1-/3.3-MHz two-element confocal-annular array and multi-stage ultrasound pulses were used for treatment. For 6-mm-diameter tumors, the ablated volume accounted for 60-70 % of the total tumor volume. The anti-tumor immune results showed increasing pulse dose from 85 to 115 elevated DAMPs release and reduced tumor growth rate. After the first high-dose pulse treatment, the infiltration level of CD8 + T cells gradually increased and then decreased on the 7th day, which contributed to a 9-day period of tumor growth arrest. Following the second treatment, the release of danger signals was further augmented. Meanwhile, the high-level infiltration of CD8 + T cells persisted for 35 days, extending the tumor growth arrest period to 25 days and prolonging the median survival period of mice to 50 days. In addition, this treatment strategy effectively reduced the number of lung metastases, confirming its ability to enhance systemic anti-tumor immune response. Furthermore, DF-MS BH ameliorated the immunosuppressive microenvironment of TNBC through first and second enhanced treatments. Ultimately, the combination therapy of DF-MS BH and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) further suppressed tumor recurrence and metastasis.

title: Diagnostic Utility of Full-Length BP180 and Native BP180-α6β4 Integrin Complex ELISAs in Serologically Inconclusive Mucous Membrane Pemphigoid.
abstract: Mucous membrane pemphigoid (MMP) is a chronic autoimmune subepithelial blistering disorder of mucosal surfaces that can cause irreversible scarring, blindness, or dysphagia. Early diagnosis is challenging because histopathology is nonspecific and conventional BP180 NC16A ELISAs have limited sensitivity. We evaluated ELISAs using full-length recombinant BP180 and a native BP180-α6β4 integrin complex in six patients with suspected oral or ocular MMP. The conventional NC16A ELISA was negative in four of six patients, and biopsy alone was often insufficient. Both assays provided useful serological support in a subset of cases when interpreted alongside direct immunofluorescence (DIF) and clinical phenotype, whereas in others DIF remained the primary basis for diagnosis. These assays can therefore complement, but not replace, clinicopathological assessment in suspected MMP.

title: Green Ultrasound-Assisted Extraction of Bioactive Phenolics From Quince (Cydonia oblonga) Leaves: Multi-Response Optimization, LC-MS/MS Profiling, and Comparison With Conventional Methods.
abstract: Quince (Cydonia oblonga Mill.) leaves are an abundant yet underutilized agricultural by-product that is rich in phenolic compounds and therefore represents a promising feedstock for value-added bioactive extracts. This study optimized the green ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE) of bioactive compounds from quince leaves using a sequential statistical approach based on Plackett-Burman screening and Taguchi-based criteria importance through intercriteria correlation (CRITIC)-weighted grey relational analysis (GRA). Under the optimum conditions (solid-to-liquid ratio 3:50 g/mL, 50% (v/v) ethanol, and 75°C), the extract exhibited a total phenolic content (TPC) of 9210.44 ± 138.25 mg GAE L - 1 , a total flavonoid content (TFC) of 6180.67 ± 94.25 mg CE L - 1 and a DPPH free radical-scavenging capacity of 76.53 ± 3.65 mmol TE L - 1 . Triplicate confirmation experiments validated the model, with an overall prediction accuracy of 97.69%. Ethanol concentration exerted the greatest influence on the grey relational grade (36.28%). Under identical operating conditions, the optimized UAE provided the most balanced extraction performance. It yielded the highest TPC, antioxidant activity, anti-inflammatory activity, and α-amylase inhibition relative to maceration, magnetic stirring, hand-shaking, and reflux, while LC-MS/MS identified quinic and chlorogenic acids as the principal constituents. These results indicate that the UAE optimized through a Taguchi-based CRITIC-weighted GRA is an effective and sustainable strategy for producing bioactive-rich extracts from quince-leaf waste. PRACTICAL APPLICATIONS: This study provides a practical, statistically grounded route for converting quince (Cydonia oblonga Mill.) leaf waste, an abundant agro-industrial by-product, into phenolic-rich extracts using a green, food-grade ultrasound-assisted process. The sequential screening and multi-response optimization framework can be adopted by food, nutraceutical, and functional-ingredient manufacturers to maximize antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and enzyme-inhibitory activities while minimizing solvent and energy use, supporting cost-effective and sustainable valorization of leaf biomass.

title: Bioactive Peptides in Functional Foods: From Production and Validation to Commercialization, Regulatory Hurdles, and Future Prospects.
abstract: Bioactive peptides (BAPs) exhibit a wide range of health-promoting properties, positioning them as key ingredients for the functional food market. This review provides a comprehensive assessment of the BAP landscape, from discovery and production to commercialization and regulation. Conventional and emerging production technologies are critically analyzed, highlighting advancements in enzymatic hydrolysis, microbial fermentation, and physical processing methods like high-pressure and ultrasound-assisted extraction. The multi-tiered validation pipeline, spanning in silico prediction, in vitro screening, and in vivo models, is examined, revealing a significant disconnect between preliminary bioactivity data and demonstrable clinical efficacy, which is a primary cause for regulatory failure. Commercialization is hampered by technical challenges, including poor bioavailability, gastrointestinal instability, and undesirable sensory attributes, which are being addressed by innovative formulation strategies such as nano-encapsulation. A comparative analysis of global regulatory frameworks, particularly the divergent approaches of the US FDA and EU EFSA, underscores the hurdles in substantiating health claims, with a universal demand for rigorous human clinical trials. Finally, the future prospects are explored, identifying critical research gaps and highlighting the transformative potential of AI-driven peptide design and personalized nutrition through nutrigenomics to unlock the full potential of BAPs. The review further links peptide structure to nine major biological activities, critically compares advanced delivery systems and manufacturing scale-up, and extends the regulatory analysis to major Asia-Pacific markets.

title: MR Imaging and Radiomics Features for Predicting Variant Histology of Bladder Cancer: A Single Centre Retrospective Analysis.
abstract: Introduction Compare MRI features of bladder variant histology (VH) and pure urothelial carcinoma (UC) and determine if MRI radiomics features can predict VH. Methods In this retrospective study, cystectomy pathology database search yielded 37 patients with tumours with more than 50% VH and preoperative MRI's. Cystectomy database search yielded 38 consecutive patients with pure UC and preoperative MRI's. Three radiologists characterized MRI T2, diffusion-weighted, apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps and postcontrast features of bladder tumours. Inter-reader agreement was assessed using Gwet's agreement and intra-class coefficients. Another radiologist segmented bladder tumours and adjacent perivesical fat on T2-weighted and ADC images using radiomics software. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) was used to determine radiomics features that distinguished VH from UC. Fifty datasets were prepared using multiple imputation approach, and variables were normalized for LASSO variable selection. Results Patients with VH (mean age = 68, 54 (72%) men) included squamous cell (n = 17), sarcomatoid (n = 6), plasmacytoid (n = 6), adenocarcinoma (n = 4) and small cell (n = 4) variants. Inter-reader agreement was similar for VH and UC (p > 0.44). All readers characterized all squamous cell carcinoma as T2 intermediate. For two of three readers, 92%-100% of hypoenhancing tumours were VH at pathology whereas 74%-78% of hyperenhancing masses were UC (p = 0.001). Combination of 11 selected radiomics features had AUC of 0.98 for training and 0.95 for validation data for prediction of VH. Conclusion Squamous cell carcinoma was T2 intermediate, and VH was more likely to hypoenhance compared to UC. Our radiomic model had excellent performance for predicting VH.

title: Impact of Breast Density and Other Factors on Mammography Guided Vacuum Assisted Breast Biopsy Microcalcification Retrieval Rates.
abstract: Introduction Mammography guided vacuum-assisted biopsy (MG-VAB) is the preferred method for histological diagnosis of screening mammography detected microcalcifications, yet the influence of breast density as well as other patient and procedure-specific factors on retrieval remains underexplored. The purpose of this study is to assess the impact of patient and procedure-specific factors on MG-VAB microcalcification retrieval rates. Methods A retrospective cohort study of 803 consecutive MG-VAB procedures for breast calcifications performed between August 2017 and May 2023 in the BreastScreen ACT population was conducted. Patient data collected included age, breast density, compressed breast thickness, lesion quadrant, calcification size, nipple-to-lesion distance, biopsy approach, specimen radiography visibility as well as presence on pathology. Bayesian logistic regression with weakly informative priors was applied to estimate microcalcification retrieval rates (MRR) and 90% credible intervals. Results The overall median MRR was 98.27% (790/803). Retrieval remained high across age groups (96.4%-99.6%), breast density (95.1%-98.7%), lesion quadrants (96.8%-99.1%), biopsy approach (97.9%-98.6%). Continuous factors such as compressed breast thickness, calcification size and nipple-to-lesion distance demonstrated stable retrieval across ranges. Conclusion MG-VAB achieves consistently high microcalcification retrieval rates across a range of patient and procedural factors, including breast density. These findings reinforce its role as the first line diagnostic method for screening detected microcalcifications.

title: From Recall to Reassurance: Common Benign Mimics in Breast Screening Assessment-A Pictorial Review.
abstract: Benign breast lesions, anatomical variants, and imaging artefacts can closely mimic malignancy on screening mammography and are a frequent diagnostic challenge in the assessment setting. This pictorial review showcases a spectrum of benign lesions encountered in a high-volume breast screening assessment setting that initially raised suspicion for malignancy but were subsequently confirmed as benign through a combination of digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT), targeted ultrasound, and clinicopathological correlation. Examples include cutaneous lesions, sebaceous cysts, intramammary lymph nodes, hamartomas, fat necrosis, vascular lesions, simple cysts and summation artefact. Through illustrative cases, we highlight key imaging features that support accurate lesion characterization and demonstrate the complementary roles of mammography, DBT, and ultrasound in distinguishing benign entities from breast cancer. Familiarity with these imaging appearances can improve diagnostic confidence, reduce false-positive recalls, and minimize unnecessary biopsies within breast screening programs.

title: Can Simple MRI Characteristics Predict Molecular Subgroups in Paediatric Medulloblastoma?
abstract: Introduction Medulloblastoma is the most common malignant paediatric central nervous system (CNS) tumour and is classified using molecular subgroups: WNT, SHH and non-WNT/non-SHH. Subgroup identification guides prognosis and treatment, but requires molecular testing, which is not universally available. MRI is routine in assessment of CNS tumours, and the MRI characteristics may serve as surrogate markers for medulloblastoma subgrouping. This study aims to use simple MRI surrogate markers identified by Perreault et al., against local medulloblastoma cases and their final molecular outcome. Method Retrospective cohort study of paediatric medulloblastomas at a single tertiary children's hospital between January 2015 and October 2025. MRI studies were reviewed by a paediatric neuroradiologist and a radiology registrar in consensus. Tumours were classified by location (cerebellar hemisphere, cerebellopontine angle/cerebellar peduncle (CP/CPA), or midline/fourth ventricle) and enhancement pattern (minimal/none = < 10%, heterogeneous = 10%-90%, solid = > 90%). Associations between MRI features and molecular subgroup were assessed. Results Twenty-two cases were analysed: SHH 22.7% (5/22), WNT 13.6% (3/22) and non-WNT/non-SHH 63.7% (14/22). Most tumours were midline (90.9%), with two hemispheric lesions and no CP/CPA. Enhancement patterns were heterogeneous (54.5%), solid (36.4%) and minimal/none (9.1%). Hemispheric location was associated with SHH tumours (p = 0.043), and all WNT tumours demonstrated solid enhancement (p = 0.036). No other statistically significant associations were identified. Conclusion MRI characteristics offer promising surrogate markers for medulloblastoma subtype. The only strong predictor we found corresponding with Perreault et al. is that hemispheric lesions are correlated with SHH-activated medulloblastoma. This supports further investigation of MRI markers as non-invasive and preoperative medulloblastoma subgroup prediction.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Scoring System and Exploratory Multiomics in Ankylosing Spondylitis: Hip Severity and Age-at-Severe-Hip-Involvement Stratification.
abstract: Introduction Accurate diagnosis and assessment of hip involvement are important for the clinical management of ankylosing spondylitis (AS). This study aimed to develop and internally validate an artificial intelligence-based Ensemble Scoring System (ESS) for AS diagnosis and hip-disease severity assessment and to explore its association with heterogeneous immune-cell infiltration and age at first documented severe hip involvement. Methods A total of 5721 patients with pelvic radiographs and linked clinical records were retrospectively included. Participants were divided into training and held-out validation cohorts at a 7:3 ratio strictly at the patient level, with no patient or image overlap. Deep-learning features extracted by a convolutional neural network were integrated with clinical variables using XGBoost to construct task-specific ensemble deep-learning (EDL) models. Exploratory proteomic, transcriptomic, single-cell RNA-sequencing, immunohistochemical, and peripheral-blood analyses were performed to investigate AS-related immune infiltration. An exploratory immune ensemble (IE) score was constructed using the monocyte proportion and EDL score. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to examine the association between the IE score and age at severe hip involvement. Results The EDL model achieved AUCs of 0.978 for distinguishing AS from non-AS, 0.990 for identifying hip arthropathy among patients with AS, and 0.996 for identifying BASRI-Hip grade ≥ 3 among patients with hip arthropathy. Monocyte percentage was an influential feature across the three EDL classification tasks. Exploratory multiomics and immunohistochemical analyses showed higher LYN expression in AS than in the corresponding non-AS fracture-control groups and suggested that LYN expression was concentrated predominantly in monocytes. A high IE score was associated with earlier severe hip involvement, with estimated median ages at first documented severe hip involvement of 36 and 50 years in the high- and low-IE-score groups, respectively. This finding represents exploratory risk stratification and does not establish independent prediction of biological disease progression. Conclusions The ESS showed strong internal validation performance for AS diagnosis and hip-disease severity classification. Exploratory analyses linked LYN dysregulation in monocytes with heterogeneous immune infiltration, while the IE score was associated with earlier severe hip involvement. Prospective multicenter external validation is required before clinical application.

title: Nodule Dye-Localization Using Interventional Fluoroscopy for Image-Guided Sublobar Lung Resection.
abstract: Background Precise localization is critical for sublobar resection of small pulmonary nodules. We evaluated the safety, technical efficiency, and clinical outcomes of preoperative percutaneous dye-localization using a cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)-enabled flat-panel detector interventional fluoroscopy system in a hybrid operating room (HOR). Methods We retrospectively reviewed 74 consecutive patients (137 lesions) who underwent image-guided localization followed by video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) sublobar resection (wedge resection or segmentectomy) between 2022 and 2023 at Chia-Yi Christian Hospital. Procedural workflow, localization success, surgical margins, and perioperative outcomes were systematically analyzed. Results Technical localization success was achieved in 100% of lesions (mean nodule diameter: 8.59 ± 4.85 mm). The procedure required a mean of 1.31 ± 0.67 puncture attempts per lesion at a mean depth of 5.22 ± 1.86 cm. Procedure-related pneumothorax occurred in 29.7% (22/74) of patients, with 14.9% (11/74) requiring pigtail catheter drainage; pneumothorax occurrence was significantly associated with multiple puncture attempts (p < 0.001) and lower-lobe lesions (p = 0.001). Lower-lobe location was significantly associated with requiring more puncture attempts (p = 0.028). For malignant lesions, the mean pathological resection margin was 17.16 ± 8.73 mm, with 92.31% achieving a margin-to-tumor ratio (MTR) ≥ 1. The mean postoperative hospital stay was 3.04 ± 1.16 days. Conclusions Single-stage image-guided dye-localization and VATS sublobar lung resection in an HOR using a biplane CBCT-enabled platform is safe, feasible, and effective. This streamlined workflow ensures high technical success and adequate surgical margins with manageable complications. Further studies are warranted to evaluate long-term oncological outcomes.

title: Machine Learning-Based Screening for Osteonecrosis of the Jaw in Panoramic Radiographs.
abstract: Background Osteonecrosis of the jaw (ONJ) is a serious condition associated mainly with antiresorptive therapy and maxillofacial radiotherapy. As detection of its radiographic findings may facilitate patient referral, this study aimed to develop convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for ONJ screening in panoramic radiographs (OPGs). Methods A dataset of 888 ONJ-positive OPGs and 888 ONJ-negative controls was assembled and annotated using bounding boxes. The dataset was split at patient level 70-10-20 for training, validation, and testing. Multiple CNNs (ResNet18, ResNet34, MobileNetV2, EfficientNet-B0) were trained on cropped image regions and evaluated using standard performance metrics. Performance on full OPGs (without cropping) was tested, and subgroup analysis was performed. Regions contributing to model predictions were visualised using Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM). Results EfficientNet-B0 performed best, with per-crop accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score of 92.24%, 89.80%, 94.69%, 94.42% and 82.05%, respectively. At 0.9 probability threshold, per-image accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score equalled 76.65%. Grad-CAM highlighted clinically relevant regions; however, differentiation from other changes in bone density was suboptimal. Conclusions Despite promising results at crop level, model performance in full OPG analysis is currently insufficient for clinical application. Further optimisation of localisation strategies and external validation are needed for reliable clinical application.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Paediatric Dentistry: A Scoping Review.
abstract: This review scoped artificial intelligence (AI) in paediatric dentistry to summarize current applications and limitations. A comprehensive literature search was completed across PubMed, Google Scholar, Scopus, Embase, IEEE Xplore, and medRxiv/aArXiv. The preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) checklist was used for reporting the present study. Studies concerning paediatric dentistry and utilizing AI, machine learning (ML) or large language models (LLMs) were included. Two independent reviewers screened and three extracted data on AI methodologies, performance metrics, and clinical applications. Fifty-nine studies were included. Computer vision studies (n = 32) most often used panoramic radiographs (n = 14), mainly for tooth detection, numbering and segmentation (n = 10) and caries detection (n = 9). Non-imaging ML studies (n = 18) primarily used clinical variables and questionnaire data (n = 8) or salivary/biological samples (n = 10). Accuracy ranged from 50% to 100%, with sensitivity reaching 100% in biomarker-based studies. LLM accuracy varied widely (33%-96%). Computer vision and non-imaging ML show promise for paediatric dentistry, particularly in the detection of dental structures and diseases, as well as risk stratification. Variable LLM performance underscores the need for standardized evaluation before clinical integration. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: AI-based tools may support paediatric dentists by improving tooth detection, dental structure assessment, caries detection, disease prediction and risk stratification. Computer vision and non-imaging machine learning approaches appear to have potential, but their clinical value depends on robust external validation, transparent reporting and integration into paediatric dental workflows. Given their variable performance, AI tools should be used only as adjunctive tools or a second reviewer.

title: Morphological, Radiographic and Three-Dimensional Scanning Characterization of the Skull and Mandible of the American Crocodile (Crocodylus acutus).
abstract: The American crocodile (Crocodylus acutus) is a widely distributed Neotropical species for which detailed osteological descriptions of the skull and mandible remain scarce. This study provides an integrative characterization of the cranial and mandibular complex using gross anatomy, descriptive cranial morphometry, radiography, and three-dimensional (3D) scanning. Four skulls and mandibles from post mortem specimens were prepared following standard osteological procedures, and descriptive cranial measurements were recorded. Radiographic projection allowed visualization of bone margins, cranial sutures, dental alveoli, fenestrae, and articular regions. Three-dimensional models generated through a structured-light 3D scanning workflow documented external contours, choanal margins, temporal and mandibular fenestrae, alveolar borders, and sutural patterns. In dorsal, ventral, lateral, and caudal views, the examined skulls displayed an elongated rostrum, dorsally positioned orbits and external nares, paired supratemporal and lateral temporal fenestrae, and a single occipital condyle. The mandibles exhibited elongated and firmly fused symphyses, pronounced retroarticular processes, and well-defined internal and external mandibular fenestrae. Dental preservation varied among specimens, but tooth spacing, conical morphology, and rostrocaudal size variation could be documented in the preserved series. These findings provide a specimen-based reference for the cranial and mandibular complex of C. acutus by integrating morphological, morphometric, radiographic, and three-dimensional (3D) scanning evidence. The digital models constitute an additional resource for anatomical teaching, comparative studies, and long-term digital documentation of osteological morphology.

title: Investigating Artificial Intelligence Performance on Mammographic Cases in High- and Low-Resourced Countries.
abstract: Population-based screening in Australia for breast cancer using mammography has delivered key outcomes in reducing deaths, but such programs are usually not present in Vietnam. Breast cancer is common in both countries, with Vietnamese women having high breast density and Vietnam having low radiology expertise. This paper investigated the performance of two state-of-the-art Artificial Intelligence (AI) models for cancer detection on Datasets 1 and 2 (Vietnam and Australian mammographic cases) and determined whether the breast density in the two datasets with different vendors affected the AI performance. Both datasets consisted of the same number of mammographic cases (865 malignant; 865 normal). Mammographic images were enhanced using the contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization algorithm. Transfer learning of the Globally-aware Multiple Instance Classifier (GMIC) and Global-Local Activation Maps (GLAM) AI models was conducted on enhanced images in the two national datasets. The breast density was classified as four levels (A, B, C, and D) by three radiologists. We combined Levels A and B into 0%-50%, and Levels C and D into 50%-100% breast density. The performance of these two AI models, both with and without transfer learning, was evaluated on the two datasets using McNemar's test. The GMIC in the pre-trained and transfer learning modes outperformed the GLAM in terms of specificity and sensitivity in the two datasets. The performance of the GMIC and GLAM with transfer learning in Dataset 2 was better, with 86.7% specificity and 88.2% sensitivity, outperforming their transfer learning model with 80.4% specificity and 81.2% sensitivity in Dataset 1. The specificity and sensitivity of the two AI models (p-values <0.05) were significantly improved using transfer learning in the two datasets. The specificity and sensitivity of GMIC with transfer learning (p-values <0.05) on the 0%-50% and 50%-100% breast density in Dataset 2 were significantly higher than those in Dataset 1, respectively.

title: Emerging Roles of Gold Nanoparticles in Lung Cancer Diagnosis and Imaging: A Promising yet Underexplored Frontier.
abstract: Cancer is known to be a major cause of death worldwide, with lung cancer responsible for the maximum number of deaths. There is an urgent need for early and effective diagnosis of lung cancer to improve the overall survival rate, which is extremely low to date. Studies have shown that 57% of lung cancers are detected only after metastasis of the tumor. Economic restraints in hospitals are resulting in decreased early diagnosis of lung cancer and an increase in aggressive, incurable grades. Traditional imaging modalities like ultrasound, x-ray, CT, and MRI scans are often unable to precisely locate the extent of metastasis of lung cancer, paving the way for better, more sophisticated diagnostic tools. Nuclear medicine techniques help in better understanding of the metabolic extent of cancer cells using radioactive isotopes. PET/SPECT scans help provide more precise grading and better understanding of tumor morphology. However, the lack of distinction between inflammatory and malignant lesions remains a diagnostic challenge. Gold nanoparticles (GNPs) have been studied as effective contrast agents, enhancing the diagnostic efficiency of lung cancer. Formulation and tagging of GNPs have improved efficacy and biodistribution of cancer drugs; however, no such gold nanoformulation is available for diagnosis to date. The use of different shapes of GNPs functionalized with specific lung cancer biomarkers can potentially increase the specificity of lung tumor diagnosis. In this review, we address the lacunae and provide a strategic roadmap for the effective development of GNP-based diagnostics, from benchtop to high-fidelity biomaterials with clinical applications for efficient lung cancer management.

title: Transvaginal Ultrasound for Endometriosis: Learning From a Decade of Diagnostic Challenges Through a Retrospective Observational Cohort Study.
abstract: Background Endometriosis is a chronic, inflammatory condition associated with pelvic pain, subfertility, and reduced quality of life. Advances in enhanced transvaginal ultrasound (eTVUS), including systematic compartment-based scanning protocols and improved operator training, have increased diagnostic accuracy, particularly for deep endometriosis. Aims To evaluate and critically reflect on the diagnostic performance of eTVUS during its implementation prior to the adoption of standardised scanning protocols. Using the #ENZIAN classification system, the diagnostic performance of eTVUS was assessed by comparing ultrasound findings with laparoscopic visualisation as the reference standard. Methods A retrospective observational study of patients with suspected endometriosis who underwent preoperative eTVUS and subsequent laparoscopy between January 2015 and January 2024 at a single tertiary hospital. Ultrasound and surgical findings were mapped to #ENZIAN compartments and grades. Agreement and diagnostic metrics were calculated using laparoscopy as the reference standard. Results Among 221 patients with paired ultrasound and laparoscopy, adnexal endometriomas were detected with a sensitivity of 81.4% and specificity of 84.1%. Tubo-ovarian complex disease demonstrated a sensitivity of 72.9% and specificity of 68.8%. Sensitivity for deep endometriosis was lower, with specificity for detection depending on anatomical location varying from 83%-95%. Bladder involvement had a PPV of 83.3% and NPV of 94.8%; ureteric disease had a PPV of 0% and NPV of ~100%. Peritoneal disease was rarely identified. Conclusion eTVUS demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy for ovarian endometriomas, moderate performance for bowel involvement, and low sensitivity for peritoneal disease.

title: Computed Tomography-Derived Abdominal Aortic Calcification Independently Predicts Survival in Rectal Cancer Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background Contemporary rectal cancer treatment pathways remain predominantly guided by tumour-related characteristics, including stage and histopathology, with comparatively limited objective assessment of physiological reserve for treatment planning. Aortic calcification represents a potential imaging biomarker reflecting systemic vascular disease, chronic inflammation and physiological reserve. We evaluated computed tomography (CT)-derived abdominal aortic calcification as a prognostic imaging biomarker for postoperative outcomes and long-term survival. Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the prospectively maintained Australian Comprehensive Cancer Outcomes and Research Database (ACCORD) of rectal cancer patients treated between 2013 and 2022. Pre-treatment staging CT was subjected to semi-automated volumetric quantification of calcium using 3D Slicer software. Calcification volume was assessed segmentally at vertebral levels L1-L4 and at the iliac vessels. Primary outcomes were major postoperative complications (Clavien-Dindo ≥ III) and overall survival. Cox proportional hazards modelling was performed using a prespecified parsimonious multivariable model. Results A total of 174 patients were included in the analysis. Increasing calcification burden demonstrated no statistically significant association with major postoperative complications (OR 1.09 per 1000-unit increase; 95% CI 0.99-1.19; p = 0.07). Increasing calcification independently predicted worse 5-year survival after multivariable adjustment (HR 1.17 per 1000-unit increase ([CI 1.08-1.28, p = 0.001]). Kaplan-Meier analyses showed separation between calcification groups, although dichotomised analyses did not reach statistical significance. Conclusion Aortic calcification independently predicts long-term survival following rectal cancer surgery but not short-term postoperative complications. Quantitative CT-derived calcification assessment may provide a rapid, objective imaging biomarker that reflects physiological reserve and represents a potential adjunct to future risk stratification pathways.

title: Acute Perinatal Stroke Characteristics and Outcome in Southern Finland.
abstract: Aim Perinatal stroke can cause lifelong morbidities. Outcome prediction is important for parental guidance and follow-up. We studied characteristics of acute perinatal stroke in a Finnish cohort. Methods We performed a population-based study, identifying infants with acute neonatal cerebral ischemia or sinovenous thrombosis (CSVT) in Southern Finland from 2010 to 2023. We analysed the incidence of stroke types, seizures, anti-seizure medication use, and outcomes. Results Altogether 88 infants (1 in 3101 live births) were diagnosed with acute perinatal stroke: 67% with arterial ischemic stroke (AIS), 22% with hemorrhagic stroke (HS) and 11% with CSVT. Seizures and anti-seizure medication use occurred in 78% of infants. Cranial ultrasound infrequently recognized AIS but usually noted haemorrhage. During follow-up, 34% of infants had no adverse outcome diagnosis. The most common outcome was cerebral palsy (CP, 35%). A combination of CP with epilepsy or seizures was more frequent in infants with AIS than in those with other stroke types. Conclusion The distribution of stroke types, symptoms, and adverse outcomes aligns with the previous literature. Acute seizures were common in AIS and HS patients. No recurrent strokes occurred during follow-up and underlying infant-related etiologies were rarely identified.

title: Radiation therapy for persistent or progressive mediastinal lymphoma after chemotherapy in FeLV-positive cats: a retrospective case series of four cats.
abstract: Background Mediastinal lymphoma in feline leukaemia virus (FeLV)-positive cats is associated with a poor prognosis, and therapeutic options may be limited when adequate disease control is not achieved with chemotherapy. The efficacy of radiation therapy in this setting has not been established. Case report Medical records were retrospectively reviewed for FeLV-positive cats diagnosed with mediastinal lymphoma between November 2018 and December 2024 that had persistent or progressive mediastinal disease after chemotherapy and were subsequently treated with radiation therapy. Treatment response was assessed by computed tomography using the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours (RECIST). Three of four cats (75%) responded to radiation therapy (two complete responses, one partial response). Respiratory signs improved rapidly in three cats (median 5 days). Local disease control was achieved in most cases; however, three cats developed progression at other sites. Survival times were 45, 150 and 352 days in cats that died, and one cat remained alive for >626 days at the time of last follow-up. No severe radiation-related adverse effects were documented during the available follow-up, although systematic evaluation of late radiation toxicity was not possible. Conclusion Radiation therapy may provide local control and rapid palliation of respiratory signs in FeLV-positive cats with persistent or progressive mediastinal lymphoma after chemotherapy. Further studies with larger cohorts are warranted.

title: Radiographic measurements of cardiac silhouette and skeletal landmarks in companion galahs (Eolophus roseicapilla) and sulphur-crested cockatoos (Cacatua galerita).
abstract: Introduction Cardiac disease is common in companion birds, yet its diagnosis remains a challenge due to limited validated tests. Radiography is frequently used to assess cardiac size in birds; however, interspecies variation necessitates species-specific reference intervals. This study aimed to establish the cardiac silhouette in companion galahs (Eolophus roseicapilla) and sulphur-crested cockatoos (Cacatua galerita). Methods Ventrodorsal (VD) and laterolateral (LL) radiographs of 30 adult galahs and 21 adult cockatoos were obtained from medical records that were admitted to the University of Queensland Veterinary Teaching Hospital from 2013 to 2023. In the VD view, cardiac width (CW) was measured with other anatomical landmarks including thoracic width (TW), clavicular distance (ClD), coracoid width (CoW) and 3rd-4th rib distance (RD). In the LL view, the cardiac length (CL) was measured and correlated to sternal length (SL). Results Significant positive correlations were found between CW and weight ( ρ=0.777 , p < 0.001); CW and TW ( ρ=0.789 , p < 0.001), in galahs. In cockatoos, significant positive correlations were found between CW and CoW ( ρ=0.541 , p = 0.011); CW and ClD ( ρ=0.491 , p < 0.021). The 25th-75th percentile range (PR) for CW:TW ranged from 52 to 62.5% and 60-65% in cockatoos and galahs, respectively. Conclusion In galahs, CW correlated positively with the TW, and the 25th-75th PR for CW:TW should be 60%-65%. In cockatoos, the CW is better correlated to the CoW and ClD with the 25th-75th PRI of 549.5%-609.5% and 91.5%-103.0% respectively. The cardiac silhouette was larger in galahs than in cockatoos.

title: Long-term follow-up and post-operative computed tomography surveillance following adrenalectomy in dogs.
abstract: Adrenal gland tumours in dogs have historically been associated with a guarded prognosis due to reported high perioperative mortality, recurrence and metastatic disease. More recent studies suggest improved outcomes following adrenalectomy. This retrospective study evaluated long-term outcomes and postoperative computed tomography (CT) findings in dogs undergoing adrenalectomy, focusing on the detection of recurrence, metastasis and newly developed pathology. Medical records of dogs treated with unilateral or bilateral adrenalectomy at The Animal Hospital at Murdoch University between January 2016 and February 2026 were reviewed. Inclusion criteria required preoperative thoracic and abdominal CT, histopathological diagnosis and follow-up CT at least 4 months postoperatively. Signalment, CT findings, surgical details, histopathology, postoperative CT findings and survival data were recorded. Twenty dogs met the inclusion criteria. Histopathology revealed phaeochromocytoma (8), adrenocortical carcinoma (5) and adrenocortical adenoma (7). Follow-up CT was performed at a median of 11.5 months (range 4-42 months). No local tumour recurrence was identified. New lesions detected in five dogs were confirmed as unrelated primary neoplasms = rather than adrenal metastases. Long-term follow-up was available for 16 dogs; 12 were alive at a median of 30 months after surgery, and deaths were unrelated to adrenal disease. Adrenalectomy effectively resolved primary adrenal disease in this cohort. Postoperative CT surveillance was valuable for excluding recurrence and progressive metastatic disease, and identifying unrelated, potentially treatable conditions before the onset of clinical signs, thus supporting its role in optimising long-term outcomes in dogs undergoing adrenalectomy.

title: The PSA test for prostate cancer screening: an abridged Cochrane review.
abstract: Objectives To assess the effects of prostate cancer screening compared to no screening in men with no prior diagnosis of prostate cancer. Methods This systematic review represents an update of a prior Cochrane review from 2013, searching multiple databases up to November 2025. We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) of prostate cancer screening vs no screening. We used standard Cochrane methods, including rating the certainty of the evidence following a Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. Results Six RCTs (789 086 participants; follow-up 3.2-23 years) were included: five evaluated prostate-specific antigen (PSA)-alone screening; one evaluated PSA combined with a kallikrein panel and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) (ProScreen). Results are based on the certainty of evidence for each outcome and are therefore mainly derived from a sensitivity analysis by risk of bias, using the European Randomised Study of Screening for Prostate Cancer (ERSPC) trial: screening likely results in a reduction in prostate cancer-specific mortality (sensitivity analysis from ERSPC: risk ratio [RR] 0.87, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.80-0.95; one study, 162 236 participants; moderate-certainty evidence; minimal clinically important difference [MCID]: one per 1000 participants). Assuming a baseline risk of 16 prostate-cancer-related deaths per 1000, this corresponds to two fewer (95% CI three fewer to one fewer) per 1000. Based on the analysis that included all eligible trials, screening may reduce overall mortality, although the CI includes the possibility of little to no effect (RR 0.99, 95% CI 0.97-1.00; I 2 = 22%; four studies, 675 121 participants; low-certainty evidence; MCID: one per 1000 participants). Assuming a baseline risk of 491 deaths from any cause per 1000, this corresponds to five fewer (95% CI 15 fewer to 0 fewer) per 1000. Screening may result in little to no difference in adverse events (RR 1.32, 95% CI 0.48-3.65; low certainty) or quality of life. In the ProScreen trial (60 745 participants, 3.2-year follow-up), combined screening probably has little to no effect on overall detection (RR 1.85, 95% CI 1.56-2.19; moderate certainty), localised detection (RR 1.88, 95% CI 1.55-2.27; moderate certainty), or advanced detection (RR 1.78, 95% CI 1.19-2.66; moderate certainty). Mortality data are not yet mature. Conclusions Screening likely reduces prostate cancer-specific mortality and may reduce overall mortality. It may have little to no effect on adverse events (as measured by intervention-related mortality). Study limitations, inconsistency, and imprecision reduced our confidence in the effect estimates. Interpretation of these findings is highly sensitive to the choice of MCID. Emerging alternatives, such as screening with a kallikrein panel and MRI, may have little to no effect on diagnoses of prostate cancer, but the results on mortality are not yet known.

Assuming a baseline risk of 491 deaths from any cause per 1000, this corresponds to five fewer (95% CI 15 fewer to 0 fewer) per 1000. Screening may result in little to no difference in adverse events (RR 1.32, 95% CI 0.48-3.65; low certainty) or quality of life. In the ProScreen trial (60 745 participants, 3.2-year follow-up), combined screening probably has little to no effect on overall detection (RR 1.85, 95% CI 1.56-2.19; moderate certainty), localised detection (RR 1.88, 95% CI 1.55-2.27; moderate certainty), or advanced detection (RR 1.78, 95% CI 1.19-2.66; moderate certainty). Mortality data are not yet mature.

Conclusions

Screening likely reduces prostate cancer-specific mortality and may reduce overall mortality. It may have little to no effect on adverse events (as measured by intervention-related mortality). Study limitations, inconsistency, and imprecision reduced our confidence in the effect estimates. Interpretation of these findings is highly sensitive to the choice of MCID. Emerging alternatives, such as screening with a kallikrein panel and MRI, may have little to no effect on diagnoses of prostate cancer, but the results on mortality are not yet known.

title: The PENIMA project: artificial intelligence decision-support tool for penile lesions - protocol paper and invitation to participate.
abstract: Objectives To present and describe the design, data collection framework, and interim cohort characteristics of the PENIMA project, a multicentre initiative establishing a clinically annotated penile lesion image repository to support future artificial intelligence (AI)-driven decision-support development - and to encourage urology and dermatology colleagues working with penile lesions to participate in the project. Patients and methods Prospective participant inclusion commenced in March 2023 across Scandinavian urological and dermatological departments. Patients with penile anatomy undergoing clinically indicated genital examination are invited to participate and provide oral and written consent as defined by local authority regulations. Clinical photographs and structured metadata are collected. Lesion classification is based on a specialist evaluation, clinical follow-up and histopathology when available. Images are pseudonymised and annotated using a secure, containerised Computer Vision Annotation Tool (CVAT) environment. Supervised machine-learning model development using convolutional neural networks is planned with patient-level dataset partitioning and evaluation using standard diagnostic performance metrics. The study was approved by relevant local authorities, and the approval number is 1-10-72-150-22. Results As of February 2026, 1125 participants and approximately 7000 images have been included. In all, 40% represented normal anatomical variants. Among lesional cases, 33% are clinically assessed as benign, 13% premalignant, and 8% malignant; 22% of all cases have histopathological verification. Concordance between clinical suspicion and histopathology is highest for penile carcinoma (84.6%, 95% confidence interval 75.0-91.0%). Conclusion The PENIMA project includes a multicentre, clinically grounded image repository reflecting real-world penile lesion presentations. The feasible and successful infrastructure provides a foundation for future development and validation of image-based clinical decision-support tools.

title: An artificial intelligence model combining MRI and ultrasound images (MRUSuNet) for prostate cancer detection outperforms radiologist MRI interpretation.
abstract: Objectives To develop the magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-UltraSound UNet (MRUSuNet), a model that uses both MRI and transrectal ultrasonography (TRUS) as input to detect and localise the three-dimensional spatial volume of clinically significant prostate cancer on TRUS images to allow better visualisation of cancer in the TRUS space. Patients and methods Pre-biopsy MRI is increasingly used to target suspicious prostate lesions. The lesions identified by radiologists are mapped onto TRUS images to enable real-time targeting during the biopsy. Yet, the misalignment of MRI and TRUS results in sampling errors, and in some cases even missing the clinically significant cancers. This study included two MRI-TRUS fusion biopsy cohorts (3000 patients) for model development, and one radical prostatectomy cohort (110 patients) used for independent validation and for the comparison with radiologist interpretation. A total of 1700 independent cases were reserved to compare the MRUSuNet with single-modality MRI-only and TRUS-only models. Sensitivity and lesion-level Dice similarity scores were computed using targeted biopsy pathology as the reference standard in the biopsy cohorts and whole-mount prostatectomy pathology in the radical prostatectomy cohort. Result The MRUSuNet achieved significantly superior sensitivity (0.80) and lesion Dice score (0.42) across all test cohorts compared to the MRI-only model (sensitivity: 0.73, P = 0.033; Dice score: 0.30, P < 0.001) and the TRUS-only model (sensitivity: 0.49, P < 0.001; Dice score: 0.27, P < 0.001). Compared to radiologists in the prostatectomy cohort, the MRUSuNet showed significantly higher specificity (0.88 vs 0.78; P = 0.004) and lesion Dice score (0.32 vs 0.27; P = 0.048), with no observed statistical difference in sensitivity (0.79; P = 1.000). Conclusion Our findings demonstrate the potential of combining MRI and TRUS in a multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) model to improve localisation of clinically significant prostate cancer on TRUS images relative to single-modality models. These findings support further study of such multimodal AI models as an adjunct to MRI-TRUS fusion workflows.

title: Comparative accuracy of imaging modalities for differentiating malignant small testicular masses.
abstract: Objectives To synthesise evidence comparing the diagnostic performance of imaging modalities in differentiating malignant from benign small testicular masses. Patients and methods A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-compliant search of PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane and Web of Science databases up to 6 May 2026 identified 11 studies comprising 707 patients with small testicular masses (predominantly <2 cm) who underwent imaging prior to a histopathological or, where unavailable, a mixed clinical/radiological follow-up reference standard. Diagnostic accuracy measures for six modalities (brightness-mode [B-Mode] ultrasonography [US], colour doppler US [CDUS], contrast-enhanced US [CEUS], magnetic resonance imaging [MRI], strain elastography [SE] and strain ratio [SR]) were synthesised using a Bayesian bivariate hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic model. Results The CEUS demonstrated the most reliable discriminatory ability with a pooled sensitivity of 91% and pooled specificity of 81%, yielding the highest diagnostic odds ratio of 46. B-Mode US remains a valid screening test with the highest sensitivity of 96% but a specificity of only 39%. CDUS showed a pooled sensitivity of 69% and a specificity of 81%. MRI had a pooled sensitivity of 91% and a specificity of 38%. SE demonstrated a pooled sensitivity of 87% and a specificity of 56%. Finally, SR reported the lowest sensitivity at 74% and a specificity of 50%. CEUS demonstrated significantly higher specificity than B-Mode US (ratio 1.9, 95% posterior interval [PI] 1.2-4.4) and MRI (ratio 1.8, 95% PI 1.0-5.2). Conclusion The CEUS demonstrates the highest combined sensitivity and specificity for differentiating benign from malignant testicular masses, significantly outperforming conventional B-Mode US and MRI in specificity. CEUS represents a compelling decision-making tool to support testis-sparing strategies and reduce unnecessary orchidectomies for indeterminate small testicular masses.

title: Segment-based comparison of multiparametric MRI, Gallium-68-PSMA-PET/CT and combined imaging with histopathology in prostate cancer.
abstract: Objectives To compare the segment-based diagnostic performance of multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI), Gallium-68-prostate-specific membrane antigen-positron emission tomography/computed tomography ( 68 Ga-PSMA-PET/CT), for detecting histopathologically confirmed prostate cancer (PCa). Patients and methods This analysis included 97 men from the prospective, interventional, phase II DEPROMP (DEtection rate of clinically significant PROstate cancer by mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT fusion biopsy) trial who underwent radical prostatectomy with whole-mount histopathological evaluation. All participants received mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT prior to biopsy. The mpMRI was interpreted according to Prostate Imaging-Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) version(v)2.1, and PSMA-PET/CT according to Prostate Cancer Molecular Imaging Standardised Evaluation (PROMISE) molecular imaging Tumour-Node-Metastasis (miTNM) criteria. The prostate was divided into 36 anatomical segments based on the PI-RADS v2.1 sector map. Each segment was correlated with histopathological findings from prostatectomy specimens. For each imaging modality, detection rates, sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were calculated at the segment level. Results A total of 3492 prostate segments were analysed. Detection rates were 74.1% (95% confidence interval [CI] 72.6-75.5) for mpMRI, 72.2% (95% CI 70.6-73.6) for PSMA-PET/CT, and 79.1% (95% CI 77.7-80.4) for the combined use of mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT. Sensitivity and specificity were 13.4% and 97.3% for mpMRI, 18.5% and 92.7% for PSMA-PET/CT, and 25.8% and 90.5% for combined mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT, respectively. Threshold-based receiver operating characteristic analyses yielded an AUC of 0.62 (95% CI 0.54-0.69) for PI-RADS, 0.68 (95% CI 0.63-0.74) for maximum standardised uptake value, and 0.69 (95% CI 0.65-0.74) for molecular imaging PSMA. Conclusion At the segment level, mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT showed comparable diagnostic accuracy with high specificity but limited sensitivity. Their combination improved sensitivity and overall detection performance, underscoring the complementary value of structural and molecular imaging for lesion localisation and precision management in PCa.

title: Transient apnoea for motion control during flexible ureteroscopic lithotripsy: a randomised trial.
abstract: Objectives To determine whether transient apnoea (TA) during flexible ureteroscopic laser lithotripsy improves active lithotripsy efficiency compared with regular mechanical ventilation (RMV) and small tidal-volume ventilation (STVV). Patients and methods In this single-centre, three-arm randomised trial, 150 adults with a single computed tomography (CT)-confirmed renal, ureteropelvic, or proximal ureteric stone measuring 10-<20 mm were assigned one-to-one-to-one to RMV, STVV, or TA. TA followed 5-min 100% oxygen pre-oxygenation, with 9-min maximum and pre-specified stopping criteria under continuous anaesthetic monitoring. The primary endpoint was active lithotripsy efficiency, defined as CT-estimated stone volume divided by elapsed active lithotripsy time. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle. Results The mean (standard deviation) active lithotripsy efficiency was 27.8 (8.9), 26.6 (8.0), and 34.3 (10.0) mm 3 /min with RMV, STVV, and TA, respectively (P < 0.001). TA increased adjusted efficiency by 5.9 mm 3 /min vs RMV (95% confidence interval [CI] 2.2-9.6 mm 3 /min) and 6.8 mm 3 /min vs STVV (95% CI 3.3-10.2 mm 3 /min). The median active lithotripsy time was 27.5, 26.5, and 22.0 min (P = 0.001); total operative time was 50.0, 50.0, and 43.0 min (P = 0.002); and surgeon-rated targeting stability scores were 7.0, 7.0, and 9.0 (P < 0.001), respectively. Postoperative Day 1/1-month stone-free rates were 88%/92%, 80%/96%, and 88%/90%, respectively, with no significant between-group differences. The median (interquartile range) achieved apnoea duration was 5.0 (4.5-6.8) min; 46/50 resumed ventilation before the 9-min maximum, most commonly for heart-rate decline/bradycardia (n = 27) or blood-pressure decline/hypotension (n = 20). No patient had a peripheral oxygen saturation <90% or a Clavien-Dindo Grade ≥III complication; transient hypercapnia and respiratory acidosis improved after ventilation resumed. Conclusion Transient apnoea improved lithotripsy efficiency and shortened operative time compared with RMV and STVV, with higher surgeon-rated targeting stability. The benefit was primarily intraoperative, without evidence of greater postoperative stone clearance. Protocolised TA may provide a brief intraoperative motion-control option with pre-oxygenation, continuous anaesthetic monitoring, and individualised termination.

title: Amygdala vulnerability in Pick disease with discrete frontotemporal dementia syndromes.
abstract: Frontotemporal lobar degeneration with tauopathy (FTLD-tau) typically manifests as either behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) or primary progressive aphasia (PPA). Tau pathology in FTLD-tau is characterized by predominantly three-repeat (3R) tau, as in Pick disease (PiD), or four-repeat (4R) tau species of corticobasal degeneration (CBD) and progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP). FTLD-tau preferentially targets frontal and anterior temporal lobes, including the amygdala, contributing to severe neuropsychiatric symptoms. This study investigated whether bvFTD and PPA due to FTLD-tau exhibit distinct amygdalar histopathology and whether these patterns reflect their initially distinct clinical phenotypes, particularly in PiD. We examined 47 autopsy-confirmed FTLD-tau cases from the Northwestern Alzheimer's Disease Research Center Brain Bank using postmortem digital pathology analysis to quantify tau phosphorylation and HLA-DR immunoreactivity in the amygdala. In a subset of 19 PiD cases (10 bvFTD-PiD, 9 PPA-PiD), we assessed neuropsychiatric symptoms, tracked longitudinally using the Neuropsychiatric Inventory-Questionnaire (NPI-Q), and quantified neuronal and Pick body densities via unbiased stereology and neuronal sizes via digital pathology analysis. Across the FTLD-tau cohort, bvFTD exhibited greater amygdalar neuroinflammation than PPA, despite comparable tau burden. Interestingly, 3R cases also demonstrated higher levels of phosphorylated tau and MHC-II-positive microglia than 4R cases. In PiD, neuropsychiatric symptoms converged over time, with PPA cases evolving to show bvFTD-like symptoms with disease progression. BvFTD-PiD showed a trend toward greater MHC-II-positive microglia than PPA-PiD, despite similar neuronal size/density and Pick body burden. Increased HLA-DR immunoreactivity correlated positively with Pick body pathology. Neurons containing tau pathology (Pick cells) were notably larger than unaffected neurons, suggesting that early tau accumulation precedes overt neuronal degeneration. These findings underscore the potential role of neuroinflammation in shaping clinical phenotypes in FTLD and highlight the role of the amygdala in complex clinicopathologic relationships. Targeting neuroinflammatory processes may represent a viable therapeutic avenue for managing neuropsychiatric symptoms in tauopathies.

title: Converging Growth Trajectories During Recombinant Human Growth Hormone Therapy in Children With Isolated and Combined Pituitary Hormone Deficiency.
abstract: Objective Growth hormone deficiency (GHD) is an important cause of growth failure in children. Although recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) promotes catch-up growth, longitudinal differences in treatment response between isolated growth hormone deficiency (IGHD) and combined pituitary hormone deficiency (CPHD) remain unclear. This study compared longitudinal growth trajectories during rhGH therapy between IGHD and CPHD patients. Design and patients A retrospective cohort study included 72 IGHD and 48 CPHD patients. Measurements Height standard deviation score (SDS) was assessed at baseline and after 12, 24, 36 and 48 months of rhGH therapy. Longitudinal trajectories were analysed using linear mixed-effects models adjusted for age at treatment initiation, bone age, BMI SDS and pituitary MRI findings. Results CPHD patients had more severe growth impairment at baseline than those with IGHD (height SDS: -5.00 ± 1.57 vs. -3.20 ± 1.12; p < 0.001). However, CPHD demonstrated greater catch-up growth, achieving larger cumulative height SDS gains after 48 months (3.10 ± 1.36 vs. 1.92 ± 0.87 SDS; p < 0.001). Mixed-effects modelling confirmed significantly different longitudinal growth trajectories (time-by-diagnosis interaction: χ 2 = 66.62, p < 0.001). Adjusted height SDS improved from -3.40 to -1.49 in IGHD and from -4.56 to -1.55 in CPHD. At 48 months, the adjusted CPHD-IGHD difference was -0.06 SDS (95% CI, -0.63 to 0.51), consistent with substantial convergence of the two growth trajectories. Older age at treatment initiation and abnormal pituitary MRI findings were independently associated with lower height SDS across follow-up. Conclusions Despite more severe baseline growth impairment, children with CPHD experienced greater catch-up growth during rhGH therapy, resulting in substantial convergence of longitudinal height SDS trajectories toward those of children with IGHD over 4 years.

title: A Familial Case of Thauvin-Robinet-Faivre Syndrome (TROFAS), Presenting With Postaxial Polydactyly and Upper Lip Vascular Malformation.
abstract: Thauvin-Robinet-Faivre syndrome (TROFAS, OMIM #617107) is a recently identified autosomal recessive disorder characterised by syndromic overgrowth, facial dysmorphism, mild intellectual disability, variable congenital anomalies, and occasional tumour occurrence. TROFAS results from homozygous or compound heterozygous variants in the FIBP gene, encoding the intracellular binding protein for acidic fibroblast growth factor. This protein plays a role in the fibroblast growth factor (FGF) signalling pathway, which is involved in cell proliferation and contributes to the development of several structures, such as the nervous system, optic vesicles, and blood vessels. Prior to the present report, TROFAS has been described in 10 patients from seven families, four of which are of Turkish origin. We report two additional Turkish siblings from a previously unreported family harbouring the recurrent homozygous c.412-3_415dupCAGTTTG likely pathogenic variant in FIBP. Both presented with typical TROFAS features; however, the male sibling exhibited a more severe neurodevelopmental profile and additional malformations, including postaxial polydactyly and upper lip vascular malformation, which, to our knowledge, have not previously been reported in association with TROFAS. A detailed clinical characterisation of these two new cases contributes to a more comprehensive delineation of the syndrome, adding potentially novel phenotypic features requiring confirmation in additional patients.

title: Flap Versus Tunneling for Horizontal Ridge Augmentation With FDBA and i-PRF: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial.
abstract: Aim This study evaluated the efficacy of conventional flap and tunneling techniques for horizontal alveolar ridge augmentation using freeze-dried bone allograft (FDBA) particles combined with injectable platelet-rich fibrin (i-PRF). Materials and methods Forty-five patients were randomly allocated to one of three groups (n = 15 each): conventional flap (CF), tunneling with membrane (TM), or tunneling without membrane (TnM). Preoperative ridge width was measured via cone beam computed tomography (CBCT). All augmentation procedures incorporated FDBA and i-PRF; an absorbable collagen membrane was applied in the CF and TM groups. Follow-up assessments, including CBCT imaging and histomorphometric analysis, were conducted 6 months postoperatively. For normally distributed data, ANOVA with Tukey's post hoc test and paired samples t-test were applied. Non-normally distributed data were analyzed using Kruskal-Wallis, Mann-Whitney U, and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Results Statistical analysis was performed on 43 patients. All groups demonstrated an increase in ridge width after 6 months. At the 2 mm level, the mean width gain was 1.28 mm (95% CI: 0.17 to 2.40) in the TM group, 2.85 mm (95% CI: 1.80 to 3.89) in the TnM group, and 1.95 mm (95% CI: 1.07 to 2.83) in the CF group. However, statistical analysis revealed no significant intergroup variation (p > 0.05). Histomorphometric assessments similarly demonstrated comparable outcomes across all groups, with no statistically significant differences observed (p > 0.05). Conclusion Within the limitations of this study, the tunneling technique, regardless of membrane use, appears to be a clinically viable alternative to the conventional flap method for horizontal alveolar ridge augmentation. However, further studies with longer follow-up periods are required to substantiate these findings. Trial registration irct.behdasht.gov.ir identifier: IRCT 20101204005305N21.

title: Three-Year Follow-Up of Clinical, Radiographic, and Patient-Reported Outcomes for Zirconia and Titanium Implants in the Posterior Region: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Objective To compare the 3-year clinical, radiographic, esthetic, and patient-reported outcomes of zirconia (Zr) and titanium (Ti) implants placed in posterior sites in a randomized, controlled within-subject design. Materials and methods Forty-two patients each received one Zr and one Ti implant. Clinical and radiographic outcomes were evaluated at baseline, 1, and 3 years after crown delivery. Marginal bone levels (MBL), peri-implant soft-tissue parameters, technical complications, esthetic outcomes (ΔE values, VAS scores), and patient-reported measures were assessed. Thirty-nine patients (37 Zr; 39 Ti implants) were available at 3 years. Results The 3-year survival rate was 100% for Ti and 94.9% for Zr implants. MBL remained stable after the initial remodeling phase, with no clinically relevant differences between materials. Peri-implant soft-tissue conditions (BOP, plaque presence, PD, KT) were similar for Zr and Ti. Two zirconia implants were lost during the observation period. Peri-implantitis was diagnosed in 7.9% of the implants, affecting three titanium and three zirconia implants. Technical complications differed between groups: chipping occurred significantly more often at Zr implant-supported crowns. Ti implants showed two screw-loosening events, while Zr implants showed two cases of decementation. Esthetic and patient-reported outcomes were comparable, with low perceived mucosal color differences and a slight preference for Zr sites, if detectable. Conclusion Zr and Ti implants showed similar peri-implant health, marginal bone stability, esthetic outcomes, and patient satisfaction after 3 years. Zr implants, however, demonstrated a slightly lower survival rate and more chipping. Trial registration The trial is registered in the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS) under the ID DRKS00008591.

title: Combined Host-Derived and Microbiological Biomarkers for the Detection of Peri-Implant Bone Loss: A Diagnostic Accuracy Study.
abstract: Aim To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of host-derived and microbiological biomarkers, alone and in combination with clinical parameters, for the detection of peri-implant bone loss (BL). Methods A university-based cohort of subjects with dental implants was examined at baseline and after a mean follow-up of 3.9 years. Peri-implant BL served as the reference standard, defined as > 1 mm between baseline and follow-up radiographs; implants with < 0.5 mm BL served as controls. At follow-up, peri-implant crevicular fluid and submarginal-microbiological samples were collected. Bone metabolism and inflammatory biomarkers were quantified using Luminex technology. Bacterial loads were quantified by qPCR. Associations of biomarkers with BL were evaluated using multilevel logistic regression models. Diagnostic accuracy was assessed using ROC curves, with AUC, sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values reported. Results Seventy-one subjects with 273 implants were included. Twenty-eight exhibited peri-implant-BL > 1.0 mm over the follow-up period. Increased levels of IL-1β, T. denticola, Fusobacterium spp., and T. forsythia were associated with BL in unadjusted analyses. However, these associations were no longer statistically significant after adjustment for clinical parameters. Individual biomarkers demonstrated limited diagnostic accuracy (maximum AUC = 0.68). In contrast, biomarker combinations with clinical parameters exhibited excellent discriminative performance (AUC > 0.95). The combination of IL-1β and BoP-or-PPD achieved the highest accuracy (AUC = 0.97). Conclusions While individual biomarkers showed limited diagnostic utility, combining multiple predictors significantly improved the ability to detect peri-implant BL. Combining IL-1β with either BoP or PPD significantly outperformed individual clinical measures but did not outperform the combination of clinical parameters, highlighting the potential of integrated biomarker and clinical parameter approaches as screening tools for detecting BL.

title: Is Routine Umbo Resection Necessary During Over-Underlay Tympanoplasty? A Histopathological and Clinical Study.
abstract: The necessity of routine umbo resection during over-underlay tympanoplasty remains controversial. To evaluate histopathological persistence of epithelial remnants according to perforation-umbo relationship and to estimate the risk of postoperative cholesteatoma. Prospective cohort of 148 consecutive Type I over-underlay tympanoplasties with minimum 24-month follow-up. Patients were grouped by perforation relation to the umbo. All resected specimens were examined with haematoxylin-eosin (H&E); pan-cytokeratin immunohistochemistry was not performed in this series. Categorical comparisons used Fisher's exact test; proportions are reported with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Post hoc upper 95% bound for cholesteatoma incidence was calculated using the Poisson approximation. Histopathology revealed epithelial remnants in 33.3% (12/36; 95% CI 18.6-51.0) of Group 1 and 21.9% (7/32; 95% CI 9.3-40.0) of Group 2; none were detected in Group 3. No cholesteatoma developed during mean follow-up of 24 months; the upper 95% confidence bound for true cholesteatoma incidence was 2.02%. Umbo-involving perforations are associated with higher rates of microscopic epithelial remnants, but microscopic remnants did not translate into cholesteatoma within the observed follow-up. Routine umbo resection is not mandatory when meticulous de-epithelialisation is achievable; selective resection based on intraoperative assessment is recommended. Longer follow-up and larger multicentre cohorts are required to exclude rare adverse events.

title: Predictive Value of Preoperative Examinations for Early Prognosis After Functional Endoscopic Sinus Surgery in Chronic Rhinosinusitis With Nasal Polyps.
abstract: Background Functional endoscopic sinus surgery (FESS) remains a primary treatment modality for chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) refractory to medical management. This study aimed to evaluate the predictive value of routine preoperative examinations for early surgical outcomes following FESS in patients with CRSwNP. Methods This prospective cohort study evaluated whether routine preoperative assessments predict early outcomes after FESS in 181 patients with bilateral CRSwNP. Preoperative evaluations included Lund-Mackay CT scores, Lund-Kennedy endoscopy scores, symptom Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), SNOT-22 and peripheral blood eosinophil counts. Patients were followed postoperatively at 2 weeks, 1, 3 and 6 months. Results Preoperative VAS showed the strongest correlation with 2-week symptom improvement (r = 0.633), remaining an independent predictor in multivariate analysis (β = 0.58). Preoperative SNOT-22 also independently predicted 2-week outcomes (β = 0.15). At 3 months, blood eosinophil counts predicted endoscopic improvement (r = 0.305), while preoperative Lund-Kennedy scores strongly predicted 6-month endoscopic outcomes (r = 0.508). Conclusions Routine preoperative assessments provide valuable predictive information for early postoperative outcomes following FESS in CRSwNP. We expect these findings to support the integration of multimodal preoperative assessment to guide patient counselling and postoperative management expectations.

title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of preoperative MRI-based pelvimetry in predicting surgical difficulty in rectal cancer: Implications for personalised surgical planning.
abstract: Background Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based pelvimetry has been investigated for predicting surgical difficulty in total mesorectal excision (TME) for rectal cancer. However, heterogeneity in pelvimetric parameters, surrogate outcomes, and study design has resulted in inconsistent evidence. This systematic review aimed to synthesise the evidence on commonly used MRI parameters and difficulty surrogates and assess their methodological robustness and clinical relevance. Methods PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched through December 2025 for studies evaluating preoperative MRI pelvimetry in patients undergoing TME for rectal cancer. Outcome parameters were surrogate measures of surgical difficulty, including operating time, intraoperative blood loss, conversion to open surgery, pathological quality metrics, and postoperative complications. Risk of bias was assessed using the Risk of Bias in Non-randomised Studies of Exposures (ROBINS-E) tool. This systematic review and meta-analysis was reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 statement and prospectively registered (PROSPERO: CRD420261287153). Results Thirty-six studies comprising 8,364 patients were included. Common parameters included sagittal measurements and axial interspinous distance (ISD) and intertuberous distance (ITD). Definitions of surgical difficulty varied substantially. ROBINS-E identified some concerns in 30 studies, a high risk of bias in five, and insufficient information in one.
