title: Accessory Cavitating Uterine Masses/Malformation: An Important Differential in Women With Intractable Dysmenorrhea and Chronic Pelvic Pain Across All Ages.
abstract: Aim Accessory cavitated uterine malformation or mass (ACUM) is a rare and under-recognized cause of dysmenorrhea and chronic pelvic pain (CPP). Various diagnostic criteria have been proposed; patients may present with atypical features. This study aimed to describe the clinical presentation, diagnostic challenges, and management outcomes of ACUM. Methods Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data was done at a tertiary care institution over 6 years. All women diagnosed with ACUM were included. Clinical presentation, imaging, preoperative diagnosis, intraoperative picture, and management outcomes were analyzed. Result Eighteen women were enrolled. The median age at presentation was 26.5 years (18-46), with 17 in the reproductive age group and one postmenopausal. The median duration of symptoms was 4 years (2 months to 11 years). Dysmenorrhea with prominent pain on one side, localized to the side of the lesion, was the predominant symptom, occurring in 17/18 (94.4%). Of these, 10/18 (55.6%) experienced both CPP and dysmenorrhea, 7/18 (38.9%) had only dysmenorrhea. Only CPP was reported in 1/18 (5.6%), woman with postmenopausal ACUM. On initial 2D-USG, one case was correctly diagnosed, while 5/18(27.8%) were misdiagnosed as rudimentary horn, 7/18(38.9%) as degenerated fibroid, 4/18(22.2%) as endometrioma, and 1/18(5.6%) as dermoid cyst. Diagnosis was confirmed on further imaging with 3D-USG or MRI in 11/18 (61.1%) cases. Seventeen women underwent surgical management, with 16/17 had excision, and one postmenopausal woman was treated by laparoscopic aspiration. Conclusion ACUM is an important differential of intractable dysmenorrhea or CPP, especially if pain is localized to either side, even in postmenopausal females.

title: Multi-Level Automated Classification of Temporomandibular Joint Degenerative Joint Disease on CBCT Using 3D Volumetric and 2D Slice-Based Approaches.
abstract: Background Temporomandibular joint degenerative joint disease (TMJ DJD) causes progressive osseous changes of the mandibular condyle and articular fossa. Although cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) enables detailed assessment, manual interpretation is time-consuming and subject to inter-observer variability. Objectives To develop and validate a multilevel AI framework for CBCT-based TMJ DJD assessment using three-dimensional classification, quantitative volumetric analysis, and two-dimensional slice-based detection. Methods Full-field-of-view CBCT scans from 222 patients were used for three-dimensional analysis. A 3D V-Net classified condyles into Normal, Osteophyte, Erosion, Flattening, and Severe Degeneration categories. Condylar volume was quantitatively compared between TMJ DJD and non-TMJ DJD groups and among degenerative subgroups. For slice-based analysis, 727 temporomandibular joints from 416 patients were retrospectively evaluated. Automated sagittal slice extraction based on the condylion landmark generated 5787 condylar and 666 articular fossa slices. YOLOv10 was used for multi-lesion detection of six condylar and three fossa categories. Results The 3D V-Net achieved an overall sensitivity of 79.47%. Condylar volume differed significantly between TMJ DJD and non-TMJ DJD groups (ANOVA, p = 0.025), whereas differences among the TMJ DJD subgroups were not statistically significant. For condylar slice-based detection, YOLOv10 achieved 94.0% sensitivity, 82.8% precision, 88.0% F1-score, and 91.3% AP@0.50. For articular fossa detection, YOLOv10 achieved 92.41% sensitivity, 83.91% precision, 87.95% F1-score, and 82.01% AP@0.50. Conclusions Three-dimensional AI enabled overall TMJ DJD classification but showed limited discrimination of specific subgroups, particularly erosion. Volumetric analysis differentiated DJD from non-DJD cases but not among DJD subgroups. In contrast, slice-based YOLOv10 effectively detected and labelled specific condylar and fossa degenerative changes, providing more detailed lesion-level characterization.

title: Internal Validation of a YOLOv8 Model for Classifying Temporomandibular Joint Disc Displacement With Versus Without Reduction on Open-Mouth Proton-Density-Weighted MRI.
abstract: Background The temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disc plays an important role in maintaining normal joint function. However, disc displacement is a common condition that can lead to pain, restricted jaw movement and chronic TMJ dysfunction. Objective To develop and evaluate a deep learning model capable of autonomously localizing the TMJ region from magnetic resonance (MR) images during mouth opening using the You Only Look Once (YOLO) v8 framework, and to discriminate between TMJ disc displacement with reduction (DDwR) and disc displacement without reduction (DDwoR). Methods This study included 237 patients (48 males, 189 females; age range, 19-83 [mean, 44.73 ± 18.3] years) who underwent MRI examination at our hospital for suspected TMJ disorders and were diagnosed with disc displacement based on imaging findings. After exclusion, 439 proton density-weighted MR images during mouth opening were preprocessed and divided on a patient basis into training (280 images), validation (71 images) and test (88 images) datasets. The TMJ region was manually annotated using LabelImg, including the condyles, articular disc and articular tubercle. The YOLOv8 deep learning model was trained for 200 epochs to localize the TMJ region and classify DDwR or DDwoR. Results The YOLOv8 model achieved promising results for the detection and classification of TMJ disc displacements. The performance metrics were a precision, recall and F1 score of 0.983, 0.988 and 0.987, respectively, indicating a high accuracy in detecting and identifying disc displacement patterns. Conclusion The YOLOv8 deep learning model demonstrated promising performance in automatically localizing and classifying TMJ disc displacement from MR images.

title: Familial Florid Cemento-Osseous Dysplasia: A Systematic Review Based on Contemporary Diagnostic Criteria.
abstract: Purpose Familial florid cemento-osseous dysplasia (FFCOD) is a rare fibro-osseous jaw disorder characterized by multifocal lesions and familial aggregation. This systematic review aimed to synthesize the evidence on the demographic, clinical, radiographic, histopathological, genetic, therapeutic, and follow-up characteristics of FFCOD. Methods A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261295922). Searches were performed in PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, SciELO, LIVIVO, ProQuest, OpenGrey, IBICT/BDTD, Google Scholar, and reference lists through April 2025. Studies following the current World Health Organization (WHO) diagnostic criteria were eligible. Two independent reviewers performed study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment using the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tool for case reports. Results Eight studies comprising 25 affected individuals were included. Females accounted for 60.0% of cases, and the mean age was 34.8 ± 19.9 years. Multifocal involvement of both jaws (48.0%) and all four quadrants (32.0%) was common. All included cases exhibited a mixed radiolucent-radiopaque appearance (100.0%), while bone expansion was the most frequent clinical manifestation (33.3%). Histopathological examination consistently demonstrated fibrocellular stroma associated with cemento- and/or bone-like mineralized material. Molecular analysis was reported in one study and identified an ANO5 missense variant. Osteomyelitis, osteonecrosis, and bone exposure/sequestration were the most frequently reported complications. Conclusion FFCOD demonstrates consistent clinicopathological characteristics, including multifocal jaw involvement, bone expansion, and a mixed radiolucent-radiopaque appearance. Although many individuals remain asymptomatic, infectious and necrotic complications may occur, emphasizing the importance of early recognition, careful treatment planning, and long-term clinical and radiographic follow-up.

title: Subcutaneous Fat Density Is an Independent Predictor of Adverse Outcomes and Shows Early Improvement After Liver Transplantation.
abstract: Background and aims Body composition is increasingly recognised as a prognostic determinant in cirrhosis, particularly in liver transplant (LT) candidates. We aimed to assess adipose and muscle compartments on computed tomography (CT) before and after LT and to evaluate their associations with mortality. Methods We recruited prospectively 121 patients with cirrhosis listed for LT. CT scans at the third lumbar vertebral level were analysed to quantify cross-sectional area (cm 2 ) and density (Hounsfield units, HU) of skeletal muscle, subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT), and visceral adipose tissue. A subset underwent a CT-scan 6 months post-LT. Results Most patients were male (76%), and the median MELD score was 14 (IQR 10-20). High SAT density (> -83 HU in women; > -74 HU in men) was associated with higher pre-transplant mortality (p = 0.005) and with reduced overall survival during follow-up (p = 0.005) compared to lower SAT density. The combined phenotype of low muscle density and high SAT density identified the subgroup with the poorest survival (p = 0.002). From baseline to 6 months post-LT, SAT density decreased significantly (p = 0.0134), whereas muscle parameters did not change significantly. Conclusions This prospective observational cohort study demonstrates that SAT density is a prognostic CT-derived marker in patients with cirrhosis awaiting LT with significant post-transplant dynamics. The impact of altered adipose tissue therefore warrants attention in this situation.

title: Distinct Plasma Proteomic Signatures Distinguish MASLD From Non-Steatotic Individuals but Not From MetALD.
abstract: Background and aims Metabolic dysfunction associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most prevalent liver disease, yet accurate early detection remains challenging. A particular diagnostic obstacle is distinguishing MASLD from metabolic dysfunction and alcohol-related liver disease (MetALD), currently defined using clinically informed moderate alcohol consumption thresholds without biological validation. This study aimed to identify and externally validate plasma proteomic signatures associated with MASLD and assess whether proteomic profiles support a molecular distinction between MASLD and MetALD as currently defined. Methods We analysed plasma proteomic profiles using OLINK data from UK Biobank (UKB) participants with liver MRI. MASLD was defined as MRI-PDFF ≥ 5% and metabolic dysfunction (n = 165), MetALD (n = 46) as MASLD with additional moderate alcohol intake and controls as PDFF < 5% (n = 741). Results Compared to controls, participants with MASLD showed 17 upregulated and 3 downregulated proteins after Bonferroni correction (adjusted p < 0.05). Among upregulated proteins, leptin (LEP), fatty acid-binding protein, liver (FABP1) and aminoacylase1 (ACY1) and among downregulated, insulin-like growth factor-binding protein 1 (IGFBP1) were externally validated in an independent cohort (clinicaltrials.gov NCT02520609, n = 47). Individuals with MetALD showed no significant proteomic distinction from MASLD. Although the small MetALD sample size may have limited detection of differences, direct differential expression analysis did not identify statistically significant differences between MASLD and MetALD under the current clinical thresholds. Conclusions MASLD was associated with a reproducible plasma proteomic signature enriched for proteins involved in lipid metabolism, inflammation and hormonal regulation. We did not identify a clear proteomic distinction between MASLD and MetALD under the current alcohol thresholds. However, this finding should be interpreted considering limited power and potential alcohol-exposure misclassification.

title: Diagnostic Value and Influencing Factors of Ultrasound-Derived Fat Fraction for Quantifying MASLD in Children.
abstract: Background & aims To evaluate the diagnostic performance of ultrasound-derived fat fraction (UDFF) for quantifying Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) in children, using Magnetic resonance imaging-derived proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) as the reference standard. Methods This prospective study enrolled 70 children with a median age of 12.23 years [IQR, 10.47-14.29] from December 2025 to April 2026. All participants underwent UDFF, MRI-PDFF, and point shear wave elastography (pSWE) examinations. Steatosis was defined as MRI-PDFF ≥ 6.4%. Correlations, agreement, diagnostic accuracy, and bias predictors were assessed using Pearson/Spearman correlation, Bland-Altman, ROC curves, and multivariable regression. Results Of 70 participants, 42 had MASLD. UDFF correlated strongly with MRI-PDFF (r = 0.84, p < 0.001). Overall mean bias was -2.19% (95% concordance limits: -15.07% to 10.68%), with a more pronounced systematic numerical bias observed in moderate-to-severe steatosis (mean bias -9.23%). No significant bias predictors were found. For detecting steatosis (≥ 6.4%), UDFF had an AUC of 0.98, optimal cutoff 5.5% (sensitivity 97.6%, specificity 92.9%, accuracy 95.7%); for ≥ S2 steatosis, the cutoff was 12.5% (AUC 0.96). Intraclass correlation for five repeated UDFF measurements was 0.98 (95% CI: 0.98-0.99). Visceral fat thickness (β = 2.004, p = 0.003) and measurement depth (β = 4.716, p = 0.033) independently predicted UDFF values. UDFF showed a weak negative correlation with pSWE Young's modulus (r = -0.258, p = 0.033). Conclusions UDFF is a non-invasive, accurate, and reproducible tool for quantifying paediatric hepatic steatosis. Although a systematic numerical bias exists relative to MRI-PDFF in moderate-to-severe cases, UDFF retains excellent discriminative ability and is suitable for screening, staging, and longitudinal follow-up of paediatric MASLD.

title: Ultrasound-Based Skeletal Muscle Assessment for Prognostication in Cirrhosis: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Background and aims Sarcopenia is a major determinant of adverse outcomes in cirrhosis, yet CT- and MRI-based assessments are difficult to implement in routine and longitudinal practice. Ultrasound is a feasible bedside alternative, but its prognostic role remains unclear. We performed a systematic review to evaluate the association between ultrasound-derived skeletal muscle measures and mortality in adults with cirrhosis. Methods This review followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251056162). MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library were searched to October 2025. Prospective studies assessing ultrasound-based muscle parameters and mortality in cirrhosis were included. Risk of bias was evaluated using QUIPS. Results Six prospective studies (n = 731) were included. Heterogeneity in muscle sites, ultrasound protocols, indexation methods, sarcopenia definitions and outcomes precluded meta-analysis. Lower ultrasound-derived muscle measures were consistently associated with higher mortality. In acute decompensation, reduced rectus femoris area predicted 90-day mortality (sHR 0.57; 95% CI 0.38-0.85). Rectus abdominis thickness and psoas indices were also associated with mortality. In hospitalized decompensated cirrhosis, ultrasound-defined sarcopenia was strongly associated with 6-month mortality (HR 6.37; 95% CI 3.15-12.87). In critically ill liver transplant candidates, higher serial rectus femoris muscle area measurements were associated with better survival. In advanced chronic liver disease, sarcopenia was linked to increased 1-year mortality. Conclusions In our systematic review, ultrasound-based muscle measures demonstrated a broadly consistent association with mortality; although not yet fully validated, they represent a promising bedside prognostic tool. Standardization is needed before clinical implementation.

title: Screening for Biliary Dysplasia Using Brush Cytology in PSC: Prevalence, Risk Factors and Outcomes.
abstract: Background and aims Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is associated with significantly increased risk of cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) with a 5-year survival below 10%. Although CCA screening remains controversial, current guidelines recommend annual surveillance via ultrasound or MRI/MRCP. Brush cytology (BC) enables early detection of biliary dysplasia (BD), but its sensitivity varies widely (8%-89%). We assessed the accuracy of BC in detecting CCA, the prevalence and risk factors for BD, and the outcomes of dysplasia screening. Methods We analysed 4017 BC samples from 984 PSC patients who underwent ERC. The exclusion criteria (n = 114) were age at diagnosis < 18 or > 65 years, early CCA diagnosis (< 1 year from PSC diagnosis), and IgG4-related cholangitis. Demographics, laboratory data and ERC scores were compared between patients with repeated BD findings (≥ 3 times) or CCA (composite endpoint) and those without. Optimal predictors were assessed using time-weighted AUC and Cox regression. Results BD was detected at least once in 10% of the patients. Repeated suspicion of dysplasia in BC was also strongly associated with BD in explanted livers. The negative predictive value was 0.99, and the overall accuracy was 0.91. Only the ERC score (≥ 7, AUC 0.87) and S-IgG4-twAUC (≥ 1.06, AUC 0.76) predicted the composite endpoint. Combining both improved accuracy (ERC-IgG4-score, AUC 0.88). Conclusions Brush cytology has a high negative predictive value for excluding CCA development. The ERC score and S-IgG4 are key predictors of biliary dysplasia, supporting their use in PSC surveillance. The ERC-IgG4-score may help guide individualized monitoring strategies.

title: Empirically Informed Blood Vessel Network Reconstruction for Multimodality Image-Based Vascular Systems Biology.
abstract: Objective Reconstruction of vascular topology from imperfect 3D imaging data is essential for accurate hemodynamic simulations. Therefore, we developed a "gap-filling" method predicated on vascular biology and empirical patterns to restore incomplete vessels, independent of the imaging modality and spatial resolution employed. Methods Our gap-filling algorithm reconstructs a vascular network based on distributions of its extant morphological features and employs different rules for healthy and tumor tissue. Algorithm performance was evaluated on (i) incomplete synthetic vascular trees with simulated CT noise, (ii) micro-CT-acquired brain tumor vasculature, (iii) micro-MRI-derived vasculature from a healthy mouse brain, and (iv) vasculature from the murine hippocampus imaged with light-sheet microscopy (LSM). Results For synthetic vascular trees, our algorithm restored more gaps when the volume fraction was between 80% and 95%. Peak vessel segment recovery occurred for intermediate volume fractions (86%-89%). Gap-filling performance was impacted when image noise was introduced. Across CT, MRI, and LSM, our method successfully reconnected missing vessel segments while preserving the overall features of the vascular network. Gap-filling of tumor vasculature, with its abnormal topology, was better when tumor-specific reconstruction rules were employed. Conclusions Our method showed efficient restoration of vascular network connectivity for 3D data derived from common imaging modalities at different resolutions. We also demonstrated the significance of applying distinct biologically-informed rules when reconstructing healthy and tumor vascular networks.

title: CT-Based Clinical-Radiomics for Differentiating Talaromyces marneffei Spondylitis From Tuberculous Spondylitis Before Pathogen Confirmation: A Multicentre Diagnostic Study in an Endemic Region.
abstract: Background Talaromyces marneffei spondylitis (TMS) is an uncommon but clinically important form of talaromycosis in endemic regions. Where talaromycosis and tuberculosis overlap, TMS may be worked up as tuberculous spondylitis (TBS), delaying fungal investigations and antifungal treatment. Objectives To assess whether pretreatment CT, routine clinical variables and radiomics features can help differentiate TMS from TBS at the initial assessment stage. Patients/methods This retrospective multicentre study included 263 patients meeting the prespecified composite reference standard (83 TMS and 180 TBS). Centre A formed the training and internal-validation cohorts; Centres B and C formed the external cohort (n = 50; 16 TMS and 34 TBS). Six clinical variables and 14 CT radiomics features were used to develop clinical, radiomics and combined models. Results TMS showed a stronger systemic inflammatory phenotype, whereas TBS generally showed more frequent disc-endplate involvement and osseous destruction. The clinical-radiomics model achieved the highest AUCs in the training, internal validation and external validation cohorts: 0.958 (95% CI, 0.924-0.992), 0.940 (95% CI, 0.871-1.000) and 0.927 (95% CI, 0.867-0.987), respectively. The external confidence interval was wide, reflecting the limited external sample size. Conclusions In regions where talaromycosis and tuberculosis overlap, a pretreatment CT-based clinical-radiomics approach may help flag patients in whom TMS should be considered early. This approach could support earlier fungal investigations while definitive microbiological, molecular or histopathological results are pending. It addresses only the TMS-versus-TBS differential and is not a general spinal-infection triage tool; the findings support further evaluation in endemic settings.

title: Differential Diagnosis Performance of ChatGPT in Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology.
abstract: Objective To evaluate ChatGPT (GPT-5.1) for ranked differential diagnoses in oral and maxillofacial pathology, assess image effects on diagnostic performance and examine output stability across repeated runs. Methods This retrospective diagnostic accuracy study included 160 biopsy-confirmed cases. Cases were evaluated using a standardised prompt under two conditions: text-only and text plus clinical photographs and/or radiographs. Each case underwent three independent runs. Performance was measured using Top-1, Top-3, Top-5 and Top-10 accuracy. Results Top-1 accuracy was 44.0% for text-only and 43.3% for text + image inputs. Accuracy increased at broader thresholds, with Top-10 accuracy reaching 80.7% and 82.9%, respectively, but no significant differences were observed between input conditions at any Top-K threshold. Top-1 performance was stable across runs, although variability was observed at broader Top-K thresholds in the text-only condition. Conclusions ChatGPT ranked the reference diagnosis first in fewer than half of cases, while broader differential lists more often included it. Images did not significantly improve accuracy, although heterogeneous and non-standardised visual inputs may have limited detection of multimodal effects. These findings support further investigation for hypothesis generation and educational use rather than clinical decision support or replacement of expert judgement and histopathological confirmation.

title: Diagnostic Performance of Artificial Intelligence in Detecting Periodontal Diseases Using Cone-Beam Computed Tomography: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Aim Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have shown promise for the detection of periodontal disease. This study aimed to synthesize current evidence on the diagnostic performance of AI models applied to cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) for periodontal disease. Methods A comprehensive literature search of MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase was conducted to identify studies on AI-assisted diagnosis of periodontal disease using CBCT published up to December 2025. The Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 (QUADAS-2) tool was used to assess the risk of bias. Results Among 10,099 records screened, eight studies met the inclusion criteria. These studies indicate that AI models, predominantly based on convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures applied to CBCT images, have substantial potential for detecting periodontal bone loss and related conditions. However, diagnostic performance metrics varied markedly across studies, and direct comparisons with human clinicians produced inconsistent findings, underscoring the need for more rigorous study designs and standardized datasets. Conclusions Despite limitations arising from heterogeneous methodologies and non-standardized data collection, CBCT-based AI models show considerable promise for enhancing periodontal disease diagnosis. Further high-quality, methodologically robust research is warranted to validate and optimize these approaches for clinical use. Trial registration PROSPERO: CRD420251273846.

title: Differential Expression of P53, CDKN2A, NOTCH1, and CASP8 in Oral Epithelial Dysplasia: An In Vitro Study to Explore Potential Malignant Transformation.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to better understand the expression of P53, CDKN2A, NOTCH1, and CASP8 proteins in progressive and nonprogressive oral epithelial dysplasia (OED) cell lines to predict malignant transformation. Materials and methods Normal oral keratinocytes (NHOK810), nonprogressive OED (D30-mild, D25-severe), progressive OED (D20-moderate, D19-severe), and oral squamous cell carcinoma (H357, BICR31, and ORL188) were co-cultured with irradiated 3T3 fibroblasts. Western blotting was used to assess the protein expression of p53, CDKN2A, NOTCH1, and CASP8 in these cell lines. Bootstrapping, one-way ANOVA, and subsequent post hoc analyses were performed for multiple comparisons. Results CDKN2A and NOTCH1 had low expression in progressive OED (p = 0.0008 and 0.0012) respectively relative to nonprogressive OED, indicating a negative tendency. Conversely, p53 demonstrated significantly higher expression in progressive OED (p = 0.0112) compared to nonprogressive OED, reflecting a positive trend of expression throughout disease progression. There was a significant difference in CASP8 expression between nonprogressive and progressive cell lines (p = 0.039); however, no linear pattern was observed as the disease advanced. Conclusion The current study illustrates that the high expression of p53, combined with low expression of CDKN2A and NOTCH1, may serve as helpful markers, providing a potential molecular complement to histopathology for predicting malignant transformation in OED.

title: Comparison Between Interlaminar and Transforaminal Endoscopic Lumbar Discectomy for Sciatic Scoliosis Secondary to Lumbar Disc Herniation: A Retrospective Study With a Minimum 1 Year Follow-Up.
abstract: Objective This study aims to compare the clinical and radiographic outcomes of interlaminar and transforaminal endoscopic lumbar discectomy (IELD and TELD) in the treatment of lumbar disc herniation (LDH) with sciatic scoliosis. Methods Patients with sciatic scoliosis secondary to LDH who had undergone IELD or TELD between January 2022 to June 2024 were reviewed. Radiographic parameters, including Cobb angle, apical vertebral translation (AVT), and coronal balance distance (CBD), were measured preoperatively and postoperatively to assess curve evolution. Clinical outcomes were evaluated using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) and the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI). Meanwhile, perioperative data were also collected. Comparisons between the groups were made by independent t-tests and χ 2 tests. Results A total of 134 patients in the IELD group and 103 patients in the TELD group were included in this study. There was no significant difference in intraoperative blood loss (13.4 ± 7.8 mL vs. 11.5 ± 7.1 mL, p = 0.067) and postoperative length of stay (2.5 ± 0.6 days vs. 2.5 ± 0.8 days, p = 0.378) between the two groups; however, the IELD group demonstrated shorter operation time (87.2 ± 17.4 min vs. 96.1 ± 23.3 min, p = 0.001) and fewer intraoperative fluoroscopy times (4.9 ± 0.7 vs. 10.3 ± 2.7, p < 0.001) compared to the TELD group. Both groups showed significant improvements in VAS and ODI scores (p < 0.05), with no significant differences between the groups. Before surgery, 86.9% (206/237) patients had a disc herniation at the convex side of the lumbosacral curve and 86.5% (205/237) patients showed a trunk shift toward the opposite side of disc herniation. After surgery, 91.8% (123/134) of the IELD group and 90.3% (93/103) of the TELD group achieved resolution of scoliosis (AVT ≤ 10 mm) within 12 months. At the final follow-up, the AVT, Cobb angle, CBD, and SVA in the IELD group were 2.7 ± 2.0 mm, 1.0° ± 0.8°, 1.2 ± 0.9 mm, and 3.4 ± 3.1 mm, respectively, with no significant differences compared to the 2.8 ± 2.7 mm, 1.1° ± 0.8°, 1.2 ± 0.8 mm, and 3.7 ± 3.5 mm in the TELD group. Conclusions Both IELD and TELD are effective and safe for LDH with sciatic scoliosis, with comparable radiographic and clinical outcomes in terms of scoliosis correction. IELD is associated with shorter operation time and fewer intraoperative fluoroscopy times in this cohort.

title: Multidimensional Management of Degenerative Scoliosis: A Comprehensive Narrative Review Integrating Diagnostic Assessment, Surgical Decision-Making, and Patient-Centered Outcomes.
abstract: Degenerative scoliosis (DS) is a common spinal deformity in aging populations and an important contributor to low back pain, neurological symptoms, and functional decline. Unlike adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, DS develops in a previously non-scoliotic spine through progressive asymmetric degeneration of the intervertebral disks, facet joints, and supporting spinal structures. Despite its growing clinical burden, management remains heterogeneous, with decision-making often fragmented across radiographic assessment, treatment planning, and postoperative outcome evaluation. Building on previous reviews of DS, this article provides a structured clinical update that organizes contemporary evidence across diagnostic assessment, individualized treatment selection, perioperative risk optimization, and patient-centered outcomes. A narrative literature review was conducted to evaluate current concepts in DS diagnosis, risk stratification, treatment strategies, and patient-centered outcomes. Relevant literature from major biomedical databases was identified and qualitatively synthesized according to clinical relevance. Current evidence supports a comprehensive assessment of DS that integrates deformity morphology, spinopelvic alignment, segmental degeneration, neurological status, bone quality, and patient-specific risk factors. Beyond coronal Cobb angle measurement, advanced imaging and alignment parameters may provide complementary information for phenotyping and treatment planning. The literature increasingly supports individualized treatment selection based on deformity severity, sagittal imbalance, physiological reserve, neurological status, and functional goals, with options ranging from nonoperative care to minimally invasive or more extensive reconstructive procedures. Surgical planning may also incorporate alignment objectives, biomechanical considerations, complication risk, frailty, and patient-reported outcomes. DS management is evolving from deformity correction-centered strategies toward a multidimensional, patient-centered paradigm. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence across diagnostic evaluation, individualized treatment selection, surgical planning, and outcome assessment while recognizing that many management strategies remain supported by heterogeneous evidence and require patient-specific consideration. Future research is needed to refine predictive models, personalized alignment strategies, and emerging technology-assisted approaches.

title: Can Deltoid Hounsfield Unit/Supraspinatus Hounsfield Unit Predict Postoperative Rotator Cuff Retear?
abstract: Objectives Retear is a common complication after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair (ARCR), yet available predictors are limited and combined models perform better than single factors. This study investigated whether the preoperative deltoid-to-supraspinatus Hounsfield unit (HU) ratio predicts retear and integrated it with established risk factors to develop an optimal predictive model. Methods This retrospective study included 243 patients with full-thickness rotator cuff tears who underwent arthroscopic repair from July 2021 to January 2025. Preoperative CT and MRI were obtained for all patients; postoperative MRI at 3-6 months evaluated tendon healing using the Sugaya classification (grades I-III: intact healing, n = 208; grades IV-V: retear, n = 35). Statistical analyses used SPSS. After normality testing, continuous variables were compared using t-test or Mann-Whitney U test, and categorical variables using chi-square or Fisher's exact test. Variables with group differences were screened by elastic net regression, then entered into binary logistic regression. ROC analysis determined optimal cutoffs, and 1000 bootstrap samples provided an optimism-corrected C-statistic for internal validation. Results Multivariate analysis identified supraspinatus fatty infiltration (FI) (p < 0.01), the supraspinatus occupation ratio (SspOR) (p < 0.01), and the deltoid-to-supraspinatus HU ratio (D/S HU) (p < 0.01) as independent predictors of rotator cuff retear. In the univariate analysis, tear width, preoperative Patte stage, and the presence of concomitant frozen shoulder differed significantly between the intact healing and retear groups; however, none of these variables remained independent predictors in the multivariate model. The D/S HU was significantly lower in the intact healing group than in the retear group (0.87 ± 0.17 vs. 1.15 ± 0.29), further supporting its value as an independent predictor of retear. The optimal cutoff values for FI, SspOR, and the D/S HU were Goutallier Stage 2, 46.02%, and 1.02, respectively. The combination of a D/S HU > 1.02 and FI ≥ Goutallier Stage 2 provided the best predictive performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.868, sensitivity of 77.1%, specificity of 81.2%, and accuracy of 89.3%. Conclusions The D/S HU was significantly associated with postoperative rotator cuff retear, and a ratio greater than 1.02 was identified as an effective threshold for predicting retear. Moreover, the combination of a D/S HU > 1.02 and FI ≥ Goutallier Stage 2 yielded the strongest predictive performance. This preoperative risk assessment model may help surgeons optimize treatment planning and better anticipate postoperative outcomes.

title: Outcomes of Subcutaneous Implantable Cardioverter Defibrillators in Patients Being Considered for Heart Transplantation: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Introduction Subcutaneous implantable cardioverter defibrillators (S-ICD) are an alternative to transvenous devices (TV-ICD) in patients not requiring bradycardia pacing, resynchronization (CRT) or anti-tachycardia pacing (ATP). At our center, S-ICDs are often preferred in patients being considered for heart transplantation (HTx) without pacing/CRT/ATP needs, as their removal post-HTx avoids retained transvenous leads which can preclude MRI surveillance for graft rejection. We assessed outcomes of S-ICDs in this population. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 201 S-ICD implants at our center; July 2016 - March 2025. Results We identified 33 patients (22 male; age 46 ± 13 years) who, at time of S-ICD implant, had been referred for HTx evaluation or were referred at any time thereafter. Etiologies were nonischemic cardiomyopathy (n = 18), hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (n = 5), ischemic cardiomyopathy (n = 4), congenital heart disease (n = 4), and myocarditis (n = 2). Median follow-up was 296 days [IQR = 72-798]. Two patients died, both non-arrhythmic. Four patients received appropriate S-ICD therapies and three had inappropriate shocks due to P- or T-wave oversensing (TWOS) (n = 2), or a rapidly conducted atrial arrhythmia (n = 1). Three patients, all with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, received transvenous device upgrades: one to CRT-P for disease progression, one to TV-ICD for ATP-terminable ventricular tachycardia and one to TV-ICD due to inappropriate shocks from TWOS. Thirteen patients underwent HTx at median 257 days [IQR = 130-453] post S-ICD; three of whom were bridged with HeartMate 3 LVADs. One LVAD patient needed S-ICD deactivation due to electromagnetic interference. There were no retained device components following HTx and S-ICD extraction. Conclusion In selected pre-HTx patients, S-ICDs offer arrhythmic protection while avoiding retained leads post-HTx.

Median follow-up was 296 days [IQR = 72-798]. Two patients died, both non-arrhythmic. Four patients received appropriate S-ICD therapies and three had inappropriate shocks due to P- or T-wave oversensing (TWOS) (n = 2), or a rapidly conducted atrial arrhythmia (n = 1). Three patients, all with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, received transvenous device upgrades: one to CRT-P for disease progression, one to TV-ICD for ATP-terminable ventricular tachycardia and one to TV-ICD due to inappropriate shocks from TWOS. Thirteen patients underwent HTx at median 257 days [IQR = 130-453] post S-ICD; three of whom were bridged with HeartMate 3 LVADs. One LVAD patient needed S-ICD deactivation due to electromagnetic interference. There were no retained device components following HTx and S-ICD extraction.

Conclusion

In selected pre-HTx patients, S-ICDs offer arrhythmic protection while avoiding retained leads post-HTx.

title: Disseminated Bartonella or Post-Transplant Lymphoproliferative Disease in Pediatric Transplant Patients: A Diagnostic Challenge.
abstract: Post transplant lymphoproliferative disease (PTLD) and infection remain the two most common complications of solid organ transplant and carry a risk of significant morbidity and mortality. PTLD is a highly variable disease with clinical signs and symptoms that are non-specific and require a high degree of suspicion to detect. The most common presenting symptoms of PTLD are malaise, fatigue, fever, and a mononucleosis-like picture; night sweats, weight loss, and lymphadenopathy are also frequent manifestations. An infection with Bartonella Henselae is another known cause of local lymphadenopathy. However, in immunocompromised individuals, Bartonella Henselae is far more likely to cause a systemic response that may mimic PTLD. The specifics regarding differentiating systemic bartonella and PTLD in pediatric solid organ transplant patients are not well described. There have been more detailed descriptions of disseminated bartonella mimicking PTLD in solid organ transplants in adult patients, but this has not been thoroughly reported or described in the pediatric population. Upon literature review, only five cases of disseminated bartonella in pediatric kidney transplant recipients have been described, with three of them possibly associated with PTLD. The past cases described antimicrobial diagnostics for bartonella and other infections, but none of these reported full histopathological findings or associated imaging studies for work-up of PTLD. In addition, past cases have only been described in Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and Cytomegalovirus (CMV) negative children. There is no consensus for treatment duration and antibiotic choice for confirmed systemic bartonella infection in pediatric kidney transplant patients due to concerns of nephrotoxicity and drug interactions. This patient who presented with fever, lymphadenopathy, nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain was worked up and treated for both Bartonella Henslae and PTLD. PET Scan and biopsies were taken for the diagnosis of PTLD and the patient had Bartonella serologies and PCR testing done as part of a broader infectious workup. Clinical decisions regarding his treatment plan and the cause of his symptoms were made based on response to treatment and the likelihood of underlying etiology based on the timeline which his symptoms improved. After an extensive workup for PTLD and altering immunosuppressive regimens temporarily for possible PTLD we ultimately determined the cause of the patients' symptoms to be secondary to B. henselae infection. The patient was treated appropriately for disseminated Bartonella and improved significantly. He has followed up as an outpatient with continued improvement in symptoms and resumed his previous immunosuppression regimen as PTLD has been ruled out. Bartonella and PTLD are diagnoses that need to be carefully considered and treated in vulnerable populations. Pediatric patients should be managed cautiously with both etiologies under consideration, and more research is needed for specific recommendations regarding differentiating and treating the two simultaneously when clinical presentation is questionable. Given the overlapping symptoms, a thorough workup to rule out and treat PTLD if necessary is recommended given its significant mortality if missed. With biopsy being the gold standard, we recommend careful consideration of performing a biopsy while treating underlying infectious concerns in cases where PTLD is a possibility in pediatric populations.

title: Comparison of Clinical and Ultrasonographic Severity Assessment in Hidradenitis Suppurativa: Prognostic Implications.
abstract: Background Accurate assessment of hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) severity is crucial for individualized management, yet conventional clinical grading may underestimate disease extent due to subclinical lesions. Ultrasound enables visualization of deep abscesses and tunnels and may provide additional prognostic information. Materials and methods Sixty-eight patients with HS underwent standardized clinical and ultrasonographic evaluation. Disease severity was classified using the International Hidradenitis Suppurativa Severity Score System (IHS4) and the modified Sonographic Scoring of HS (mSOS-HS). Concordance between the two systems was assessed, and ultrasonographic grading and features were analyzed in relation to achievement of IHS4-55 at week 12. Results The mSOS-HS classified 18 patients (26.5%) as having more severe disease than IHS4. The two grading systems showed statistically significant agreement, with the Kappa value approaching the threshold for moderate agreement (Kappa = 0.395, 95% CI: 0.204-0.586, p < 0.001). Patients with higher mSOS-HS grades were less likely to achieve IHS4-55 at week 12 (p = 0.014). Among specific ultrasonographic features, the railway sign, defined as parallel hyperechoic lines within tunnel-like structures, was significantly associated with failure to achieve IHS4-55 (p = 0.003). Conclusion Ultrasonography reveals subclinical HS involvement beyond clinical examination and provides prognostic information for treatment response. The mSOS-HS complements IHS4 for comprehensive disease staging, while the railway sign may serve as an imaging biomarker for unfavorable response across real-world treatment settings.

title: Non-invasive Imaging Modalities for Breslow Thickness Estimation in Melanoma: A Scoping Review.
abstract: Background Breslow thickness (BT) is the most important prognostic biomarker in cutaneous melanoma and directly influences surgical management, sentinel lymph node biopsy decisions and survival outcomes. Several non-invasive imaging modalities have been investigated for preoperative BT estimation; however, their relative performance and clinical applicability remain unclear. Objective To evaluate the agreement between non-invasive imaging-derived and histopathologically measured BT and to compare the technical characteristics, diagnostic performance, and clinical utility of currently available imaging modalities for preoperative melanoma staging. Methods A scoping review was conducted according to Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and reported following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to December 1, 2025. Original studies evaluating non-invasive imaging techniques for BT estimation in cutaneous melanoma were included. Imaging modalities assessed comprised dermoscopy, reflectance confocal microscopy (RCM), optical coherence tomography (OCT), ultrasound (US), multispectral imaging (MSI), photoacoustic techniques, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), and artificial intelligence (AI)-based approaches. Results Ninety-two studies met the inclusion criteria. Dermoscopy provided indirect assessment of invasiveness, while RCM and OCT offered complementary microstructural information but limited direct thickness estimation. US, particularly high-frequency (≥20 MHz) and ultra-high-frequency (≥50 MHz) systems, showed the strongest and most consistent evidence for direct BT assessment, with correlation coefficients often exceeding 0.90 and high performance across clinically relevant thresholds. Nevertheless, performance varied across devices, probe frequencies, acquisition protocols, and operators, with frequent overestimation and reduced accuracy in selected subgroups (in situ and thin melanomas). MSI showed moderate-to-good classification performance, while photoacoustic techniques yielded promising results but limited to small cohorts. Evidence for MRI and SPECT was scarce. AI-based approaches achieved moderate-to-good predictive performance but did not consistently outperform experienced clinicians, with generalizability limited by dataset and methodological heterogeneity. Conclusions US currently represents the most extensively validated and clinically applicable non-invasive modality for preoperative BT estimation. A hierarchical imaging approach appears most appropriate, with dermoscopy as the first-line diagnostic tool, RCM and OCT providing additional lesion characterization, and HFUS enabling complementary depth assessment in lesions strongly suspicious for melanoma. Emerging photoacoustic and AI-based approaches require further validation, while histopathology remains the reference standard for definitive diagnosis and BT measurement.

title: Polarization Sensitive Optical Coherence Tomography for Surgical Margin Assessment for Canine Soft Tissue Sarcoma.
abstract: Soft tissue sarcomas (STSs) and skeletal muscle both appear high scattering on spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) imaging, which resulted in instances of misclassification by observers in prior soft tissue sarcoma margin assessment studies. Polarization-sensitive optical coherence tomography (PS-OCT) is an extension of OCT that provides additional information about tissue polarization contrast. In this prospective study we wanted to evaluate whether PS-OCT improves tissue differentiation and diagnostic accuracy compared to spectral-domain OCT (SD-OCT) alone. PS-OCT images from surgical margins of 10 resected STS were compared with histopathology to identify characteristic features of normal and neoplastic tissues. Then, six observers of varying OCT image interpretation experience assessed surgical margins from 30 resected STS using SD-OCT alone and SD-OCT combined with PS-OCT. PS-OCT images demonstrated distinct birefringence (optical patterns), corresponding to tissue organization: skeletal muscle exhibited alternating high and low birefringence bands, fascia showed variable birefringence and STS had uniformly low birefringence. Overall diagnostic accuracy was high for both modalities [correct classification rate: SD-OCT alone 93.7% (95% confidence interval (CI): 90.1, 96.0) vs. SD-OCT combined with PS-OCT 92.6% (95% = CI: 89.3, 95.4)]; adding PS-OCT did not significantly improve accuracy across all observers (p = 0.82), though expert observers benefited significantly (p = 0.0018). Interobserver and intraobserver agreement ranged from substantial to near perfect. These findings suggest PS-OCT can be interpreted reliably after brief training and may enhance accuracy for experienced users. Further research should explore structured training and real-time applications for comprehensive surgical margin evaluation.

title: A New Application of 64 CuCl 2 PET/CT: Imaging of Cats With Mammary Carcinoma.
abstract: Feline mammary carcinoma (FMC) is an aggressive and highly metastatic cancer that shares molecular and clinical characteristics with human triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), making it a relevant comparative model for a disease lacking targeted therapies. This study investigated the feasibility and clinical utility of 64 CuCl 2 PET/CT imaging in cats with naturally occurring mammary carcinoma. Eight cats (seven tumour-bearing, one healthy control) were administered an intravenous dose of 64 CuCl 2 and underwent whole-body PET/CT imaging. Semi-quantitative analysis was performed using standardized uptake values (SUVs), and tumour-to-muscle ratios were calculated to assess lesion conspicuity. Serum ceruloplasmin concentrations were measured as a marker of systemic copper metabolism. All primary masses were 64 Cu-avid and conspicuous, with consistently elevated tumour-to-muscle ratios across tumour-bearing cats, allowing clear differentiation between neoplastic and normal tissue. Imaging provided additional staging information by identifying locally invasive and metastatic disease that was not fully evident on physical examination. Physiologic tracer distribution was characterized by high uptake in the liver and gallbladder and low uptake in skeletal muscle, which served as a reliable reference tissue. Serum ceruloplasmin concentrations varied widely and did not correlate with tumour uptake. These findings suggest that 64 CuCl 2 PET/CT is a feasible functional imaging modality for FMC, potentially aiding in tumour detection. This was an exploratory study, and not all imaging results could be confirmed by cytology or histopathology. Nonetheless, our findings suggest that 64 CuCl 2 PET/CT should be investigated further as a method for probing copper utilization in FMC.

title: Clinical Presentation, Acute Clinical Response, Drug Tolerability, and Short-Term Outcome of Cats Treated for Acute Congestive Heart Failure With Pimobendan (2017-2022): 71 Cases.
abstract: Objective To describe clinical effects, drug tolerability, and short-term outcomes of cats treated with pimobendan (PB) in conjunction with other therapies for acute congestive heart failure (CHF). Design Retrospective single-center study (2017 to 2022). Setting Academic teaching and referral hospital. Animals Seventy-one cats with acute CHF treated with PB and furosemide. Treatment included dobutamine (DB) in 15 cases. Measurements and main results Physical examination results, laboratory results, and radiographic pulmonary infiltrate scoring were assessed in all cats at admission and 24 h later. Respiratory rate and radiographic pulmonary infiltrate scores decreased after 24 h of therapy (p < 0.0001 for both values). Anemia and hypochloremia were more common than azotemia, hyponatremia, and hypokalemia on Day 1. Serum chloride and potassium concentrations decreased, and serum creatinine concentration increased after therapy (p < 0.05), but none of these values was associated with prolonged hospitalization or reduced survival. Cats receiving PB exhibited few adverse clinical signs. Seven of 15 cats (47%) that received concurrent DB therapy were suspected of having adverse effects that responded to decreased dosage or discontinuation of the medication. There was no difference in survival to discharge (p = 0.17) or days of hospitalization (p = 0.78) between cats receiving DB therapy and those that did not. Overall survival to discharge was 76%, and 75% of cats discharged alive were discharged in ≤3 days. Conclusions The short-term prognosis for cats treated for acute CHF was good, and PB therapy appeared to be well tolerated. Most cats showed clinical and radiographic improvement in the first 24 h of therapy and were hospitalized for ≤3 days. The addition of DB to therapy in some cats did not alter survival and was associated with adverse clinical signs in 7/15 cats (47%) treated with DB.

title: Bilateral Keratouveitis and Secondary Glaucoma in a Young Dog With Immune-Mediated Polyarthritis and Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome.
abstract: A 7-month-old intact female mixed-breed dog presented emergently for inability to walk, lethargy, and vomiting. The patient was diagnosed with immune-mediated polyarthritis (IMPA) and secondary systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS). Bilateral keratouveitis and secondary glaucoma developed within 24 h of presentation. Thorough diagnostic testing failed to identify an underlying etiology. Despite aggressive medical management, the patient developed rapid vision loss. Due to poor visual prognosis and anticipated need for long-term medical management, both eyes were enucleated. Histopathological evaluation of both globes revealed severe corneal endothelial injury most consistent with endotheliitis with associated uveitis and endophthalmitis. Testing of ocular tissue with PCR and immunohistochemistry for canine adenovirus was negative, and comprehensive infectious disease screening, joint cultures, and ocular histopathology identified no other causative agents. Following enucleation, the dog systemically improved with anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial medical management. This report highlights a unique and severe case of bilateral keratouveitis with glaucoma following a systemic inflammatory event.

title: Effect of thoracic duct identification by CT lymphangiography and intraoperative contrast on surgical outcome in cats with idiopathic chylothorax.
abstract: Objective To report the success of thoracic duct (TD) enhancement in cats with idiopathic chylothorax on preoperative computed tomography lymphangiography (CTLA) and intraoperative TD colorization (IOC), and to compare surgical outcomes between cats that did and did not have successful pre- and intraoperative TD enhancement. Study design Multi-institutional retrospective study. Animals A total of 24 cats undergoing preoperative CTLA, IOC and TD ligation between February 2016 and January 2025. Methods Signalment, preoperative diagnostics, method of iohexol administration and quality of TD enhancement on CTLA, surgical procedure, success of TD enhancement via intraoperative colorization, postoperative complications, and clinical outcome were reviewed. Results TD enhancement on CTLA was successful in 70.8% of cats, with similar quality of enhancement appreciated with metatarsal and popliteal iohexol injection. TD colorization with indocyanine green (ICG) seen via near-infrared fluorescence (NIRF) was successful in four of five (80%) cats, while methylene blue was successful in eight of 15 (53%) cats. title: Outcome following lag screw fixation of non-C3 carpal slab fractures in horses.
abstract: Objective To describe clinical features and short- and long-term outcomes of horses treated with lag screw fixation of slab fractures of the radial carpal (Cr), intermediate carpal (Ci), ulnar carpal (Cu), second (C2) or fourth (C4) carpal bones. Study design Retrospective case study. Animals Horses (n = 19) treated with lag screw fixation for slab fractures of Cr, Ci, Cu, C2 or C4. Methods Medical records of patients with carpal slab fractures were reviewed, and those undergoing internal fixation of slab fractures involving Cr, Ci, Cu, C2, or C4 carpal bones from January 2008 to January 2026 were included. Long-term outcomes were obtained by a standardized questionnaire. Descriptive data are presented. Results Predominant breeds included Thoroughbreds (7/19) and Warmbloods (7/19). A total of 10 of 19 fractures were caused by traumatic falls, including six during recovery from general anesthesia. Five of 19 surgeries were performed with arthroscopic guidance, and 14/19 surgeries were performed with computed tomography (CT) guidance. Survival beyond 1 year was 88%, with 53% returning to previous athletic function and 71% owner satisfaction. Conclusion Prognosis for return to the previous level of work was good and comparable to that previously reported for internal fixation of C3 slab fractures. Clinical significance Lag screw fixation provides good outcomes in survival, return to work, and owner satisfaction for slab fractures of Cr, Ci, Cu, C2, or C4.

title: Update on non-radiologic ocular and orbital imaging in thyroid eye disease: a review.
abstract: Significance Thyroid eye disease (TED) involves inflammatory, vascular, and fibrotic remodeling of periocular tissues that is traditionally characterized by clinical activity scores and, at times, by conventional neuroimaging. Emerging noninvasive imaging modalities are poised to enhance clinical assessment by objectively quantifying inflammation, vascular alterations, fibrosis, and changes in tissue architecture. These tissue biomarkers have the potential to improve prediction of disease progression and therapeutic response beyond what can be inferred from clinical activity scores alone. Aim This review synthesizes established and emerging periocular nonionizing imaging techniques for TED, including ultrasound-based methods, optical coherence tomography (OCT), confocal microscopy (CM), and spatial frequency domain imaging (SFDI). Approach Peer-reviewed studies evaluating human subjects with TED were reviewed to understand the technical aspects, advantages, limitations, and clinical relevance of each modality. Results Ultrasound elastography and high-frequency ultrasonography enable assessment of tissue stiffness, thickness, and vascularity but are limited by operator dependence and penetration depth. OCT and OCT-angiography provide high-resolution evaluation of retinal, choroidal, and anterior segment structural and vascular changes associated with orbital congestion. Confocal microscopy identifies anatomical alterations that differentiate active from inactive disease. SFDI enables wide-field, noncontact quantification of periocular optical properties, with preliminary findings suggesting sensitivity to inflammatory edema. Conclusions This review summarizes current and emerging imaging modalities used to provide quantitative, high-resolution assessment of structural and functional tissue changes in TED.

title: SEFCA-Net: a semantic-edge-frequency cross-attention network for diabetic retinopathy lesion segmentation.
abstract: Significance Diabetic retinopathy (DR) lesion segmentation provides pixel-level lesion localization in fundus images. However, such lesions are often tiny, sparsely distributed, low-contrast, morphologically diverse, and visually similar to vessels or surrounding retinal structures, making accurate localization difficult. Many existing methods emphasize multi-scale spatial representation learning and handle boundary ambiguity and subtle texture differences mainly through encoder-decoder fusion. We therefore examine boundary and frequency representations as explicit, complementary inputs to semantic decoding. Aim We aim to develop SEFCA-Net, a semantic-edge-frequency cross-attention network for diabetic retinopathy lesion segmentation. The main objective is to examine whether semantic, edge, and frequency-domain representations can be fused under semantic guidance to improve pixel-level lesion localization without compromising the semantic decoding stream. The evaluation focuses on four lesion categories, including hard exudates, hemorrhages, soft exudates, and microaneurysms, using public benchmarks and a DDR-to-IDRiD cross-dataset setting. Approach SEFCA-Net uses HRNet-W48 as the semantic backbone to extract multi-scale semantic features and explicitly constructs edge and frequency-domain representations from input fundus images. The learnable multi-scale edge branch extracts boundary-sensitive features, while the all-channel multi-scale discrete cosine transform (DCT) frequency-domain branch generates texture-sensitive responses to low-contrast lesions. The semantic-edge-frequency cross-attention decoder uses the semantic representation as the primary stream and injects edge and frequency-domain features through semantic-guided window-based cross-attention. Performance is evaluated using the area under the precision-recall curve (AUPR), Dice, and Intersection-over-Union (IoU). Results On DDR, SEFCA-Net achieves 47.85% mean AUPR (mAUPR), 46.76% mean Dice, and 31.22% mean IoU. On IDRiD, it reaches 69.74% mAUPR; when trained on DDR and tested on IDRiD, it obtains 59.83% mAUPR. Ablation studies show that either auxiliary branch improves the semantic-only baseline and that the complete configuration gives the highest mAUPR. Multi-scale Sobel modeling and DCT outperform the tested single-scale and wavelet alternatives, respectively. Conclusions SEFCA-Net shows that semantic features can remain the main decoding stream while boundary-sensitive features and texture-sensitive responses are integrated in a controlled manner. Under the evaluated protocols, the model shows competitive in-domain performance and records the highest DDR-to-IDRiD mAUPR among the reproduced methods.

title: Benchmarking deep learning-based reconstruction methods for photoacoustic computed tomography with clinically relevant synthetic datasets.
abstract: Significance Deep learning (DL)-based image reconstruction methods for photoacoustic computed tomography (PACT) have developed rapidly in recent years. However, most existing methods have not employed standardized datasets, and their evaluations rely on traditional image quality (IQ) metrics that may lack clinical relevance. The absence of a standardized framework for clinically meaningful IQ assessment hinders fair comparison and raises concerns about the reproducibility and reliability of reported advancements in PACT. Aim A benchmarking framework is proposed that provides open-source, anatomically plausible synthetic datasets and evaluation strategies for DL-based acoustic inversion methods in PACT. Approach The datasets each include over 10,000 two-dimensional (2D) stochastic breast objects with clinically relevant lesions and paired measurements at varying modeling complexity. The evaluation strategies incorporate both traditional and task-based IQ measures to assess fidelity and clinical utility. A preliminary benchmarking study is conducted to demonstrate the framework's utility by comparing DL-based and physics-based reconstruction methods. Results The benchmarking study demonstrated that the proposed framework enabled comprehensive, quantitative comparisons of reconstruction performance and revealed important limitations in certain DL-based methods. Although they performed well according to traditional IQ measures, they often failed to accurately recover lesions. This highlights the inadequacy of traditional metrics and motivates the need for task-based assessments. Conclusions The proposed benchmarking framework enables systematic comparisons of DL-based acoustic inversion methods for 2D PACT. By integrating clinically relevant synthetic datasets with rigorous evaluation protocols, it enables reproducible, objective assessments and facilitates method development and system optimization in PACT.

title: Decoder-FFPE-seq enables sensitive, genome-wide spatial transcriptomics of archival tissues at single-cell resolution.
abstract: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue-compatible spatial transcriptomics (ST) is transforming biology and histopathology, but achieving high sensitivity, genome-wide coverage, single-cell resolution, and researcher accessibility remains challenging. To address these challenges, we here present a dendrimeric DNA coordinate barcoding design for FFPE tissue-adapted spatial RNA sequencing (Decoder-FFPE-seq) by integrating RNA-to-DNA probe conversion with blotting-assisted barcoding. Decoder-FFPE-seq provides single-cell resolution with a >2.6-fold sensitivity increase in whole-transcriptome mouse brain and archived human sample profiling over existing platforms, resolving potential cellular identity of low-abundance genes, finer tissue architecture, and capturing an epithelial-mesenchymal transition-associated signature for prognostic value. With expanded probe libraries, Decoder-FFPE-seq captures long noncoding and viral RNAs, revealing their spatial coregulatory networks with messenger RNAs in oral squamous cell carcinomas (OSCCs). In an OSCC immunotherapy cohort, two CD8 + T cell subpopulations were respectively identified in pre- and postchemoimmunotherapy samples, potentially linked to treatment response. Decoder-FFPE-seq establishes a robust, high-resolution, and accessible framework for sensitive ST profiling of archival tissues in fundamental and translational studies.

title: Insights into temporal and spatial dynamics of short association fiber formation in the human fetal brain.
abstract: Short association fibers (SAFs) form the local scaffold of cortical connectivity and support early functional specialization. However, their development before birth remains largely unknown. Using fetal diffusion magnetic resonance imaging from the Developing Human Connectome Project and histology from the Zagreb Collection of human brains, we present an in utero reconstruction of SAF pathways in the human brain. We tracked their volumetric and microstructural developmental trajectories in 243 fetuses spanning a critical period of connectome formation. We found that SAFs emerge before sulcal folding, initially as flat, loosely arranged pathways along the subplate-white matter interface, and later reorganize into coherent U-shaped bundles. Their maturation followed a sensorimotor-to-association gradient, paralleling cortical development. Nonlinear, bundle-specific trajectories captured multiphasic maturation, with subplate dynamics preceding increases in axonal coherence and early myelination. These findings reveal how the brain's local wiring is established during prenatal development and provide insight into the origins of individual variability.

title: Ultrasound-driven electronically programmable microbubbles.
abstract: Ultrasound-actuated microbubbles have served as efficient microscale engines demonstrating wireless actuation, simplified robotic architectures, and rapid response. Despite recent advances, a limitation of many microbubble technologies is that they use passive capturing of bubbles. The lack of control over bubble placement and size hinders the ability to individually address specified bubbles, a feature that would be important for performing multiple functions. Here, we present an on-chip bubble customization platform that enables active control of individual microbubbles. Instead of trapping bubbles, we purposely generate them via electrolysis on electrode arrays. The bubbles, when actuated by an external ultrasound input, create a variety of programmed flows ranging from streaming due to volumetric oscillation of a single bubble to diverse symmetry-broken directional flows when multiple bubbles interact. The bubble configuration can also be altered by simply increasing the electrolysis voltage on specified electrodes to detach the unneeded bubbles. We find that in this regime, when coupled to acoustic oscillations, we can generate a distinct bubble shooting flow pattern whose flow direction is selectively controlled by the incident ultrasound frequency. Collectively, the active bubble reconfiguration ability unlocks a range of previously inaccessible acoustofluidic functions in a single device with unprecedented controllability.

title: BCG vaccination mitigates tau pathology and restores cognitive function in PS19 mice.
abstract: Retrospective studies in patients with nonmuscle invasive bladder cancer have reported a significant reduction in Alzheimer's disease incidence (12 to 78%) among Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) recipients versus controls. To investigate the underlying mechanisms, we evaluated BCG in the PS19 mouse model of tauopathy. We found that BCG administration reduced hippocampal phospho-tau and microgliosis while preserving neuronal markers. In vivo volumetric T2-magnetic resonance Imaging (MRI) demonstrated attenuation of brain atrophy accompanied by increased glutamate-weighted chemical exchange saturation transfer-MRI signals. Functionally, BCG-treated mice showed improved performance in the novel object recognition test, as well as improved body-weight maintenance and survival. Transcriptomic profiling of the hippocampus revealed near complete normalization of the PS19 disease-associated gene expression signature toward that of healthy controls. Flow cytometric profiling of brain myeloid populations demonstrated a reduction in activated resident microglia, but total microglia cells remain elevated. Moreover, an increase of trained immunity marker CD80 on the recruited peripheral myeloid cells ensues following BCG treatment. Consistent with this shift in myeloid state, primary brain myeloid cells from BCG-treated mice also exhibited enhanced phagocytosis of fluorescein isothiocyanate-labeled tau fibrils and increased lactate production. Together, these findings indicate that BCG induces systemic and central nervous system myeloid cell reprogramming that limits neuroinflammation, enhances tau clearance, and rescues cognitive and neurodegenerative phenotypes in a tauopathy model. BCG is a safe, readily available therapy that merits consideration as a preventive agent against dementia.

title: A fluorescent choline kinase alpha inhibitor for intraoperative molecular imaging during resection of canine NSCLC tumors.
abstract: Choline kinase α (ChoKα) is a biomarker of lung cancer, is overexpressed in 60% of human pulmonary malignancies, and is associated with an aggressive phenotype and poor clinical outcome. Patients with lung cancer who undergo surgery have a recurrence rate of 30 to 50%, indicating a potential need for better tumor detection modalities. A near-infrared fluorescent ChoKα-targeting imaging agent, JAS239 (λ ex , λ em : 745, 775 nanometers), was developed for intraoperative identification of tumors, their margins, and local metastases. In lung cancer cells, JAS239 inhibited phosphocholine production, reduced viability in a dose-dependent manner, and accumulated in the cytoplasm where ChoKα is active. JAS239 had favorable pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics for imaging metastatic lung lesions in mice. In situ and ex vivo fluorescence imaging of primary lung tumors in a canine clinical trial showed distinct tumor identification and margin delineation with a tumor-to-background ratio of 5.0 ± 0.6 and a contrast-to-variance ratio of 2.0 ± 0.2 at 0.5 milligram/kilogram. Fluorescence imaging identified a clinically significant event where an occult lesion was found after primary tumor resection. Fluorescence imaging also identified a close surgical margin, which prompted further investigation. Immunohistochemistry for ChoKα showed overexpression in canine lung tumors proportional to tumor fluorescence. Ex vivo human tumor painting demonstrated preferential JAS239 localization with a tumor-to-background ratio of 1.5 ± 0.1 and a contrast-to-variance ratio of 0.9 ± 0.1. These studies establish JAS239 as a safe and effective imaging agent for intraoperative lung tumor detection, warranting further evaluation for human patients with lung cancer.

title: Molecular epidemiology and pathological burden of Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis in staple livestock from Pakistan: implications for zoonotic surveillance and livestock productivity.
abstract: Paratuberculosis (Johne's disease), caused by Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis (MAP), is a chronic granulomatous enteritis affecting domestic and wild ruminants worldwide, with significant economic losses. Its potential zoonotic implications in humans have increased concern globally. Despite its global importance, limited data exist on MAP prevalence in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. A cross-sectional study was conducted in Peshawar district, Pakistan, using a multimodal diagnostic approach. Serum ( n = 350), fecal ( n = 350), and tissue samples (intestine and mesenteric lymph nodes; n = 400) were collected from cattle and buffaloes. Samples were analyzed using indirect enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, Ziehl-Neelsen staining, histopathology, and PCR targeting IS900, IS1311, and Mycobacterium bovis -specific genes. Seroprevalence of MAP was 9% (17/175) in cattle and 4% (7/175) in buffaloes ( P = 0.03). Acid-fast bacilli were detected in 22% (39/175) of cattle and 10% (19/175) of buffalo fecal samples. Gross pathological lesions, including thickness/corrugation in the intestine and hemorrhages/edematous swelling in the mesenteric lymph node, were found at higher frequencies in cattle compared to buffaloes. PCR confirmed MAP in 5% of cattle and 3% of buffalo tissue samples, while one cattle sample harbored M. bovis . Emaciated animals exhibited significantly higher lesion severity ( P < 0.001). This study confirms endemic MAP infection in staple livestock of the study area, with higher susceptibility in cattle. This study underscores the importance of molecular diagnostics in surveillance and the critical role of abattoirs in monitoring disease prevalence. The presence of MAP and co-detection of M. bovis highlight the need for integrated control strategies under a One Health framework to investigate and mitigate potential zoonotic risks and production losses in resource-limited dairy systems.IMPORTANCEThis study provides the first comprehensive molecular epidemiological data on Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis (MAP) in cattle and buffaloes from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. Using a multimodal approach (serology, histopathology, and PCR), it reveals significant infection rates, with cattle being more susceptible than buffaloes. The work is critically significant as it confirms the endemic presence of MAP in a key dairy region and highlights a concurrent infection with Mycobacterium bovis , underscoring a compounded potential zoonotic risk. These findings emphasize the urgent need for integrated One Health strategies to mitigate transmission through improved surveillance, milk pasteurization, and control programs in resource-limited settings.

title: Impact of different clarithromycin resistance in Mycobacterium abscessus lung disease: a multicenter cohort study.
abstract: Macrolides remained cornerstone of Mycobacterium abscessus treatment, but emerging resistance patterns compromised therapeutic efficacies. Clarithromycin resistance can manifest as either mutational or inducible, while the clinical impacts of different resistance mechanisms in M. abscessus pulmonary disease (MAB-PD) had been poorly characterized. We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study from 2011 to 2023 across four tertiary centers in Taiwan. Adults with clarithromycin-resistant MAB-PD were included and stratified by resistance type: mutational vs inducible. Outcomes included all-cause 3-year mortality, microbiological clearance, and radiographic progression. Among 108 enrolled patients, 16 (14.7%) had mutational resistance and the remaining 92 had inducible type. Isolates comprised 103 M. abscessus , three M. massiliense , and two M. bolletii . Mutational resistance was associated with significantly higher 3-year mortality (18.8% vs 4.3%, P = 0.03) and lower acid-fast smear conversion rates in treated patients (18.2% vs 67.6%, P = 0.004). Multivariable analysis identified mutational clarithromycin resistance as an independent predictor of mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 5.21, 95% confidence interval 1.10-24.6, P = 0.04). Strains with mutational resistance demonstrated higher median minimal inhibitory concentrations to linezolid (24 vs 16 mg/L), cefoxitin (64 vs 32 mg/L), and amikacin (16 vs 8 mg/L). Mutational clarithromycin resistance in MAB-PD is associated with substantially worse clinical outcomes compared to inducible resistance, including higher mortality and poorer treatment responses. These findings suggested that more intensive treatment strategies might be needed for mutational clarithromycin resistance in MAB-PD. Importance Macrolide resistance critically undermines treatment outcomes in Mycobacterium abscessus lung disease, yet the prognostic impact of distinct resistance mechanisms has remained unclear. This multicenter study demonstrates that mutational clarithromycin resistance, although less common than inducible resistance, is associated with markedly higher mortality, poorer microbiological response, and broader multidrug resistance. These findings provide clinically actionable evidence that not all macrolide resistance is equivalent. Recognizing mutational resistance as a high-risk phenotype has important implications for risk stratification, prognostication, and treatment intensification, supporting a more personalized approach to managing MAB-LD in routine clinical practice.

title: Malignant phyllodes tumour with spinal metastasis presenting as cauda equina syndrome.
abstract: Malignant phyllodes tumours (MPTs) are rare fibroepithelial breast neoplasms. While local recurrence is relatively common, distant metastasis is uncommon. Spinal metastases are exceptionally rare, with only a handful of cases in the literature. This case describes a female in her early 50s with a prior diagnosis of borderline phyllodes tumour status post right mastectomy and adjuvant radiotherapy. Two years post treatment, she presented with progressive lower back and bilateral leg pain, later identified as severe spinal canal compression causing cauda equina syndrome secondary to an L4 vertebral lesion. A decompression with biopsy was performed, followed by a two-stage L4 vertebrectomy, cage reconstruction, and instrumented L2-S1 spinal fusion. Although histopathology was inconclusive, molecular profiling confirmed that the spinal lesion was metastatic MPT. This case underscores the aggressive potential of MPTs and the importance of considering spinal metastases in the differential diagnosis of patients with back pain and a history of phyllodes tumour.

title: Insights into diagnosis and management of giant adrenal pseudocysts.
abstract: Adrenal cysts are rare lesions that may coexist with, or mimic, malignant adrenal tumours. Their shared imaging characteristics may cause misdiagnosis with potentially harmful outcomes.We report the case of a young man who presented with several months of headaches and mild anaemia. Non-contrast CT imaging revealed a giant left adrenal cystic lesion measuring 19×15×15 cm with indeterminate CT attenuation and internal debris. 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography demonstrated low peripheral uptake favouring a benign aetiology. The multidisciplinary recommendation was for excision given the lesion size, mass effect and risk of rupture. Open adrenalectomy confirmed a benign pseudocyst. This case demonstrates the diagnostic challenges posed by giant adrenal pseudocysts and highlights the importance of multimodality imaging and multidisciplinary input to prevent misdiagnosis and ensure appropriate management.
