title: Petrous Apex Mucocele: A Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: BackgroundA petrous apex mucocele is a rare benign cystic lesion that can present with symptoms due to pressure on surrounding structures, including the internal carotid artery, Meckel's cave and the fifth and sixth cranial nerves, as well as the cavernous sinus region and inner ear.MethodsA 36-year-old male presented with 8 months of diplopia when looking to the right, a right-sided temporoparietal headache, and paresthesia in the right half of his face. An MRI revealed a 26 × 32 × 37 mm lesion in the right petrous apex. The lesion's signal characteristics were most consistent with a mucocele. We performed an endoscopic endonasal transclival marsupialization and created a wide drainage opening, which we supported by inserting a stent containing mometasone furoate.ResultsThe postoperative course was marked by transient arterial hypertension, which required antihypertensive treatment. Postoperative imaging studies revealed no intracranial complications and confirmed that the drainage pathway remained patent.ConclusionIn the differential diagnosis of lesions in the medial portion of the petrous apex, a mucocele should be considered. In appropriately selected cases, endoscopic endonasal marsupialization can be an effective option. To maintain postoperative patency of the drainage pathway, an implant containing mometasone furoate may also be used.

title: Rare Migrated Fishbone Foreign Body in the Nasopharynx.
abstract: Although impaction of the pharyngoesophageal fishbone represents a common otolaryngological emergency, migration of an ingested fish bone into the nasopharynx is an extremely rare clinical occurrence. We present a 57-year-old woman who developed acute odynophagia one hour after fish ingestion, accompanied by a single choking episode, in the absence of nausea or vomiting. The oropharyngeal examination at the bedside failed to identify any foreign body. Given the patient's refusal to computed tomography (CT), she was discharged for outpatient surveillance. Twenty-four hours later, she returned with persistent refractory pharyngeal pain. Repeated pharyngeal endoscopy revealed neither foreign material nor mucosal injury. Multiplanar coronal CT reconstruction identified a 2.63 cm linear hyperattenuating bone fragment within the nasopharyngeal cavity. After topical nasal decongestion, flexible fiberoptic nasopharyngoscopy confirmed a partially embedded migrated fish bone, which was successfully retrieved endoscopically using alligator grasping forceps. Odynophagia resolved immediately after extraction and the patient remained asymptomatic throughout the 2 week follow-up. For patients with persistent pharyngeal pain and high clinical suspicion of retained foreign bodies despite negative physical examination and endoscopic findings, CT should be considered the first-line cross-sectional modality to prevent missed.diagnoses and life-threatening cervicofacial septic complications.

title: Recognizing Odontogenic Maxillary Sinusitis in the ENT Clinic: Four CT Findings That Should Prompt Dental Evaluation.
abstract: Objective: This retrospective cohort study evaluated the proportion of maxillary sinuses with radiographic findings consistent with an odontogenic contribution among patients with imaging-confirmed acute or chronic maxillary sinusitis presenting to a single academic ENT clinic over one year. Sixty-five CT scans (84 sinuses) underwent multidisciplinary review for prespecified radiographic features. By highlighting imaging findings indicative of dental origin this study aims to improve recognition of possible odontogenic disease and appropriate multidisciplinary evaluation. Methods: Sixty-five patients were evaluated. Inclusion criteria required a visit diagnosis of chronic maxillary sinusitis (ICD10 J32.0) or acute maxillary sinusitis (ICD10 J01.00, J01.01), and a sinus CT within the preceding year. Each scan underwent multidisciplinary review by an oral and maxillofacial radiologist, an otolaryngologist, an otolaryngology resident, and a medical student. Scans were evaluated for maxillary sinus floor mucosal thickening and radiographic features suggestive of an odontogenic contribution, including periapical pathology, oroantral communication, large dental restorations, and widened periodontal ligament (PDL) space. Dental referral recommendations were based on multidisciplinary consensus from CT findings alone. Data were summarized using descriptive statistics. Results: Radiographic findings consistent with an odontogenic contribution were identified in 50/84 (59.52%) affected maxillary sinuses from 40 patients. Among these 50 sinuses, 17 (34%) showed widened PDL space, 15 (30%) showed oroantral communication, 28 (56%) showed periapical pathology, and 9 (18%) showed large dental restorations. There was consensus among the multidisciplinary team that in retrospect, among the 40 patients with OS, 38 required dental referrals. Conclusion: Radiographic findings consistent with an odontogenic contribution indicated a higher single-center cohort prevalence than expected based on population-level prevalence reports. The findings support deliberate review of the maxillary dentition on sinus CT, with this study outlining the key imaging features for odontogenic sinusitis.

title: MTL-LymphNet: A Lightweight Multi-Task Learning Framework for Simultaneous Lymph Node Segmentation and Metastasis Classification in Thyroid Cancer Ultrasound.
abstract: Ultrasound assessment of cervical lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid carcinoma is crucial but suffers from inter-observer variability. Existing deep learning solutions typically use separate single-task pipelines, resulting in parameter redundancy. We propose MTL-LymphNet, a lightweight, backbone-agnostic multi-task learning framework that simultaneously segments lymph nodes and classifies metastasis within a single forward pass, evaluated across 3 backbones and 4 loss weighting strategies. On 338 images from 2 independent clinical centers, MTL-LymphNet achieved an internal cross-validation Dice coefficient of 0.891 ± 0.022 and AUC of 0.948 ± 0.027. Bidirectional external validation revealed substantial domain shift, with cross-center Dice of 0.865 and 0.779, and AUC of 0.733 and 0.830. The multi-task configuration offered a favorable efficiency-performance trade-off (∆Dice = Δ, -0.014, P < .0001) for 40% fewer parameters than separate models. No backbone or weighting strategy consistently dominated, and calibration degraded substantially under domain shift (ECE: 0.049 internally vs 0.178-0.304 externally), requiring center-specific recalibration before clinical use. To our knowledge, this is the first MTL framework for cervical lymph node analysis with bidirectional multi-center validation and systematic ablation. With a compact size of 22.6 to 29.1 MB and CPU inference of 81 to 131 ms, MTL-LymphNet demonstrates technical feasibility as a CAD tool warranting prospective validation.

title: Rapid noncontrast MRI screening for iliac and left renal vein compression: A practical bSSFP technique.
abstract: ObjectivesTo describe a rapid, widely available, noncontrast magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) technique for first-line morphologic assessment of suspected iliac and left renal vein compression in patients with symptoms potentially related to pelvic venous disorders.MethodsWe use a two-stack axial two-dimensional balanced steady-state free precession (bSSFP) acquisition extending from the renal hila through the iliac bifurcation. The sequence is available on major MRI platforms as TrueFISP (Siemens), FIESTA (GE), or bTFE (Philips). Typical 1.5-T parameters are TR/TE 3.0-3.8/1.5-1.9 ms, flip angle 60-80°, 5-mm slice thickness, and 1.3-1.6-mm in-plane resolution. Localized shimming is performed for each stack.ResultsThe abbreviated examination requires approximately 10 minutes of scanner time, including planning and breath-hold acquisitions. It depicts the site and degree of iliac or left renal vein compression and demonstrates collateral pathways that may support physiologic relevance. Morphologic abnormalities are interpreted in the clinical context and are not considered diagnostic of a symptomatic syndrome in isolation.ConclusionsA short bSSFP protocol can provide a practical, radiation-free gateway examination when comprehensive MR venography is unavailable or undesirable. It may facilitate appropriate referral and procedural planning, while invasive assessment, including intravascular ultrasound when stenting is contemplated, remains necessary in selected patients.

title: Sex differences and prevalence of prior deep vein thrombosis among patients with incidental iliac vein compression on computed tomography.
abstract: PurposeThe purpose of this study was to identify risk factors and evaluate clinical outcomes associated with incidental left common iliac vein compression on CT imaging.MethodsThis is a retrospective study that reviewed venous-phase abdomen and pelvis CT scans to identify patients with incidental extrinsic compression of the left common iliac vein due to an overlying right common iliac artery. A total of 726 patients were included (364 females, 362 males; mean patient age: 61.9 ± 15.9 years). Board-certified radiologists reviewed all CT scans. Significant left iliac vein compression was defined as >50% luminal narrowing.ResultsSignificant iliac vein compression was identified in 114 (15.7%) patients and was more common in females (19.5%) versus males (11.9%) ( p < 0.01). Patients with iliac vein compression >50% had significantly lower BMI than those without compression (24.8 ± 6.2 vs 28.7 ± 7.2 kg/m 2 , p < 0.01). Patients with incidental left iliac vein compression had a higher rate of prior left lower extremity DVT ( p = 0.02).ConclusionIncidental left common iliac vein compression was present in approximately 16% of patients and was more frequent among females. Compression was associated with lower BMI and more than twice the rate of ipsilateral DVT, despite no prior diagnosis of MTS. These findings suggest that incidental iliac vein compression could have more clinical significance than previously recognized.

title: LipoVena AI framework: A physician-centered artificial intelligence-assisted approach for longitudinal assessment in lipedema and chronic venous disorders.
abstract: BackgroundChronic venous disorders and lipedema are complex and frequently underdiagnosed conditions characterized by heterogeneous clinical presentations, progressive tissue remodeling, and substantial variability in treatment response assessment. Despite advances in minimally invasive vascular interventions, longitudinal evaluation in routine clinical practice continues to rely heavily on subjective interpretation, non-standardized comparative imaging, and physician-dependent assessment pathways. The integration of multimodal vascular data into structured longitudinal clinical workflows remains limited.ObjectiveThis study introduces the LipoVena AI Framework , a physician-centered conceptual artificial intelligence-assisted clinical support architecture designed to facilitate multimodal integration, longitudinal treatment-response evaluation, and personalized monitoring in lipedema and chronic venous disease management.MethodsA retrospective observational clinical dataset consisting of 32 patients with chronic venous insufficiency, lipedema, reticular veins, spider veins, and mixed venous-lymphatic phenotypes was reviewed. Standardized standing-position photography, duplex ultrasound imaging, procedural documentation, and longitudinal 1-month follow-up assessments were integrated within a conceptual AI-assisted workflow. Representative patients underwent multimodal minimally invasive treatment strategies including endovenous laser therapy (EVLT), CLACS-guided sclerotherapy, radiofrequency-based tissue remodeling, and compression therapy. The proposed framework conceptually integrates multimodal imaging analysis, vascular mapping, comparative longitudinal assessment, and physician-supervised AI-assisted interpretation.ResultsRepresentative 1-month follow-up observations demonstrated visible improvements in contour harmonization, superficial venous prominence, tissue irregularity, skin texture uniformity, and vascular burden across multiple venous and lipedema phenotypes. Comparative multimodal analysis integrating clinical photography and duplex ultrasound findings enabled structured longitudinal assessment of therapeutic response patterns. Upper-extremity lipedema cases additionally demonstrated measurable contour and tissue-texture improvement following multimodal treatment strategies. The proposed framework illustrated the potential role of AI-assisted longitudinal comparison and multimodal integration in supporting objective treatment-response evaluation within physician-centered vascular care workflows.ConclusionThe LipoVena AI Framework presents a conceptual translational model for future AI-assisted vascular and lipedema medicine by integrating standardized clinical imaging, duplex ultrasound evaluation, multimodal treatment documentation, and longitudinal follow-up analysis within a physician-centered ecosystem. Although prospective multicenter validation and quantitative AI modeling remain necessary, the present framework highlights the potential of explainable and physician-supervised artificial intelligence systems to support personalized, data-driven, and longitudinally optimized vascular care.

title: EXPRESS: Longitudinal Quantitative MRI of Blood-Brain Barrier Leakage in Chronic Cerebral Hypoperfusion Rat model.
abstract: Objective-Methods:Chronic cerebral-hypoperfusion is a key contributor to vascular cognitive impairment, with blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction proposed as an early driver of white matter injury. The temporal-evolution and regional-heterogeneity of BBB-leakage remain poorly characterized in vivo. We longitudinally assessed BBB permeability in Sprague-Dawley rats subjected to bilateral-common carotid artery occlusion (2VO) versus sham controls using contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI 9.4T over 12-weeks. Gadolinium-leakage maps were generated and analyzed in predefined regions (cortex, hippocampus, striatum, corpus callosum). Exploratory histological observations included GFAP immunostaining, and circulating biochemical biomarkers (sTWEAK, MMP-9, GOT, cytokines) were quantified.Results:Localized BBB disruption was observed at weeks 3, 6 post-2VO and progressed heterogeneously, with pronounced leakage strictly targeted toward corpus callosum, hippocampus and striatum. Despite descriptive trends showing increased astroglial activation, systemic biochemical biomarkers did not correlate with imaging-derived central BBB-leakage. Volumetric analysis revealed subtle but significant brain atrophy (18% whole-brain reduction) preceding overt T2-signal abnormalities. In the 2VO model studied, BBB dysfunction in chronic-hypoperfusion appears to be a dynamic, region-specific process.Conclusion:Longitudinal contrast-enhanced MRI detected changes that were not mirrored by the circulating biomarkers studied, suggesting its potential utility as a surrogate endpoint in preclinical studies, which should be confirmed in larger cohorts and complementary models.

title: EXPRESS: Diagnostic and prognostic value of on-site CT-derived fractional flow reserve in intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis.
abstract: Background The role of CT-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) in cerebrovascular disease remains undefined. This study validated the diagnostic and prognostic value of an on-site CT-FFR in symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (sICAS) patients. Methods This retrospective study enrolled sICAS patients with 30 - 99% stenosis confirmed by CTA, divided into two substudies. The diagnostic performance study included 259 patients undergoing CTA and CT perfusion (CTP) or four-dimensional CTA (CTP as reference standard). In prognosis study, 452 patients with at least 1-year follow-up were included. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model was used to measure CT-FFR. Diagnostic performance was assessed by receiver-operating characteristic (ROC) curves, and predictive value by Cox regression analysis. Results The diagnostic performance of CT-FFR was significantly higher than diameter stenosis (DS) on both per-patient (P = 0.009) and per-lesion (P = 0.004) basis. And the cut-off value of CT-FFR diagnosing cerebral hypoperfusion was 0.80. 15.0% (68 / 452) patients experienced recurrent ischemic events during the median 24 (17-33) months follow-up. CT-FFR provided incremental prognostic value beyond traditional cardiovascular risks plus DS (AUC = 0.797 vs 0.716, P < 0.001). Conclusion This on-site CT-FFR can serve as a valuable tool for diagnosis and risk stratification in sICAS patients.

title: EXPRESS: Cerebral blood flow-oxygen metabolism uncoupling at 24 hours after stroke thrombectomy.
abstract: BackgroundFollowing successful endovascular therapy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke, tissue with abnormal perfusion may have impaired oxygen extraction and metabolism. MRI model-based oxygen extraction fraction (OEFmax) and cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen (CMRO2) were characterized in hypoperfusion and hyperemia regions 24 hours post-EVT.MethodsEighty-four patients were included with anterior circulation vessel occlusion, successful recanalization, and an MRI at 24 hours post-EVT. Time-to-maximum (Tmax) and cerebral blood flow (CBF) were evaluated for hypoperfusion and hyperemia. CBF, OEFmax, and CMRO2 were quantified using i) segmentation-based and ii) single slice region of interest (ROI) analyses. Normalized CBF, OEFmax, and CMRO2 were calculated by dividing the segmentation or ROI value by the contralateral value.ResultsSixty-seven (80%) patients had abnormal perfusion; hypoperfusion in 22 (26%), hyperemia in 36 (43%), and both in 9 (11%). Compared to control, hypoperfused regions demonstrated a 62% CBF decrease, 52% CMRO2 decrease, and 68% OEFmax increase (p<0.01). Hyperemic regions demonstrated a 58% CBF increase, 26% CMRO2 increase, and 25% OEFmax decrease (p<0.01). Hyperemia had no significant correlation between normalized CBF and CMRO2 (p=0.14).ConclusionHyperemia regions demonstrated cerebral blood flow-oxygen metabolism uncoupling, suggesting the underlying mechanism as loss of cerebrovascular autoregulation rather than hypermetabolic demand.

title: EXPRESS: Longitudinal FDG-PET reveals early hypermetabolism associated with astrocyte changes in TgF344-AD rats.
abstract: Background Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by alterations in brain glucose metabolism, classically showing [18F]FDG-PET hypometabolism in later stages. However, emerging evidence suggests a transient phase of glucose hypermetabolism early in the disease, for which biological basis remains unclear. Methods We combined longitudinal and cross-sectional approaches in TgF344-AD rats and wild-type controls at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months. Longitudinal assessments included [ 1 8 F]FDG-microPET imaging, behavioral testing, and cerebrospinal fluid biomarker analysis. Cross-sectional analyses included amyloid histopathology, western blot and ex vivo glutamate uptake measurements. Results TgF344-AD rats exhibited increased cerebral glucose metabolism at 9mo, predominantly in cortical regions. This phase coincided with emerging cognitive impairment and early amyloid deposition. CSF analyses showed increased GFAP at 9-12mo and reduced S100B at 9mo, while microglial/inflammatory markers remained unchanged. WB confirmed region-specific GFAP alterations without changes in neuronal or synaptic markers. Glutamate uptake was increased in the cortex and hippocampus at 9mo. Conclusion These findings identify a transient phase of increased glucose metabolism early in disease progression, associated with astrocyte-related changes, suggesting that early hypermetabolism may reflect non-neuronal processes. This has implications for the interpretation of [18F]FDG-PET as a biomarker in early AD and for understanding early physiological responses to AD pathology.

title: Four-dimensional CT angiography-derived dynamic collaterals and perfusion deficits as predictors of stroke recurrence in moderate middle cerebral artery stenosis: A prospective cohort study.
abstract: BackgroundNon-cardioembolic non-disabling minor ischemic stroke carries a considerable risk of early recurrence that is not fully captured by clinical severity scales. Hemodynamic impairment and collateral status may improve risk stratification.PurposeTo assess the prognostic value of four-dimensional computed tomography angiography (4D-CTA)-derived collateral status and CT perfusion parameters for predicting recurrence in patients with minor stroke and moderate middle cerebral artery (MCA) stenosis.Material and MethodsIn this prospective study (July 2024 to June 2025), 183 patients with minor ischemic stroke (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) ≤ 5) and symptomatic moderate (50%-69%) MCA stenosis were enrolled. All underwent multimodal CT imaging and received standardized dual antiplatelet therapy. Collateral status was graded using 4D-CTA (modified American Society of Interventional and Therapeutic Neuroradiology/Society of Interventional Radiology (ASITN/SIR)), and perfusion parameters, including relative cerebral blood flow (rCBF) and Tmax, were quantified. The primary endpoint was recurrent ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack. Cox regression and subgroup analyses were performed.ResultsOver a median follow-up of approximately 10 months, rCBF < 30% volume was the only independent predictor of recurrence (hazard ratio (HR) = 1.168, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.039-1.314; P = 0.010). Poor collateral status showed a non-significant trend overall (HR = 2.079; P = 0.093) but was strongly associated with recurrence in patients without limb weakness (HR = 9.875; P = 0.030).ConclusionMultimodal CT-derived hemodynamic parameters outperform clinical scores in predicting recurrence. rCBF <30% is a robust predictor, while 4D-CTA collateral assessment is particularly valuable in clinically mild patients without motor deficits.

title: Cardiac diagnostic modalities in polycythemia vera: A narrative review.
abstract: Polycythemia vera is a chronic myeloproliferative neoplasm in which erythrocytosis, Janus kinase-signal transducer and activator of transcription activation, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and abnormal blood-cell activation converge to increase cardiovascular risk. This narrative review examines how electrocardiography, echocardiography, coronary angiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, and right-heart catheterization contribute to recognition and characterization of cardiac involvement in polycythemia vera. Reported abnormalities include QT and P-wave changes, atrial arrhythmias, acute coronary syndromes, subclinical biventricular dysfunction, pulmonary hypertension, intracardiac thrombosis, and hypertrophic remodeling. Large observational datasets in myeloproliferative neoplasms also exhibit clinically important burdens of myocardial infarction, heart-failure hospitalization, bleeding, and echocardiographic pulmonary hypertension, although polycythemia vera-specific estimates remain limited. Baseline cardiovascular testing is increasingly relevant before novel therapies and trial enrollment; however, an abnormal test should prompt confirmation, reversible-cause assessment, and protocol-specific review rather than be treated as a universal contraindication. Hematocrit control and low-dose aspirin reduce thrombotic events, while evidence that cytoreductive therapy reverses electrocardiography or imaging abnormalities remains sparse. A symptom- and risk-directed diagnostic approach, integrated with hematology and cardiology assessment, is therefore more defensible than routine universal cardiac screening.

title: Application of bedside ultrasound guidance in difficult diagnostic lumbar puncture in infectious diseases: Technical specifications, clinical evidence, and practical prospects.
abstract: Diagnostic lumbar puncture is a core procedure in the diagnosis and management of infectious diseases. However, in patients with complex anatomical conditions, such as obesity and spinal deformities, the traditional blind puncture method is often challenging to perform, resulting in a substantially higher failure rates and increased complication risks. Bedside ultrasound guidance provides a precise, visual solution to these challenges and represents an emerging tool for improving clinical practice. This narrative review aimed to comprehensively examine the clinical value of ultrasound-guided lumbar puncture in infectious diseases, focusing on the current evidence base, core ultrasound technical principles, standardized pre-puncture assessment procedures, and clinical implementation strategies. Furthermore, it sought to empower infectious disease physicians to utilize safe, efficient, and scalable auxiliary techniques while outlining future directions. Compared with traditional landmark-based methods, ultrasound guidance significantly improves the first-attempt puncture success rate by approximately 20%-30%. Its key technical advantages include real-time visualization of the needle tip, identification of the optimal insertion point, and reduction of procedural complications.

title: Artificial intelligence in hepatitis: Advances in diagnosis, treatment optimization, and prognostic prediction.
abstract: Hepatitis remains a major global health challenge and an important contributor to liver fibrosis, cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and liver-related mortality worldwide. Early diagnosis, effective treatment selection, and accurate prognostic stratification remain critical unmet needs in clinical hepatology. Artificial intelligence, particularly machine learning and deep learning, has emerged as a promising approach to addressing these challenges through the integration and analysis of large-scale, heterogeneous biomedical datasets. This narrative review synthesizes advances in artificial intelligence applications in hepatitis research and clinical practice published over the past decade, organized across three clinical domains: diagnosis, treatment optimization, and prognosis prediction. In the diagnostic domain, artificial intelligence-based approaches have been applied to medical imaging, digital pathology, and multi-omics data to enhance the detection, classification, and staging of liver disease. In the therapeutic domain, machine learning models have been increasingly deployed to support drug discovery, optimize therapeutic regimens, and predict individual treatment responses. In the prognostic domain, artificial intelligence-driven models have shown promising performance in predicting disease progression, survival outcomes, and clinical complications. Nevertheless, key limitations persist, including data heterogeneity, limited external generalizability, and barriers to clinical translation. Future progress will depend on prospective multicenter evaluation, use of interoperable multimodal data, development of transparent models that account for uncertainty, and evidence that artificial intelligence improves clinical decisions and patient outcomes rather than performance metrics alone.

title: Beyond chemobrain: A stepwise approach to identifying cognitive impairment in non-CNS cancer survivors.
abstract: Cancer-related cognitive impairment (CRCI) is common in patients with non-central nervous system malignancies, but its identification remains difficult because symptoms are heterogeneous, may predate treatment, and are not captured by a single measure. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on epidemiology, clinical phenotype, risk factors, neuropsychological assessment, neuroimaging, and practical pathways for identifying CRCI in oncology care. Emerging literature highlights subjective-objective discordance and self-awareness as clinically relevant dimensions. Prevalence varies by timing and method, with higher estimates from self-report than from screening tools or formal batteries. Identification is more reliable when assessment combines patient-reported outcomes (PRO), brief objective screening, and focused neuropsychological testing within baseline vulnerability and concurrent symptom burden. Older age, lower cognitive reserve, pretreatment cognitive impairment, systemic illness, fatigue, insomnia, mood symptoms, pain, and medication effects are major modifiers. In clinical settings, neuroimaging is useful primarily for differential diagnosis: conventional brain MRI excludes competing neurologic disorders, while volumetric MRI, diffusion imaging, resting-state functional MRI, and [18F]FDG-PET currently provide group-level evidence rather than individual diagnostic signatures. At present, CRCI is best identified through a stepwise clinical strategy integrating PRO evaluation, objective testing, risk profiling, and selective imaging, considering individual patient modifiers rather than a single diagnostic test.

title: Prognostic value of CT-measured baseline tumor volume in nivolumab-treated metastatic renal cell carcinoma.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the association between baseline metastatic tumor volume measured on computed tomography (CT) and survival outcomes in patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC) receiving nivolumab as second line or later line therapy. Materials and methods We retrospectively analyzed 43 patients with mRCC treated with nivolumab between August 2013 and March 2022. Baseline metastatic tumor volume was measured on CT scans obtained within 30 days before treatment initiation. The cohort median (117 cm 3 ) was used as an exploratory, data derived cut-off to define low- and high-volume groups. Progression free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. Results Median PFS and OS were 26.97 and 28.11 months, respectively. Median PFS was 40.62 months in the low-volume group and 9.74 months in the high-volume group (p=0.012), while median OS was 46.9 and 12.89 months, respectively (p=0.006). High tumor volume and multiple metastatic sites were associated with poorer survival outcomes. Baseline imbalances in IMDC risk classification and nivolumab treatment line were observed between groups. Conclusion Higher baseline metastatic tumor volume was associated with poorer survival outcomes in patients with mRCC treated with nivolumab. CT-based tumor volumetry may provide complementary prognostic information; however, these exploratory findings require validation in larger, prospective cohorts.

title: A large-scale consensus study of a diagnostic algorithm for canine and feline mammary tumor histopathology: An attempt to improve inter-observer agreement.
abstract: Histological classification of mammary proliferative lesions in dogs and cats is essential for prognostic and predictive studies, as well as for comparative oncology; however, standardization of diagnoses is highly affected by substantial interobserver variability. In this study, a structured diagnostic algorithm based on the Davis-Thompson Foundation classification was assessed for the ability to improve interobserver agreement in the morphological diagnoses of mammary gland lesions in dogs and cats. Consensus diagnoses of 114 selected mammary lesions (91 canine, 23 feline) made by 16 veterinary pathologists with mammary tumor expertise were used as the gold standard, and 79 veterinary pathologists from 21 countries evaluated digitized whole slides in 2 rounds: a first reading without the algorithm and a second reading with the algorithm. Interobserver concordance was measured using unweighted kappa statistics for lesion category (hyperplastic/dysplastic, benign, malignant) and histological subtype. Across all lesions, agreement was higher for lesion category than for histological subtype. A slight improvement in concordance was observed when applying the algorithm, both for category (k = 0.72, before, and k = 0.73, after) and histotype classifications (k = 0.40, before to k = 0.42, after). Also, by using the algorithm, 73/79 raters (92%) modified at least 1 diagnosis and, among these, approximately two-thirds reached agreement with the gold standard in at least 1 case. Considering histotypes, malignant tumors with mixed epithelial and myoepithelial components showed persistently low agreement. Overall, the algorithm provided a reproducible diagnostic framework that may support training and improve standardization of canine and feline mammary tumor classification.

title: Artificial intelligence in veterinary diagnostic histopathology: Concepts, applications, and clinical implementation.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) in human diagnostic histopathology has advanced rapidly, but clinical adoption has lagged behind research. Veterinary diagnostic pathology, being less regulated, could adopt AI faster, but the extent of its integration into diagnostic laboratories is unknown. This article combines a narrative introduction to key concepts, a scoping review of published applications, and an exploratory survey of diagnostic laboratories to provide an overview of AI in veterinary diagnostic histopathology. The narrative review highlights emerging approaches, including vision transformer-based foundation models and self-supervised learning, which may improve generalizability and reduce data requirements, although adaptation to the veterinary context remains challenging. The scoping review identified 34 studies published through a September 5, 2025, literature search, indicating steady but limited growth. Most used convolutional neural networks for relatively low-level tasks such as cell quantification, area measurement, and diagnosis. The survey had a low response rate (2 of 5 laboratories). Both respondents recognized potential benefits of AI. One laboratory had incorporated 2 AI models into routine diagnostic workflows and was evaluating additional applications, while the other had not yet implemented AI but was actively considering several models. Reported barriers included generalizability, latency, and cost. Overall, AI research in veterinary diagnostic histopathology is growing, but clinical adoption remains incompletely characterized. While less restrictive regulation may allow faster uptake than in human medicine, the lack of oversight places responsibility for validation on laboratories and pathologists. For trustworthy implementation, veterinary pathologists must understand AI fundamentals, and the field should prioritize standards for validation, transparency, and reporting.

title: Enhancing the translational potential of the ovine pulmonary adenocarcinoma model.
abstract: Ovine pulmonary adenocarcinoma (OPA) is a transmissible lung cancer of sheep caused by Jaagsiekte sheep retrovirus (JSRV), resulting in substantial animal welfare concerns and economic losses worldwide. We previously developed a bronchoscopic JSRV catheter instillation technique targeting the cardiac lung lobe that reliably reproduced the spectrum of OPA lesions observed in naturally occurring disease. Beyond its value for investigating JSRV pathogenesis, this experimental system provides a large animal platform for studying human lung cancer. Here, we sought to enhance its translational utility by increasing the number of virus inoculation sites and introducing a novel transbronchial intraparenchymal injection technique. Two-month-old lambs received JSRV at 4 lung sites: the left and right cardiac lobes by bronchoscopic catheter instillation and the left and right ventral diaphragmatic lobes by transbronchial intraparenchymal injection. Disease progression was monitored by monthly computed tomography, with postmortem examination and immunohistochemistry confirming OPA in 17/18 (94%) inoculated sheep. Six sheep (35%) developed advanced OPA, generating 22 gross tumors for translational studies. Bronchoscopic catheter instillation produced larger, faster-growing tumors with increased connective tissue, bronchus-associated lymphoid tissue, and intra-airway fluid, whereas intraparenchymal injection generated smaller, localized lesions. Radiomic analysis further demonstrated distinct tumor evolution between the 2 delivery methods. These findings show that both inoculation techniques are safe and effective, while also producing complementary tumor phenotypes. By increasing tumor yield per animal while generating lesions with differing growth characteristics, this refined OPA model provides a more versatile and translationally relevant platform for lung cancer research, while supporting the reduction in animal use.

title: High-Grade Percutaneous Medial Collateral Ligament Pie-Crusting Is Not Associated With Clinically Meaningful Valgus Instability.
abstract: Background Medial collateral ligament (MCL) pie-crusting is used during medial meniscal surgery to improve visualization and reduce the risk of chondral injuries. However, some surgeons extend the release site beyond routine incremental perforation, and the effect of this more extensive release on postoperative medial laxity remains unclear. Purpose To determine whether high-grade percutaneous MCL pie-crusting during medial meniscus posterior root tear (MMPRT) repair results in clinically meaningful valgus instability postoperatively as assessed by valgus stress radiography. Study design Case series; Level of evidence, 4. Methods A retrospective review was performed of patients who underwent isolated MMPRT repair with high-grade MCL pie-crusting and no prior knee ligament surgery. High-grade pie-crusting was defined intraoperatively by an audible and palpable release and a substantial medial compartment opening (≥6 mm) under arthroscopic visualization. Postoperative bilateral valgus stress radiographs were obtained at a mean of 5.9 ± 2.0 months with the knee positioned at 20° of flexion. Gapping was measured in millimeters, and the side-to-side difference was calculated using the contralateral knee as an internal control. An a priori power analysis based on a 3.2-mm threshold for clinically meaningful medial-sided laxity demonstrated a required sample size of 15 patients. The side-to-side difference in medial compartment gapping was analyzed using the 1-sample t test compared with the 3.2-mm threshold. Results A total of 21 patients met inclusion criteria. The mean medial compartment gapping was 7.84 ± 1.65 mm in the operative knee and 6.62 ± 1.37 mm in the contralateral knee. The mean side-to-side difference was 1.21 ± 1.07 mm (95% CI, 0.73-1.70 mm). The observed difference was significantly less than the 3.2-mm threshold associated with clinically meaningful medial-sided instability ( P < .001). Conclusion High-grade percutaneous MCL pie-crusting advanced to a defined intraoperative endpoint during MMPRT repair resulted in small increases in medial compartment gapping that remained below biomechanically defined instability thresholds. These preliminary findings suggest that high-grade MCL pie-crusting improves visualization and instrumentation without being associated with clinically meaningful valgus laxity postoperatively.

title: Iron oxide nanoparticles for hepatocellular carcinoma theranostics: From nanoplatform design to clinical translation.
abstract: The challenges in early diagnosis and effective treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) are largely attributable to the underlying cirrhosis, impaired hepatic reserve, and the added complexity of heterogeneous tumor vascularity in many patients. Iron oxide nanoparticles (IONPs) are promising platforms for HCC diagnosis and treatment because of their magnetic properties, tunable magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) contrast, magnetothermal conversion capability, and modifiable surface chemistry. These features enable IONPs to be used for image-guided diagnosis, liver-directed locoregional therapy, systemic drug delivery, and treatment monitoring. In this review, we summarize the composition, crystal structure, size-dependent magnetic properties, surface modification, and in vivo fate of IONPs, along with how these characteristics influence their performance in HCC imaging and therapy. For diagnostic applications, we focus on passive accumulation, particularly mononuclear phagocyte system (MPS)-mediated hepatic contrast, ligand-mediated active targeting, and multimodal imaging. We then review therapeutic strategies, including magnetic hyperthermia (MHT), stimuli-responsive drug delivery, and combination therapy. Major barriers to clinical translation are also addressed, encompassing the heterogeneous enhanced permeability and retention (EPR) effect, high background uptake by non-tumoral liver tissue, liver function-related safety concerns, limitations of alternating magnetic fields, and manufacturing reproducibility.

title: Combined Application of 3D Reconstruction and ICG Fluorescence Imaging in Pelvic Lymph Node Dissection for Bladder Cancer: A Retrospective Study.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the feasibility and safety of combining preoperative computed tomography (CT)-based three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction with indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence imaging for guiding pelvic lymph node dissection (PLND) in bladder cancer. Methods This retrospective study included 72 patients who underwent radical cystectomy with standard PLND between January 2023 and January 2026: 30 received preoperative CT-based 3D reconstruction plus ICG guidance (3D + ICG), and 42 received ICG guidance alone (ICG-only). Surgical and pathological outcomes were compared. PLND operative time and total lymph node yield were analyzed using multivariable linear and Poisson regression, respectively, with adjustment for calendar time and operating surgeon. A second model additionally adjusted for age, BMI, and pT stage. Recurrence outcomes were reported descriptively. Results No significant differences were observed in baseline characteristics between the two groups. PLND operative time was shorter in the 3D + ICG group than in the ICG-only group (median [interquartile range (IQR)], 45 [42-48] vs 58 [52-64] min; p < 0.001), while total lymph node yield was higher (median [min-max], 17 [6-39] vs 11 [8-20]; p < 0.001). Lymph node yields were also higher in the internal iliac, external iliac, and obturator regions. After adjustment for calendar time and operating surgeon, these differences remained significant (operative time: adjusted β , -13.43 minutes; 95% confidence interval [CI]: -16.54 to -10.33; p < 0.001; total yield: adjusted IRR, 1.43; 95% CI: 1.24-1.65; p < 0.001). The effect estimates remained similar in the second model. Postoperative complication rates and Clavien-Dindo severity distributions did not differ significantly. During a median follow-up of 25 months (IQR: 14-31), recurrence was documented in 2 of 30 patients (6.7%) in the 3D + ICG group and 4 of 42 patients (9.5%) in the ICG-only group. Conclusion The combined use of preoperative CT-based 3D reconstruction and intraoperative ICG fluorescence imaging was associated with shorter PLND operative time and a higher pelvic lymph node yield than ICG guidance alone.

title: GFC-Unet: An optimized 3D U-Net-based method for brain tumor segmentation.
abstract: Accurate brain tumor segmentation is critical for diagnosis and treatment planning. However, U-Net-based models struggle with complex tumor morphologies and fine boundaries. This paper proposes a novel brain tumor segmentation network, termed GFC-Unet. Built upon the 3D U-Net architecture, this network introduces three core modules: (1) the Multi-modal Feature Recalibration (MFR) module; (2) the Gated Feature Convolution (GFC) module; and (3) the Feature Uncertainty Evaluation (FUE) module. Experimental results on the Brain Tumor Segmentation (BraTS) 2020 and 2021 datasets demonstrate that GFC-Unet achieves Dice coefficients of 92.82%, 87.74%, and 87.47% on BraTS2020, and 92.61%, 87.49%, and 86.89% on BraTS2021 for whole tumor (WT), tumor core (TC), and enhancing tumor (ET), respectively. Ablation studies validate the effectiveness of each module. Furthermore, extended experiments on the Data Science Bowl (DSB) 2018 cell nucleus segmentation and International Skin Imaging Collaboration (ISIC) 2018 skin lesion segmentation tasks demonstrate the strong generalization capability. By integrating these modules, GFC-Unet improves segmentation accuracy and boundary delineation, demonstrating promise for supporting clinical decision-making.

title: Photon-counting CT in tumor imaging: A review of comparative evaluations and technical innovations.
abstract: Malignant tumors remain a major global public health challenge, and the limitations of conventional energy-integrating detector computed tomography (EID-CT) in spatial resolution, early lesion detection, and quantitative analysis continue to constrain precise diagnosis and treatment of tumors. Photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT), an emerging CT technology, has shown promising potential in tumor imaging. In this study, the literature on PCCT in oncologic imaging was searched and screened. Existing reviews lack an integrated analysis of comparative evaluation and technological innovation for oncological applications, with insufficient large-sample clinical evidence and discussion of multimodal imaging-AI integration. Regarding these issues, the included literature was classified and analyzed based on comparative evaluation research and technological innovation research. First, the medical background and theoretical basis of PCCT in tumor imaging are introduced. Subsequently, recent relevant studies are reviewed from the perspectives of comparative evaluation and technological innovation. Finally, the current research status and development trends in this field are analyzed and discussed. PCCT achieves high-resolution, low-dose, spectral tumor imaging for lesion detection and tissue characterization. Therefore, PCCT may support precise imaging diagnosis and personalized tumor treatment.

title: Modified FBP and BPF algorithms for stationary computed tomography with linearly distributed sources.
abstract: BackgroundStationary computed tomography with linearly distributed sources (SLCT) improves temporal resolution by avoiding gantry rotation. For the dual-SLCT (DSLCT) configuration, it faces challenges associated with redundancy and truncation issues in projection data. Existing FBP-based methods require complicated weighting strategies, whereas BPF-based methods for truncated data require geometry-specific formulations, which may limit their direct applicability to DSLCT.ObjectiveThis study presents two approaches to overcome the above challenges: a weighted Katsevich-type FBP (WK-FBP) algorithm and a locally refined backprojection filtration (LR-BPF) method.MethodsThe WK-FBP incorporates a Parker-like weighting strategy to handle data redundancy, applying weighting only to conjugate ray pairs during backprojection, thus simplifying the implementation process. The LR-BPF refines the classical BPF by locally adjusting the projection derivative, thereby accommodating linear scanning trajectories while effectively avoiding truncation artifacts. The two methods were evaluated under truncated and non-truncated conditions, with and without noise.ResultsBoth algorithms are applicable to DSLCT scanning. For non-truncated data, the WK-FBP achieves accurate image reconstruction. However, under truncation, WK-FBP reconstructions exhibit noticeable artifacts, whereas the LR-BPF consistently provides accurate results.ConclusionsWK-FBP is effective for DSLCT without truncation, whereas LR-BPF provides robust reconstruction performance under truncation.

title: Bilateral Palatal Root Agenesis of Maxillary Fourth Premolars in 2 Welsh Corgis: A Cone Beam Computed Tomography (CBCT)-Based Case Report.
abstract: Palatal root agenesis of the maxillary fourth premolar (PM4) is a rarely reported developmental anomaly in dogs. This report describes 2 cases of bilateral palatal root agenesis in Welsh Corgis that had complicated crown-root fractures. Initial intraoral radiography suggested absence of the palatal root; however, cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) with 3-dimensional reconstruction provided definitive visualization confirming complete bilateral absence of the palatal roots and associated root canal systems in both patients. Based on these anatomical findings, conventional root canal treatment was performed only on the mesiobuccal and distal roots, which resulted in favorable clinical outcomes during the follow-up period. Furthermore, a 10-year retrospective review of 6683 dental records across 2 referral hospitals identified only 2 cases among 244 Welsh Corgis, which corresponded to record-based frequencies of 0.03% (95% CI, 0.004-0.108%) in the overall canine population and 0.82% (95% CI, 0.099-2.929%) in Welsh Corgis. These findings suggested that palatal root agenesis of the maxillary PM4, although rare, may occur bilaterally and should be carefully considered during diagnosis and treatment planning of fractured carnassial teeth. This study highlighted the utility of CBCT in distinguishing true root agenesis from other anatomical variations. Although both cases occurred in Welsh Corgis, larger studies are required to determine whether any breed-related tendency exists.

title: AMSSE-SwinTrans: A harmonized multimodal hybrid framework with explainable AI for ischemic stroke lesion segmentation.
abstract: BackgroundAccurate ischemic stroke lesion segmentation from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is important but challenging due to variability in lesion morphology. Traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) effectively capture local spatial features but often struggle to capture long-range contextual dependencies needed for irregular lesions. Transformer-based architectures are good at capturing global context; however, they are computationally expensive and difficult to deploy in resource-constrained environments. The black-box nature of deep learning models limits their clinical adoption owing to lack of transparency.ObjectiveThis study introduces AMSSE-SwinTrans, a lightweight hybrid CNN-Transformer framework to make stroke lesion segmentation accurate, efficient and interpretable across different MRI modalities.MethodsThis study proposes AMSSE-SwinTrans, a lightweight hybrid CNN-Transformer framework that combines adaptive multi-scale squeeze-and-excitation (AMSSE) module with simplified transformer blocks employing multi-head self-attention, along with explainable AI (XAI) for clinical interpretation. The model was evaluated on a single-channel harmonized multimodal two-dimensional MRI Slices from ATLAS v2.0 and ISLES 2022 dataset.ResultsThe model achieved an overall Dice of 0.8629, lesion-specific Dice of 0.7535. An ablation study demonstrated a significant performance improvement when each component was added. The model comparisons were all significant with Wilcoxon signed-rank test yielding p-value ( p < 0.001) across all comparisons. With only 27.67 M parameters, 17.67 GFLOPs, and 9.22 ms inference time per slice, the architecture is well-suited for deployment in resource-constrained clinical settings. The interpretability of the model is supported by Attention Rollout and Grad-CAM++ visualizations.ConclusionAMSSE-SwinTrans establishes itself as a resource-efficient and interpretable framework for multimodal stroke lesion segmentation.

title: AI-driven biosensor data fusion for multimodal activity recognition in health monitoring systems.
abstract: BackgroundAI-driven healthcare monitoring systems are increasingly being developed to support elderly individuals through continuous and discreet monitoring of routine behavioral patterns.ObjectiveThis study aims to develop a multimodal framework for identifying mobility patterns by integrating inertial and vision-based sensor data to improve the accuracy and robustness of behavioral recognition.MethodsInertial data are denoised using a median filter, while video feeds are converted into grayscale frame sequences and enhanced using a Gaussian filter. Rectangular windowing is applied to inertial data, whereas U-Net is used for visual segmentation. Features are extracted using Gammatone Filter Cepstrum (GFC), Gaussian Likelihood Threshold Model (GLTM), Power Spectral Density (PSD), and temporal moments from inertial data, and Distance Transform, Gist, ORB, and SURF from visual data. The modalities are fused using shared class labels, followed by fuzzy-logic-based feature optimization and classification using a CNN-GRU hybrid model.ResultsThe proposed multimodal framework achieves 95.20% accuracy on the Continuous Multimodal Human Action Dataset (C-MHAD) and 94.79% on the multi-modal 3D human pose estimation dataset using mmWave, RGB-D, and inertial sensors (mRI) dataset, demonstrating improved behavioral categorization compared with unimodal approaches.ConclusionThe results highlight the potential of multimodal inertial and vision-based sensing for robust AI-assisted healthcare monitoring. However, evaluation is currently limited to public benchmark datasets and requires further validation in clinical settings.

title: RA-BCNet: Residual attention breast cancer network for high-precision breast cancer detection.
abstract: BackgroundBreast cancer remains a major global health concern, and early and accurate detection is critical for improving clinical outcomes. However, variations in lesion characteristics and imaging conditions in Digital Breast Tomosynthesis (DBT) images present substantial challenges for automated breast tumor classification.ObjectiveThis study aims to develop a robust and interpretable deep learning framework, termed RA-BCNet-PReLU, by integrating residual attention mechanisms with Parametric Rectified Linear Unit (PReLU) activation for accurate multi-class breast tumor classification.MethodsThe proposed framework employs a structured processing pipeline comprising Min-Max normalization, stratified sampling, and targeted image augmentation for data preprocessing and generalization. Lesion segmentation is performed using a convolutional neural network (CNN), with segmentation further optimized using the Dynamic Hybrid Grey Wolf-Sunflower Optimization (DHGWSFO) algorithm. Subsequently, handcrafted shape, color, and spatial descriptors are integrated with deep features extracted using ResNet-50 to obtain a comprehensive lesion representation. The fused features are then classified using a residual attention-based CNN with PReLU activation. The model was evaluated on a DBT mammography dataset and externally validated on the CBIS-DDSM dataset. Model reliability was assessed using five-fold cross-validation, ANOVA, paired t -tests, and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, while Grad-CAM was employed to improve model interpretability.ResultsThe proposed RA-BCNet-PReLU achieved a mean classification accuracy of 96.87% ± 0.42 on the DBT dataset and 98.72% ± 0.35 on the CBIS-DDSM dataset, with corresponding AUC values of 0.967 and 0.981, respectively. Statistical analyses demonstrated the reliability of the obtained results, while Grad-CAM visualizations highlighted clinically relevant regions contributing to the model's predictions.ConclusionThe proposed RA-BCNet-PReLU framework demonstrates high classification performance, robustness, and interpretability across DBT and external mammography datasets. Its integration of optimized lesion segmentation, hybrid feature representation, residual attention, and explainable visualization indicates its potential as an effective computer-aided tool for automated breast cancer detection and clinical decision support.

title: Design and fabrication of a lumbar spine simulator for fluoroscopy-guided intervertebral disk puncture.
abstract: Fluoroscopy-guided spinal interventions require anatomically representative and radiographically compatible physical models for procedural simulation. Cadaveric specimens and animal models, while valuable, are limited by cost, availability, ethical considerations, and restricted repeatability. These limitations motivate the development of cost-efficient lumbar spine simulators compatible with C-arm fluoroscopic imaging. Vertebrae and pelvic structures were generated from open-source STL files and fabricated using fused deposition modeling. Post-processing included surface polishing and fabrication of silicone molds to reproduce vertebral geometry. Combinations of two-component polyurethane casting resin, calcium sulfate, barium sulfate, and iohexol were tested to evaluate radiographic visibility and identify a suitable radiopaque formulation. Vertebral elements were assembled using silicone interfaces to form puncturable intervertebral spaces. Soft tissues and skin were imitated using gelatin-glycerin foam and pigmented silicone. Radiographic appearance was assessed under C-arm fluoroscopy. Among the tested formulations, polyurethane composite containing 5 wt% calcium sulfate provided sufficient radiographic visibility while avoiding excessive radiopacity and was selected for the final simulator. The simulator reproduced key lumbar anatomical features and enabled clear visualization of the needle trajectory under fluoroscopy. Design optimization produced a lighter and more compact configuration than the initial prototype. This study presents a reproducible 3D-printed lumbar spine simulator with tunable radiographic properties compatible with fluoroscopic imaging. The proposed design provides a cost-efficient physical model for image-guided procedural simulation and technical development, intended for non-commercial academic and educational use.

title: A multivariate Bayesian biomarker screening algorithm that incorporates clinical covariates.
abstract: Advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has limited treatment options and poor survival. Early detection of HCC improves survival, but current ultrasound screening is inconsistent and poorly adhered to. Biomarker-based blood tests offer a more accurate, accessible, and reliable alternative. Recent developments in methods for early detection of HCC have focused on the trajectories of multiple biomarkers, assuming that biomarkers follow a joint hierarchical mixture model with random changepoints. We extend this model, allowing covariates to influence three aspects of the model: biomarker trajectories, diagnosis times, and subject-specific prior risks. We evaluated whether covariates could capture unexplained heterogeneity in biomarker levels to improve early detection. A Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm was implemented to derive posterior distributions used in risk calculations among future patients and to determine whether a patient has a positive screen. The screening algorithm was evaluated through simulation studies under a range of possible covariate extensions. The Hepatitis C Antiviral Long-term Treatment against Cirrhosis (HALT-C) trial was used to further study the proposed biomarker screening algorithms for HCC using cross-validation.

title: Mammogram utilization among women with vision and/or hearing loss: Insights from the 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance Survey.
abstract: PurposePersons with sensory loss face significant barriers when accessing healthcare services, specifically screening for breast cancer. The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention recommend that women aged 40-74 get screened for breast cancer every 2 years; however, few studies have analyzed whether sensory loss influences the receipt of mammograms. The purpose of this study was to examine the association between sensory (vision, hearing, or dual) loss and mammography utilization among women 40-74 years of age.MethodsThis study used data for women aged 40-74 from the 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance Survey (n = 55,363) to analyze the relationship between self-reported sensory loss and receipt of breast cancer screenings. Weighted complex samples logistic regression analyses were conducted using SPSS Version 29.ResultsWomen aged 40-74 with dual sensory (both vision and hearing) loss were half as likely to have received a mammogram in the past 2 years (adjusted odds ratio (AOR) = .533, 95% confidence interval (CI) = [.354-.803]) in comparison to those with neither disability. Women aged 40-74 with dual sensory (both vision and hearing) loss were twice as likely to have not received a mammogram in the past 5 years or more (AOR = 2.480, 95% CI = [1.317-4.669]) in comparison to those with neither disability.ConclusionWomen aged 40-74 with dual sensory loss were significantly less likely to receive mammograms. Further research focused on understanding and addressing the factors influencing access to breast cancer screenings is needed.

title: Breast cancer overdiagnosis due to mammography screening-A long-term follow-up population study of BreastScreen Norway.
abstract: ObjectivesEstimates of breast cancer overdiagnosis related to mammography screening vary substantially. Overdiagnosis is commonly defined as cases that would not have been detected during the person's remaining lifetime in the absence of screening. We here aim to quantify overdiagnosis in the population-based BreastScreen Norway mammography screening program using long-term follow-up and more detailed modeling than previous studies.SettingWe applied data on Norwegian screening patterns and breast carcinoma incidence for the period 1987-2019, covering women aged 49-84, leveraging the gradual implementation of the organized biennial BreastScreen Norway screening program for women aged 50-69 during 1995-2005.MethodsUsing an extended age-period-cohort model, we estimated excess lifetime risk of invasive breast cancer and ductal carcinoma in situ in the presence of program screening, as an indicator of overdiagnosis among screen-detected cases.ResultsLifetime risk of breast carcinomas was 6.6% (95% confidence interval: 2.5%-10.7%) higher for invited than for non-invited women. This indicates that 18% (95% confidence interval: 7.3%-28.0%) of screen-detected cases may be overdiagnosed, and that approximately one in 86 (95% confidence interval: 54-210) screened women were overdiagnosed during their screening period. Using effect estimates from previous studies, we estimated that approximately three women are overdiagnosed for every breast cancer death prevented by screening, and that 87% of overdiagnosed tumors might grow extremely slowly.ConclusionsOverdiagnosis related to mammography screening is a considerable problem, but its extent may be smaller than reported in some previous studies. Most overdiagnosed tumors likely grow very slowly.

title: Diagnostic Utility of Velopharyngeal MRI in Children With Unexplained Velopharyngeal Insufficiency.
abstract: ObjectiveTo explore the utility of velopharyngeal MRI in contributing additional diagnostic information for patients with velopharyngeal insufficiency (VPI) of unknown etiology.DesignRetrospective cohort study.SettingTertiary children's hospital.ParticipantsChildren with clinically significant VPI without a confirmed etiology.InterventionsStandardized perceptual speech assessment with nasometry, non-sedated MRI, and multidisciplinary review for treatment planning.Main Outcome MeasuresMRI-informed etiologic classification, anatomic and functional contributors to VPI, and management recommendations.ResultsAmong 89 children, six (6.7%) presented with clinically significant VPI of unknown etiology on routine examination. MRI identified occult submucous cleft palate or atypical levator veli palatini morphology in five (83.3%) and adenoid-supported VP closure in three (50%). Involution was expected to unmask increased pharyngeal depth in two (33.3%). MRI supported patient-specific recommendations for speech therapy, surgical interventions, and longitudinal monitoring.ConclusionsMRI provided clinically meaningful diagnostic information beyond routine examination and informed management decisions for children with VPI.

title: Lung Localization of Endosalpingiosis: Challenges of Rare Manifestation of Müllerianosis.
abstract: Endosalpingiosis (ES) is a benign, nonneoplastic condition of the Müllerian system characterized by the ectopic implantation of fallopian tube-like ciliated columnar epithelium. Unlike endometriosis, ES lacks endometrial stroma and therefore does not produce the characteristic hemorrhagic episodes or extensive inflammatory responses associated with endometriosis. Although ES is primarily identified in the visceral pelvic peritoneum, extrapelvic manifestations are exceedingly rare, with pulmonary and pleural localization, accounting for ∼0.1% of reports. This report describes the clinical presentation of thoracic ES in a 40-year-old woman who presented with catamenial spontaneous primary pneumothorax. Despite a remote surgical history for ovarian endometriosis 10 years earlier, the patient had a prolonged period of clinical latency and no evidence of current pelvic recurrence. Videothoracoscopic surgery revealed a 5-mm apical pulmonary nodule and diffusely calcified pleural plaques. Histopathology and immunohistochemistry are remain gold-standard diagnostic methods for differentiating ES from thoracic endometriosis syndrome or malignancy. The diagnosis was confirmed by epithelial immunoreactivity for Müllerian transcription factors (PAX8 and WT1), keratin 7, and estrogen/progesterone receptors, together with the absence of cluster of differentiation 10 expression, which argued against endometrial stroma, and calretinin negativity, which argued against mesothelial origin. The pathophysiology of thoracic ES may resemble that of pulmonary endometriosis, involving transdiaphragmatic or vascular migration of Müllerian cells. For symptomatic presentations, surgical excision combined with long-term suppressive hormonal therapy is recommended to reduce epithelial proliferation. Given that the emerging literature suggests a possible link between ES and gynecological malignancies, rigorous long-term postoperative surveillance remains essential.

title: Aberrant Desmin Expression in a Middle Ear Neuroendocrine Tumor: Expanding the Immunophenotypic Spectrum.
abstract: Middle ear neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) are uncommon neoplasms that exhibit both epithelial and neuroendocrine differentiation. Aberrant desmin expression in middle ear NET has not been documented previously and may create a diagnostic pitfall due to morphologic overlap with myogenic and rhabdoid tumors. A 52-year-old man presented with right ear pain, fullness, and facial deviation. Imaging revealed a soft-tissue mass involving the middle ear cavity and the mastoid air cells, with ossicular erosion. Histopathology showed an infiltrative neoplasm arranged in nests, trabeculae, cords, and pseudoacini composed of monomorphic cells with plasmacytoid/rhabdoid morphology. Immunohistochemically, the tumor cells showed diffuse positivity for KRT, synaptophysin, chromogranin, and diffuse strong desmin expression, while myogenin, MYOD1, p63, calponin, TTF1, CDX2, and GATA3 were negative. SMARCB1/INI1 expression was retained, and the Ki67 index was <2%. A diagnosis of middle ear NET with aberrant desmin positivity was rendered. The patient remained disease-free 18 months following surgical excision. The index patient expands the immunophenotypic spectrum of middle ear NET by documenting diffuse aberrant desmin expression. Awareness of this unusual finding is important to avoid misdiagnosis as rhabdomyosarcoma or other rhabdoid neoplasms. Accurate diagnosis requires careful integration of morphologic and immunohistochemical features, and long-term follow-up remains essential despite the generally indolent behavior of middle ear NETs.

title: IDH-Mutant Astrocytomas in Patients Older than 55 Years: A Retrospective Analysis.
abstract: Diffuse gliomas are the most common malignant brain tumors in adults, stratified by isocitrate dehydrogenase ( IDH1/IDH2 ) mutation status. While the median age for central nervous system (CNS) World Health Organization (WHO) grade 2 to 3 IDH-mutant astrocytomas is 38 years, older patients of >55 years predominantly exhibit IDH-wildtype gliomas and confer a poorer prognosis. To examine the clinicopathologic spectrum of IDH-mutant astrocytomas in older adults, we retrospectively reviewed all astrocytic tumors diagnosed at our institution between 2021 and 2024 in patients >55 years. Twenty-two IDH-mutant astrocytomas (median age: 63 years; range: 56-79; male:female = 9:13) were identified and compared descriptively to a historical cohort of 179 IDH-mutant astrocytomas in younger patients. Grade distribution among older patients paralleled that of younger adults: CNS WHO grade 2 (55%), grade 3 (18%), and grade 4 (27%). Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed T2/FLAIR mismatch sign in 25% of grade 2 tumors and in none of the higher grades; 50% of grade 2 tumors demonstrated contrast enhancement. IDH1 p.R132H accounted for 95% of mutations, with 1 p.R132G variant. ATRX loss was seen in 71% and strong p53 immunoreactivity in 83% of evaluable tumors. Copy-number analysis ( n = 10) revealed CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion in 10% and heterozygous loss in 20% . Despite their rarity, IDH-mutant astrocytomas in older adults are more prevalent than historically appreciated and maintain imaging and molecular profiles akin to tumors in younger adults. Accordingly, IDH1 p.R132H-specific immunohistochemistry remains a cost-effective first-line screening tool irrespective of age.

title: Operative Treatment of Quadrimalleolar and Quadrimalleolar-Equivalent Ankle Fractures: Radiographic and Clinical Outcomes Following Component-Based Operative Fixation.
abstract: Background Quadrimalleolar (QM) and quadrimalleolar-equivalent (QME) fractures expand the trimalleolar concept by adding an anterior osseous syndesmotic component (Chaput or Wagstaffe fragment). Outcomes after operative fixation remain incompletely defined. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 36 consecutive patients (18 QM, 18 QME) who underwent open reduction and internal fixation between April 2019 and December 2024, with a minimum 12-month follow-up. All patients underwent a component-based operative treatment strategy comprising preoperative computed tomographic (CT) characterization of each malleolar and syndesmotic component, morphology-based management of anterior fragments, and intraoperative arthroscopic assessment of residual instability. Syndesmotic reduction was assessed on bilateral CT 1 cm proximal to the plafond using direct anterior and posterior differences, fibular translation, and fibular rotation, referenced to the contralateral ankle. Clinical outcomes included Olerud-Molander Ankle Score (OMAS) and visual analog scale (VAS). Results Baseline demographics did not differ significantly between groups. QME injuries were predominantly SER (supination-external rotation) type IV/Weber B (94.4%), whereas QM showed an even distribution between SER and PER (pronation-external rotation) and between Weber B and C ( P = .01). No significant side-to-side differences were observed in any of the 4 parameters in either group at 1 year (all P > .05); given the limited sample size, these nonsignificant findings may be subject to a type II error. Intra- and interobserver reliabilities were excellent (intraclass correlation coefficient 0.901-0.988). Mean OMAS improved to 86.1 ± 6.8 (QM) and 85.3 ± 5.7 (QME); VAS decreased to 1.0 ± 0.7 in both (within-group P < .001; between-group P = .82). All fractures united; 3 minor wound complications resolved with local care. Conclusion A component-based operative treatment strategy was safe and associated with maintained anatomic distal tibiofibular alignment and favorable short-term outcomes in both QM and QME. The absence of a control group precludes conclusions on clinical necessity or superiority, and combined evaluation of these biomechanically distinct patterns should be interpreted with caution. Level of evidence Level IV, retrospective comparative case series.

title: Accuracy of Computer-Assisted Navigation in Total Ankle Arthroplasty Surgery Using Computed Tomography: A Short Report.
abstract: Background Computer-assisted navigation (CAN) offers dynamic intraoperative guidance in total ankle arthroplasty (TAA). Although laboratory data suggest superior precision, in vivo evidence is lacking. This study used weightbearing computed tomography (WBCT) to evaluate CAN accuracy of postoperative TAA implant position relative to the plan. We hypothesized that absolute discrepancies would be <3 mm or <3°. Methods Thirteen consecutive patients (November 2024-November 2025) underwent TAA using CAN. Preoperative computed tomography-based 3D models were used for templating. Postoperative WBCT scans were used to measure final implant seating, and computerized measurements were used to identify implant placement discrepancy. We analyzed absolute discrepancies between planned vs final postoperative positions. Results Tibial absolute discrepancies were within desired limits for varus/valgus (1.65° ± 1.43°), slope (1.87° ± 1.34°), and cut height (0.68 ± 0.62 mm) but not for axial rotation (3.97 ± 2.64). For the talus, varus/valgus (2.93° ± 1.86°) and cut height (0.66 ± 0.71 mm) absolute discrepancies were within desired limits. The increased talar slope deviation (3.90 ± 2.89) in the final position may be due to non-navigated implant impaction. Conclusion Although discrepancies persisted in tibial rotational alignment and talar positioning, the low variability across measurements suggests that CAN may support accurate implant positioning. These short-term positioning accuracy findings support the utility of CAN as a potential tool for enhancing implant positioning reproducibility in TAA. Level of evidence Level IV, case series.
originalAbstract:
Background

Computer-assisted navigation (CAN) offers dynamic intraoperative guidance in total ankle arthroplasty (TAA). Although laboratory data suggest superior precision, in vivo evidence is lacking. This study used weightbearing computed tomography (WBCT) to evaluate CAN accuracy of postoperative TAA implant position relative to the plan. We hypothesized that absolute discrepancies would be <3 mm or <3°.

Methods

Thirteen consecutive patients (November 2024-November 2025) underwent TAA using CAN. Preoperative computed tomography-based 3D models were used for templating. Postoperative WBCT scans were used to measure final implant seating, and computerized measurements were used to identify implant placement discrepancy. We analyzed absolute discrepancies between planned vs final postoperative positions.

Results

Tibial absolute discrepancies were within desired limits for varus/valgus (1.65° ± 1.43°), slope (1.87° ± 1.34°), and cut height (0.68 ± 0.62 mm) but not for axial rotation (3.97 ± 2.64). For the talus, varus/valgus (2.93° ± 1.86°) and cut height (0.66 ± 0.71 mm) absolute discrepancies were within desired limits. The increased talar slope deviation (3.90 ± 2.89) in the final position may be due to non-navigated implant impaction.

Conclusion

Although discrepancies persisted in tibial rotational alignment and talar positioning, the low variability across measurements suggests that CAN may support accurate implant positioning. These short-term positioning accuracy findings support the utility of CAN as a potential tool for enhancing implant positioning reproducibility in TAA.

Level of evidence

Level IV, case series.

title: Silent Hypoxemia in High-Altitude Pulmonary Edema: A Case Report.
abstract: We report a case of a trekker who ascended to Tilicho Lake (4919 m) from Kathmandu (1400 m) in 3 days. On day 3, he descended to Shree Kharka (4045 m). The following day, he trekked to Yak Kharka (4025 m) where, although he had no symptoms, he measured his own oxygen saturation (SpO 2 ) at 72% in ambient air. Overnight, his SpO 2 ranged from 75-80% on oxygen 2L/min via nasal cannula. The next day his SpO 2 dropped to 47% while still on oxygen. He descended on horseback to Manang (3500 m), where his SpO 2 was 70% on room air. He was diagnosed with high-altitude pulmonary edema (HAPE). He was treated with oxygen, 4L by nasal cannula, and nifedipine. The following day, he flew to Kathmandu, where he made a full recovery. Trekkers may develop life-threatening HAPE without obvious symptoms or signs. Slow ascent can decrease the likelihood of developing HAPE, but trekkers do not always follow the recommended ascent rate. Early detection, by history and physical examination and with point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS), if available, is critical in resource-limited regions such as ours. The keys to managing HAPE are early recognition and management, including descending to a lower altitude as soon as possible.

title: Limb Body Wall Complex: Report of a Discordant Case in a Monozygotic Twin Pregnancy.
abstract: Limb Body Wall Complex (LBWC) is a rare, severe congenital malformation syndrome characterized by thoracoabdominal wall defects, craniofacial anomalies, and limb and spinal malformations. Its incidence ranges from 0.04 to 3.3 per 10,000 births. We present a case of LBWC diagnosed in a monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy at 17 weeks of gestation. The mother was 28-year-old, primigravida, and had no notable medical history. Ultrasound identified abnormal positioning of 1 embryo, suggestive of adherence to the amnion. First-trimester scans revealed increased nuchal translucency and foot malposition in fetus A, while fetus B showed a cystic hygroma along with significant abdominal wall and spinal anomalies. Selective termination of fetus B was performed at 17 weeks but was complicated by the intrauterine demise of both fetuses. Postmortem examination of fetus B confirmed classical LBWC features: abdominopelvic wall defect with evisceration adherent to the placenta, lower limb amyotrophy, severe kyphoscoliosis, and craniofacial abnormalities. The pathogenesis of LBWC remains unclear, with hypotheses including early amnion rupture, vascular disruptions, and embryonic developmental errors. Diagnosis is typically made by prenatal ultrasound in the first trimester. LBWC is generally lethal, warranting pregnancy termination. While multiple pregnancies may increase the risk, discordant presentation in monochorionic twins remains exceptionally rare.
