title: Decoding Treatment Response and Prognosis in Unresectable Locally Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer by Integrating Spatiotemporal Heterogeneity From 18 F-FDG Positron Emission Tomography-Computed Tomography: A Multicenter Study.
abstract: Purpose Treatment response in unresectable locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (LA-NSCLC) is highly variable due to marked intratumoral heterogeneity, while existing predictive biomarkers lack accuracy. We aimed to develop and validate a pretreatment 18 F-FDG positron emission tomography (PET)-computed tomography (CT)-derived spatiotemporal heterogeneity model to predict treatment response and prognosis in unresectable LA-NSCLC, and to explore its biological underpinnings. Materials and methods In a multicenter cohort of 434 patients with unresectable LA-NSCLC (training: n = 215; internal validation: n = 93; external validation: n = 126), treatment response was classified as responsive or nonresponsive based on initial assessment. Four distinct habitats (PEThigh-CThigh, PETlow-CTlow, PETlow-CThigh, and PEThigh-CTlow) were generated via the Otsu algorithm. Temporal heterogeneity was quantified using metabolic hotspot displacement (normalized distance from the hotspot to the tumor centroid and normalized distance from the hotspot to the tumor periphery) and integrated with spatial radiomics to build a multidimensional spatiotemporal model. Model performance was evaluated against conventional metrics, with interpretability enhanced via nomogram and SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis. Survival outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier curves, and public transcriptomic data were analyzed to characterize underlying pathways. Results The spatiotemporal model accurately predicted treatment response with AUCs of 0.822 (training), 0.821 (internal validation), and 0.810 (external validation), significantly outperforming conventional whole-tumor PET-CT models. It maintained robust generalizability across treatment subgroups and effectively stratified patients by progression-free survival and overall survival ( P < .01). PEThigh-CThigh habitat volume fraction correlated with treatment resistance, whereas PETlow-CTlow habitat correlated with better response. Exploratory pathway analysis highlighted key pathways involving drug metabolism, glycolytic reprogramming, and immune microenvironment remodeling. Conclusion This study establishes a noninvasive spatiotemporal heterogeneity biomarker based on 18 F-FDG PET-CT that reliably predicts treatment response and prognostic outcomes in unresectable LA-NSCLC. It offers valuable insights for personalized clinical decision making and supports precision oncology.

title: Concurrent thyroid and abdominal diffuse large B-cell lymphoma arising in the milieu of chronic fibrosing thyroiditis.
abstract: Firm tender thyroid masses present a diagnostic challenge, with differentials including benign fibroinflammatory conditions and neoplastic processes. Imaging modalities cannot reliably distinguish between these differentials. The sampling-dependent nature of both cytopathology and core-biopsy histopathology introduces the potential for indeterminate or misleading results. Surgical biopsy can have high complication rates depending on the underlying condition. Here we report the case of a patient with chronic autoimmune thyroid disease who initially presented with fibroinflammatory thyroid disease and was subsequently diagnosed with B-cell lymphoma. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges associated with these conditions, the limitations of the sampling-dependent tissue assessment and the importance of re-evaluating the diagnosis when the clinical course is discordant with the initial biopsy findings.

title: Coexisting adrenal hemangioma and aldosterone-producing micronodule presented as adrenal incidentaloma.
abstract: Adrenal hemangiomas are rare benign vascular tumors, an uncommon cause of adrenal incidentalomas. We report a patient with coexisting adrenal hemangioma and aldosterone-producing micronodules within the same adrenal gland. A 67-year-old man was referred for an incidental left adrenal mass. Noncontrast computed tomography revealed a 1.6 × 1.4 cm lesion with an unenhanced attenuation value of 40 Hounsfield units. Initial hormonal evaluation was unremarkable except for an elevated aldosterone-to-renin ratio (ARR) of 115.6. On follow-up evaluation, the ARR decreased to 52.8, with a relatively low aldosterone concentration of 9.5 ng/dL (264 pmol/L; reference range, 2.52-39.2 ng/dL [69-1087 pmol/L]), yielding equivocal findings for primary aldosteronism. Serial imaging revealed growth to 3.4 × 2.8 cm over 3 years. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed a T2-hyperintense lesion with peripheral nodular enhancement and delayed centripetal filling, suggestive of adrenal hemangioma. Owing to continued growth, laparoscopic adrenalectomy was performed. Histopathological examination confirmed cavernous hemangioma. Given the marked postoperative reduction in ARR to 9.7, additional pathological review identified an adjacent CYP11B2-positive aldosterone-producing micronodule. This report illustrates that adrenal incidentalomas may have dual pathologies. An integrated assessment of imaging, biochemical findings, clinical course, and histopathology, together with close clinicopathological collaboration, is essential for accurate diagnosis and management.

title: Long-term cyclic ectopic adrenocorticotropic hormone syndrome with extreme fluctuations and adrenal insufficiency.
abstract: A 77-year-old woman presented with worsening glycemic control and hypokalemia and was found to have adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)-dependent hypercortisolism with loss of diurnal cortisol variation and failure of suppression on low- and high-dose dexamethasone suppression tests. Computed tomography (CT) demonstrated bilateral adrenal enlargement, whereas pituitary magnetic resonance imaging and chest CT failed to identify a source of ACTH secretion, leading to a diagnosis of occult ectopic ACTH syndrome. During 15 years of follow-up, she exhibited cyclic fluctuations in ACTH and cortisol concentrations, including episodes of severe hypercortisolism with ACTH levels exceeding 2000 pg/mL (>440 pmol/L) (reference range, 7.2-63.6 pg/mL [1.6-14.0 pmol/L]) and cortisol concentrations of 30-60 μg/dL (828-1656 nmol/L) (reference range, 6.2-19.4 μg/dL [171-535 nmol/L]), alternating with spontaneous remission. Serial imaging revealed dynamic adrenal morphological changes, with enlargement during hypercortisolemic phases and regression during remission. During treatment with ketoconazole, mitotane, and osilodrostat, the patient experienced recurrent significant hypocortisolic episodes, some of which were likely treatment-associated and required hydrocortisone replacement therapy. This case highlights an exceptionally prolonged course of cyclic ectopic ACTH syndrome characterized by extreme hormonal oscillation, reversible adrenal hyperplasia, and recurrent hypocortisolism, emphasizing the importance of long-term biochemical surveillance and individualized therapeutic adjustment.

title: When anorexia nervosa conceals Cushing syndrome: a diagnostic pitfall in hypercortisolemia.
abstract: A 37-year-old woman presented with severe hypertension, mood changes, and weight loss (body mass index 14.6 kg/m 2 ). She exhibited restrictive eating behaviors consistent with anorexia nervosa, alongside biochemical hypercortisolemia with serum cortisol 43.6 µg/dL (1204 nmol/L; reference range: 6.2-18.1 µg/dL; 170-500 nmol/L), 24-hour urinary free cortisol 430.3 µg/24 hours (1187 nmol/24 hours; reference range: <60.2 µg/24 hours; <166 nmol/24 hours), and unsuppressed adrenocorticotropic hormone of 19.1 pg/mL (4.2 pmol/L; reference range: 7.3-63.1 pg/mL; 1.6-13.9 pmol/L). The cortisol level after the 1 mg dexamethasone suppression test was 23.9 µg/dL (659 nmol/L; reference range: <1.8 µg/dL; <50 nmol/L). Cortisol remained markedly elevated after nasogastric feeding and weight restoration. Pituitary magnetic resonance imaging revealed a 4 mm left anterior pituitary lesion. High-dose dexamethasone suppression, corticotropin-releasing hormone stimulation, and inferior petrosal sinus sampling confirmed a pituitary source of adrenocorticotropic hormone. The patient underwent transsphenoidal resection of a corticotroph adenoma. Eleven months later, her hypertension and restrictive eating behaviors had resolved, and her mood significantly improved. Cushing syndrome can coexist with anorexia nervosa, masking typical cushingoid features and presenting with psychiatric manifestations and weight loss. Persistent hypercortisolemia despite nutritional rehabilitation should prompt dynamic endocrine testing and pituitary evaluation to ensure timely diagnosis and treatment.

title: Calcimimetic therapy modified the radiological, surgical, and histopathological features of a parathyroid adenoma.
abstract: Calcimimetics are increasingly used to control hypercalcemia before parathyroidectomy. Although treatment-induced degenerative changes have been reported in parathyroid adenomas, their effects on preoperative imaging and surgical planning remain unclear. A 70-year-old woman with primary hyperparathyroidism was administered preoperative evocalcet (2 mg/day). After ∼2 months, serum calcium levels decreased to the hypocalcemic range, prompting drug discontinuation before surgery referral. Upon presentation, corrected serum calcium normalized to 9.1 mg/dL (SI: 2.28 mmol/L; reference range, 8.8-10.1 mg/dL [SI: 2.20-2.53 mmol/L]), whereas intact parathyroid hormone remained mildly elevated at 65.7 pg/mL (SI: 7.0 pmol/L; reference range, 10-65 pg/mL [SI: 1.1-6.9 pmol/L]). Ultrasonography revealed a right superior parathyroid lesion, with markedly decreased Doppler flow. Four-dimensional computed tomography revealed weak enhancement throughout the contrast-enhanced phase. Parathyroidectomy revealed marked fibrosis and dense adhesions around the recurrent laryngeal nerve, making dissection technically demanding, although the nerve was preserved. Histopathological examination confirmed parathyroid adenoma with extensive fibrosis, cystic degeneration, necrosis, and macrophage infiltration. Therefore, calcimimetic therapy may modify the radiological and histopathological characteristics of parathyroid adenomas and intraoperative findings relevant to surgical planning. Recognition of these treatment-induced changes may improve the interpretation of preoperative images, help surgeons anticipate dense adhesions, and facilitate meticulous surgical dissection.

title: Primary adrenal small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma in a patient with sarcoidosis and synchronous colon adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Primary adrenal neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC), particularly the small cell subtype, is exceptionally rare. In patients with sarcoidosis, inflammatory lymphadenopathy may mimic a metastatic disease, making disease detection difficult. A 76-year-old man with sarcoidosis was referred for an enlarging left adrenal incidentaloma that had increased in size from 7 mm to 19 × 14 mm over 3 years. Hormonal evaluation revealed unremarkable findings; laparoscopic adrenalectomy was performed because malignancy could not be excluded. Histopathological examination revealed small cell NEC with positive synaptophysin and chromogranin A staining, and a Ki-67 labeling index of 80%. One month after surgery, para-aortic lymphadenopathy was detected. Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (CT) showed uptake in the para-aortic lymph nodes and ascending colon, where colonoscopy identified synchronous adenocarcinoma. The cause of the lymphadenopathy was uncertain because of coexisting sarcoidosis and colon cancer. Cisplatin plus irinotecan induced a partial response; however, disease progression was observed. CT-guided lymph node biopsy confirmed metastatic NEC. Second-line amrubicin therapy reduced tumor size; comprehensive genomic profiling revealed a tumor mutation-burden-high phenotype. This case highlights diagnostic challenges in the evaluation of lymphadenopathy in patients with sarcoidosis and synchronous malignancy, emphasizing the importance of pathological confirmation for guiding appropriate management.

title: Diagnostic challenges of masked arginine vasopressin deficiency in neurosarcoidosis complicated by sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor use.
abstract: A wide variety of endocrine disorders caused by sarcoidosis have been reported to date. We report the case of an 82-year-old male patient who presented with hypercalcemia and anterior pituitary hormone deficiency at the time of his sarcoidosis diagnosis and was subsequently diagnosed with arginine vasopressin deficiency (AVP-D) 6 months after the initiation of glucocorticoid therapy. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed an enlarged pituitary gland, thickened pituitary stalk, and loss of the posterior pituitary bright spot, raising the suspicion of hypothalamic-pituitary sarcoidosis. Despite improvement in hypercalcemia, anterior pituitary function, and pituitary enlargement and stalk thickening with glucocorticoid therapy, subjective symptoms of dry mouth and polyuria gradually became apparent several months after the start of treatment. While the characteristic hypotonic polyuria of AVP-D was not prominent, we surmised that these typical clinical features were masked by adrenal insufficiency, chronic kidney disease (CKD), and concurrent use of a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor for type 2 diabetes. This case highlights the fact that the typical presentation of AVP-D can be masked by concurrent SGLT2 inhibitor use and CKD, emphasizing careful assessment of water balance in such patients.

title: Late-onset hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction in a childhood cancer survivor treated with cranial irradiation.
abstract: Hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction is a well-recognized late complication in childhood cancer survivors (CCSs) treated with cranial irradiation. We report a 42-year-old male with a history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia diagnosed at 5 years of age and treated with chemotherapy and 26 Gray whole-brain irradiation. He presented with right upper extremity paresis due to bilateral chronic subdural hematomas. Following burr-hole drainage for the left chronic subdural hematoma, he developed anorexia, fatigue, and hyponatremia and was referred to the endocrinology department. Endocrine evaluation demonstrated hypothalamic adrenal insufficiency, severe adult growth hormone deficiency, mild gonadal dysfunction, and mixed hypothyroidism. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed a suprasellar arachnoid cyst with compression of the pituitary gland. To our knowledge, this represents one of the longest reported intervals between childhood cancer treatment and the diagnosis of hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction, which became clinically apparent 37 years after treatment following a prolonged asymptomatic period. This case suggests that hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction may remain clinically silent and gradually progress for decades before becoming unmasked by the physiological stress, highlighting the need for prolonged, potentially lifelong, endocrine surveillance in CCS.

title: The relationship between cardiometabolic disease and vertebral bone strength, mineral density, and mass in US adults.
abstract: Context Cardiometabolic disease (CMD) may increase vertebral fracture risk through deterioration in bone structure and/or tissue properties, compromising bone strength. Objective Evaluate the relationship between CMD and vertebral bone measures. Design Cross-sectional. Participants Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) study participants with year 25 (2010-2011) abdominal computed tomography (CT) scans (n = 2728). Exposure CMD (abdominal obesity, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, or hypertension) status (≥1 vs 0) and burden (0, 1, 2, ≥3). Outcome measures Vertebral strength, volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD), and bone mass, obtained via biomechanical CT analysis. Methods Multivariable linear regression evaluated the association between CMD and vertebral bone measures. Sex-specific models were adjusted for age, race, height, weight, and additional social determinants of health, lifestyle factors, and comorbidities. Effect modification by race, age, and menopausal status was evaluated. Results Overall, at least 1 CMD was identified in 72.3% of men and 70.5% of women. In the fully adjusted model, CMD status was significantly associated with lower total (β = -6.32 mg/cm 3 ; P = .018), trabecular (β = -4.53 mg/cm 3 ; P = .048), and cortical (β = -6.63 mg/cm 3 ; P = .034) vBMD in men. Greater CMD burden was associated with lower total and trabecular vBMD. The negative association between CMD and vBMD was stronger in men ≤50 years. There was no association in women. Conclusion In this biracial cohort of Black and White adults from the United States, CMD was associated with significantly lower total and subcompartment vertebral vBMD in men.

title: Inflammatory and Autoimmune Axonal Neuropathies.
abstract: Objective This article outlines the clinical patterns, diagnostic strategies, and treatment principles for patients with inflammatory and autoimmune axonal neuropathies. Latest developments Recent studies highlight the role of serum neurofilament light chain as a biomarker of the rate of active axonal injury and the increasing use of rituximab over cyclophosphamide for induction in neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis. Imaging modalities, such as magnetic resonance neurography and fludeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET), aid in identifying biopsy targets and monitoring disease activity. Essential points Inflammatory axonal neuropathies encompass a spectrum of immune-mediated disorders presenting with mononeuritis multiplex, asymmetric sensorimotor polyneuropathy, sensory ataxia, or plexopathy. The diagnosis requires a high degree of clinical suspicion, detailed electrodiagnostic evaluation, and consideration of systemic features. Nerve biopsy, although limited by patchy yield, can confirm the diagnosis and guide immunotherapy decisions. Treatment focuses on halting inflammation and preventing relapses, with corticosteroids as first-line induction and steroid-sparing agents for maintenance. A structured follow-up approach, including standardized neurologic examinations, functional assessments, and ancillary testing, is essential for tracking disease progression and treatment response.

title: Video Head Impulse Testing for Acute Dizziness in Stroke Protocols: A Prospective Pilot Study.
abstract: Background and objectives Dizziness is a common emergency department (ED) concern, yet posterior-circulation strokes can be difficult to detect with standard clinical tools and neuroimaging alone. Quantitative video head impulse test (vHIT) provides an objective bedside measure of vestibulo-ocular reflex function and can help differentiate central from peripheral causes of acute dizziness. Methods We conducted a prospective, single-center feasibility and diagnostic-accuracy study of adults (18-90 years) presenting on an ED stroke pathway for acute dizziness. vHIT was performed within 48 hours of presentation, after completion of standard stroke evaluation. Two vestibular-trained clinicians, blinded to clinical and imaging data, classified vHIT as peripheral, central, equivocal, or poor quality. The reference standard (stroke vs nonstroke) was the final diagnosis adjudicated by stroke neurologists using all clinical information, noncontrast CT, and MRI when available. Diagnostic metrics for stroke were calculated for interpretable vHIT studies and in an intention-to-diagnose analysis. Results Thirty patients underwent vHIT; 11 (36.7%) had acute ischemic stroke and 19 (63.3%) had nonstroke diagnoses. Interpretable vHIT results (central or peripheral pattern) were obtained in 23 of 30 patients (76.7%). Overall, vHIT patterns were central in 19 (63.3%), peripheral in 4 (13.3%), equivocal in 3 (10.0%), and poor quality in 4 (13.3%). Among strokes, 9 of 11 (81.8%) had a central pattern and none had a peripheral pattern. In the primary analysis of interpretable studies, vHIT sensitivity and negative predictive value for stroke were both 100%, while specificity was 28.6% and overall accuracy was 56.5%. In the intention-to-diagnose analysis including all patients, sensitivity and negative predictive value remained 100%, with specificity at 21.1% and accuracy at 50.0%. Discussion Our findings suggest that vHIT was feasible in most ED stroke-pathway patients with acute dizziness and demonstrated high sensitivity and negative predictive value when a clearly peripheral pattern was present, supporting its potential role as an adjunctive rule-out tool. However, specificity was low, and nearly one-quarter of studies were equivocal or poor quality, limiting its use as a standalone diagnostic test. With further validation and larger studies, vHIT may help support more targeted use of hospital admissions, diagnostic workups, and ED stroke resources in patients without evidence of central pathology.

title: A Multidisciplinary Neuro-Lupus Program for the Evaluation and Management of Patients With SLE and Cognitive Concerns.
abstract: To develop and implement a standardized, comprehensive multidisciplinary program for the evaluation and management of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and cognitive concerns that would lead to improved diagnosis and management. The Neuro-Lupus Program evaluated 50 patients with SLE referred for any neurocognitive concern over a 12-month period. A specific sequential work-up protocol was developed for standardized patient evaluation. Initial history and examination were performed by a dedicated lupus neurologist followed by referral for comprehensive neurocognitive testing. Patients with suspected mood or psychotic disorders were evaluated in a specialized autoimmune psychiatry clinic. MRI brain scans were performed in all patients. Patients with MRI evidence of inflammation or cognitive impairment were further assessed with CSF studies and FDG-PET/CT brain. Management of neuropsychiatric medications and immunotherapy was a collaboration between neurology, psychiatry, and rheumatology. Full neurocognitive evaluation revealed a previously undiagnosed cognitive impairment in 46.4% of patients tested (mild 39.3%, major 7.1%), with an additional 39.3% demonstrating a normal cognitive profile with isolated weakness. MRI demonstrated white matter disease in 50% of patients and cerebral atrophy in 10%. Brain FDG-PET/CT was performed in 8 patients (16%), 7 (88%) of which were abnormal. CSF studies demonstrated normal protein and white cell counts, but 25% had elevated kappa free light chains. As a result of this program, neuropsychiatric medications were optimized in 86% of patients and 8% had an escalation in immunotherapy. This multidisciplinary Neuro-Lupus Program model brings together neurologists, psychiatrists, rheumatologists, and neuropsychologists to standardize the approach to neurocognitive symptoms in SLE. Among the patients enrolled, this program detected previously undiagnosed cognitive impairment in the majority of those tested and was associated with changes in neuropsychiatric and immunotherapy management.

title: Functional and Structural Imaging Features of Cognitive Profiles in Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: Background and objectives Cognitive impairment affects 40%-70% of patients with multiple sclerosis (MS). Although recent hypothesis-driven and data-driven efforts have identified cognitive phenotypes, functional substrates underlying impairment in such phenotypes are still not clear. Our objective was to identify distinct cognitive phenotypes using clustering in a large cohort of patients with MS and characterize their associated clinical, structural MRI, and resting-state (RS) functional connectivity (FC) features. Methods We conducted an observational, cross-sectional study with right-handed patients with MS and age-matched and sex-matched healthy controls (HCs) who underwent neurologic and neuropsychological evaluation (Brief Repeatable Battery of Neuropsychological tests). Latent profile analysis on cognitive test Z-scores identified MS cognitive phenotypes. 3.0T MRI was used to derive atrophy measures and RS FC within default mode network (DMN I/II), executive control network (ECN), left/right fronto-parietal, language, and salience networks. Linear regression models compared structural MRI and RS FC across cognitive phenotypes and HCs, while polynomial contrasts assessed RS FC patterns across groups. Results Three hundred and sixty-nine patients with MS and 168 HCs were enrolled. Four cognitive phenotypes were detected: preserved cognition ([PC], n = 67[18.2%]), mild single-domain verbal fluency involvement (MSD-VF, n = 37[10.0%]), mild single-domain attention involvement (MSD-A, n = 197[53.4%]), and severe multidomain (SMD) involvement (SMD, n = 68[18.4%]). At corrected threshold, PC patients showed decreased deep gray matter (GM) volumes ( p < 0.001-0.001) and similar RS FC vs HCs, whereas MSD-VF exhibited no significant atrophy and no differences in RS FC vs HCs. MSD-A displayed lower cortical/deep GM volumes vs HCs ( p < 0.001-0.005), whereas SMD had worse clinical and atrophy features ( p < 0.001-0.04), as well as decreased DMN II RS FC ( p = 0.01-0.04) vs other groups. Polynomial contrast analyses revealed significant quadratic patterns with increased RS FC in MSD-VF vs HC/PC groups, followed by decrease in MSD-A and SMD, within DMN II ( p = 0.005), ECN ( p = 0.005), and language network ( p < 0.001). Discussion PC exhibited intact RS FC, whereas SMD presented widespread structural and DMN RS FC damage. These findings advance our understanding of cognitive heterogeneity in MS by revealing distinct structural and functional neuroimaging profiles across cognitive phenotypes, encouraging future longitudinal and multimodal investigations to improve disease characterization and prognostic stratification.

title: Portable Ultra-Low-Field MRI in Neurologic Diseases: Current Status and Potential in Clinical Practice, Research, and Trials.
abstract: Neurologic diseases are highly prevalent, and MRI plays a crucial role in their diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment monitoring. Conventional MRI at high magnetic field strength (≥1.5 tesla) is one of the most widely used modalities in clinical practice and a common outcome measure in clinical trials. Despite its importance and effectiveness, challenges, such as high cost, limited accessibility, and disease-related constraints, can hinder its widespread use. Recent advancements in portable ultra-low-field (<0.1 tesla) MRI technology offer potential solutions by enabling point-of-care brain imaging for neurologic diseases. However, the substantially lower magnetic field strength results in lower signal-to-noise ratio, reduced spatial resolution, and more limited imaging contrast, although ongoing computational approaches aim to mitigate some of these limitations. In this narrative review, we examine current evidence on applications of portable ultra-low-field MRI to neurologic disorders, discussing the technology's utility, limitations, and clinical implications. In addition, we highlight key open research questions and future opportunities for further integration of this emerging technology.

title: Spinal Cord and Nerve Root Involvement in Histiocytic Neoplasms: A Retrospective Observational Cohort Study.
abstract: Background and objectives Histiocytic neoplasms, including Erdheim-Chester disease (ECD), Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH), and Rosai-Dorfman-Destombes disease (RDD), have frequent nervous system involvement. The aim of this study was to characterize the neurologic, radiologic, and laboratory features of spinal cord and nerve root involvement in histiocytic neoplasms. Methods We evaluated patients with biopsy-proven ECD, LCH, or RDD seen at a tertiary referral center between January 1996 and December 2024. Patients were included if spinal MRI demonstrated spinal cord or nerve root involvement. Spinal MRI was performed for evaluation of myelopathic or radicular symptoms or as part of staging in patients with CNS involvement. We collected demographic variables, neurologic syndromes and imaging patterns, treatment characteristics, and outcomes including disability (Expanded Disability Status Scale [EDSS] score) and ambulatory status. The primary outcome was neurologic disability at nadir and last follow-up; secondary outcomes included radiographic patterns and clinical response to treatment. Data were summarized descriptively, with exploratory group comparisons performed using parametric or nonparametric tests as appropriate. Results Among 415 patients with ECD (n = 183), LCH (n = 144), or RDD (n = 88), spinal cord or nerve root involvement was identified in 42 (ECD, 27; LCH, 4; RDD, 11). The median age at onset was 43.1 years (interquartile range 32.1-58.5), and 18 (43%) were female. Most cases were symptomatic (36/42, 86%), with myelopathy as the first neurologic manifestation in 26 (72%). Parenchymal infiltration predominated in the ECD group (17/27, 63%), compared with LCH (2/4, 50%) and RDD (2/11, 18%) groups (Fisher exact test across groups, p = 0.035). Root involvement was more frequent in the RDD group (8/11, 73%) than in the ECD (7/27, 26%) or LCH (1/4, 25%) group (Fisher exact test across groups, p = 0.021). The median EDSS score at nadir was 4.0; 43% required ambulatory aid or worse. After treatment, 22 of 36 symptomatic patients (61%) improved clinically and radiographically, more often in RDD (10/11, 91%) and LCH (2/3, 67%) groups than in the ECD group (10/22, 46%; Fisher exact test across groups, p = 0.022). At a median 5.8-year follow-up, 8 of 38 survivors (21%) required ambulatory assistance or were nonambulatory. Discussion Spinal cord and nerve root involvement occurs in histiocytic neoplasms. These findings support prioritizing spinal MRI in patients with neurologic symptoms or high-risk disease features because early identification may inform diagnosis and management.

title: Association Between Plasma N-Terminal Tau, Cognitive Decline, and Neurodegeneration in the ADNI Cohort.
abstract: Background and objectives Blood-based biomarkers offer a cost-effective, minimally invasive alternative to neuroimaging and CSF biomarkers. Newly developed fluid biomarkers, including the N-terminal tau fragment (NT1), show promise for identifying individuals at risk for Alzheimer disease (AD) and for monitoring disease progression. Here, we determine whether NT1 levels are associated with key clinical and biomarker measures in a large, well-characterized cohort. Methods Participants from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) cohort with available plasma NT1, β-amyloid (Aβ)-PET, MRI, and clinical measures (Clinical Dementia Rating) were included in this observational study. NT1 was measured using the Quanterix Simoa HD-X platform. PET, MRI, clinical, and other plasma measures were obtained using established ADNI procedures. A subset also had NULISA-based plasma measures of amyloid and tau and tau-PET assessed. Linear regression and linear mixed-effects models were used to assess cross-sectional and longitudinal associations between NT1 and clinical or biomarker measures, adjusting for relevant covariates. Multivariable-adjusted Cox regression was performed to evaluate the association between baseline NT1 levels and risk of clinically diagnosed mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or AD. Mediation analysis was conducted to examine whether hippocampal atrophy mediates the relationship between NT1 and memory decline. Spearman correlations were used to examine continuous relationships between plasma NT1 and continuous fluid and neuroimaging markers. Results A total of 755 participants (mean age: 72.9 [7.0], female: 375 [50%]) were included in the study. Plasma NT1 levels were elevated in MCI/AD individuals (B MCI/AD [SE] = 0.09 [0.022], p = 1.98 × 10 -4 ) and were cross-sectionally associated with worse memory performance (B [SE] = -0.25 [0.09], p = 0.005). Aβ moderated the association between elevated NT1 and greater cognitive decline across multiple domains (memory: B [SE] = -0.17 [0.074], p = 0.022; executive function: B [SE] = -0.24 [0.082], p = 0.004; language: B [SE] = -0.21 [0.075], p = 0.006). NT1 levels were negatively associated with hippocampal volume (B [SE] = -264.49 [125.99], p = 0.036) and predicted longitudinal atrophy (B [SE] = -42.00 [16.90], p = 0.013). Accelerated hippocampal atrophy largely mediated the association between higher baseline NT1 level and greater memory decline (B [95% CI] indirect effect = -0.082 [-0.135 to -0.03], p = 0.003, B [95% CI] proportion mediated = 70.1% [32.6%-155.3%], p = 0.004). Higher NT1 levels were associated with higher levels of plasma biomarkers, including NULISA-based brain-derived (BD) plasma pTau (BD-pTau181, BD-pTau217, BD-pTau231: p 's < 5.01 × 10 -6 ) and Simoa-Based pTau181 ( p < 4.51 × 10 -15 ) and neurofilament light chain ( p < 5.34 × 10 -7 ). Discussion Plasma NT1 may be useful in assessing amyloid-dependent cognitive decline and neurodegeneration.

title: Pearls & Oy-sters: Diagnosis of Pediatric Tumefactive Multiple Sclerosis With MRI Biomarkers.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a demyelinating disease of the CNS with an estimated incidence of 0.05-2.85 per 100,000 children. One subtype, tumefactive MS, is particularly rare and difficult to diagnose, especially in differentiating from tumor. We describe the case of a 16-year-old boy who presented with subacute onset of headaches, cognitive difficulties, dizziness, blurry vision, right arm weakness, numbness, and gait difficulty. MRI of the brain demonstrated a multilobulated, contrast-enhancing, T2 hyperintense area of diffusion restriction in the left frontal lobe, an extensive left periventricular lesion, and multifocal T2/fluid-attenuated inversion recovery hyperintense lesions. He clinically improved with IV steroids and a 1-month oral steroid taper, and then, 2 weeks after completion of the taper, he experienced recurrent headaches and cognitive decline. Repeat brain MRI (3T) with MS protocol which included 3D T2* gradient recalled echo was notable for lesions demonstrating central vein sign (CVS) and paramagnetic rim-like areas within the large left frontal lesion characterized by positive phase shift and associated contrast enhancement. Based on the presence of typical symptoms, multiple enhancing and nonenhancing lesions in the periventricular and juxtacortical regions, and 6 CVS-positive lesions, the patient met 2024 McDonald criteria, and the diagnosis of MS was made. The patient was treated with IV steroids followed by oral steroids and then started on ocrelizumab. This case demonstrates how recognition of CVS is critical, because early and accurate diagnosis enables timely treatment without unnecessary interventions.

title: Association of Skin Denervation With Brain Atrophy and Cognitive Impairment in Patients With Parkinson Disease.
abstract: Background and objectives Small fiber pathology is an intrinsic feature of Parkinson disease (PD), yet its relevance to central neurodegeneration remains unclear. Given that cognitive impairment is a major manifestation of disease progression closely linked to cortical structural changes, we aimed to determine whether peripheral skin denervation is associated with cognitive impairment and brain atrophy in PD. Methods In this cross-sectional study at a movement disorders center in China, patients with PD and healthy controls (HCs) were recruited. Key inclusion criteria included a clinical PD diagnosis based on the Movement Disorder Society criteria and an age range of 50-99 years. Patients were classified into normal cognition (PD-NC), mild cognitive impairment (PD-MCI), and patients develop dementia (PDD). All participants underwent skin biopsy for quantification of intraepidermal nerve fiber density (IENFD), neuropsychological assessments, and structural MRI. Multivariable regression and mediation analyses examined associations among IENFD, cognition, and brain volumes. Results A total of 155 patients with PD (mean age, 63.4 years; 52% female; PD-NC: n = 75; PD-MCI: n = 40; PDD: n = 40) and 50 HCs (mean age, 60.3 years; 50% female) were included. IENFD demonstrated a progressive decline across the PD cognitive spectrum (HC: 7.18 ± 2.44; PD-NC: 5.89 ± 2.05; PD-MCI: 4.65 ± 1.33; PDD: 3.40 ± 1.15 fibers/mm). IENFD positively correlated with global and 5 domain-specific cognitive scores (β = 0.170-0.387, p < 0.05). Lower IENFD was independently associated with an increased risk of cognitive impairment (odds ratio = 0.541, 95% CI 0.420-0.697) and showed good diagnostic performance in distinguishing PD-MCI and PDD from PD-NC (area under the ROC curve = 0.772, 95% CI 0.697-0.838). Furthermore, IENFD correlated with frontal and insular gray matter volumes (β = 0.155-0.195, p < 0.05), which statistically mediated the associations between IENFD and cognitive performance (proportion mediated for global cognition: 8.0%-10.2%). Discussion Our study suggests that skin denervation is closely associated with cognitive impairment in PD and that regional brain atrophy statistically mediates this relationship. These findings provide novel evidence for the peripheral-central axis in PD, suggesting that small fiber pathology may mirror central neurodegeneration. Future multicenter and longitudinal studies are required for validation.

title: Clinical Factors Associated With Discordant Plasma P-Tau217 and Established Alzheimer Disease Biomarkers.
abstract: Background and objectives Plasma phosphorylated tau (p-tau) 217 is increasingly used for Alzheimer disease (AD) diagnosis and treatment decisions but may be discordant with established AD biomarkers. False-positive (FP) plasma results may lead to overtreatment and false-negative (FN) results to missed or delayed disease-modifying therapies. We evaluated factors associated with discordant results. Methods This retrospective study included participants enrolled in memory and aging studies at Mayo Clinic with "positive" (>0.324 pg/mL) or "negative" (<0.186 pg/mL) plasma p-tau217 results and confirmatory AD biomarkers. Plasma results were classified as true positive (TP), true negative (TN), FP, or FN, referencing amyloid-PET and CSF p-tau181/β-amyloid (Aβ) 42. Clinical and laboratory variables were compared using univariate analyses; multivariable logistic regression evaluated independent associations with discordance. Results Among 706 participants (median 70.0 [interquartile range 15.8] years; 54% male), 60 (8.5%) had discordant plasma p-tau217 results. FN results (5.6%) were more frequent than FP results (2.8%; p = 0.007). Discordance was associated with older age (odds ratio [OR] 1.61 per decade, 95% CI 1.23-2.14) and obstructive sleep apnea (OR 1.94, 95% CI 1.08-3.49). FN (vs TP) results were associated with milder clinical stage (global Clinical Dementia Rating [CDR] ≤0.5 vs CDR ≥1; p < 0.001), higher Mini-Mental State Examination scores (OR 1.20 per point, 95% CI 1.05-1.36), obstructive sleep apnea (OR 2.01, 95% CI 1.01-4.3), higher body mass index (OR 1.11/kg/m 2 , 95% CI 1.03-1.20), and higher estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR: OR 1.33/10 mL/min/1.73 m 2 , 95% CI 1.05-1.69). In age-adjusted models, body mass index (OR 1.14, 95% CI 1.03-1.25), eGFR (OR 1.63/10 mL/min/1.73 m 2 , 95% CI 1.22-2.16), and earlier clinical stage (CDR ≤0.5) were independently associated with FN results. FP (vs TN) results were associated with older age (OR 2.37, 95% CI 1.36-4.09), thyroid disease (OR 4.41, 95% CI 1.36-14.3), lower eGFR (OR 0.48/10 mL/min/1.73 m 2 , 95% CI 0.31-0.66), and advanced disease stage (CDR ≥1). In age-adjusted models, eGFR (OR 0.54/10 mL/min/1.73 m 2 , 95% CI 0.35-0.82) and advanced disease stage (CDR ≥ 1 vs CDR 0: OR 11.11, 95% CI 2.0-50.0; vs CDR 0.5: OR 4.55, 95% CI 1.12-16.67) were independently associated with FP results. Discussion Plasma p-tau217 results and established AD biomarkers were discordant in 8.5% of participants. Clinical stage and factors related to brain amyloid clearance, renal clearance, and volume of distribution were associated with discordant results. These insights may inform mechanisms of discordance and identify patients requiring confirmatory biomarker measures.

title: Acute Imbalance Syndrome vs Acute Vestibular Syndrome: Clinical and Topographical Differentiation.
abstract: Background and objectives Stroke is a major differential diagnosis in patients with acute vertigo/dizziness or imbalance. Current diagnostic algorithms such as head impulse test, gaze-evoked nystagmus, and test of skew are optimized for presentations with spontaneous nystagmus (SPN), traditionally called acute vestibular syndrome (AVS). However, in recent studies, a relevant proportion of patients with stroke-related vertigo/dizziness had no SPN, but rather postural or gait imbalance, a phenotype lately termed acute imbalance syndrome (AIS). We aimed to outline the pathoanatomical differences of stroke-related AIS vs AVS and its clinical implications. Methods Patients with MRI-proven stroke-related acute vertigo/dizziness or imbalance were included in this emergency department (ED) cohort study at LMU Hospital prospectively. Vestibular, ocular motor, and postural signs were documented (including SPN presence/intensity by video oculography, postural imbalance by posturography). Patients were classified as suffering from AIS or AVS based on the presence of SPN. Stroke lesion distribution was depicted in Montreal Neurological Institute space and supplemented by structural disconnectome mapping from the lesion cores. Multivariate lesion symptom-mapping based on support-vector regression and disconnectome mapping was applied for SPN intensity and sway path as surrogate markers for AVS and AIS. Results Of 75 patients (age: 65.7 ± 13.3 years, 40% female), 58.7% were diagnosed with AIS, 38.7% with AVS, and 2.7% with central positional vertigo. In AIS, the lesion core was located in the anterior cerebellar lobe and deep cerebellar nuclei (superior cerebellar artery/posterior inferior cerebellar artery territory) connecting to the bilateral pontomesencephalic tegmentum through the superior cerebellar peduncle. AVS stroke lesions were mostly located in the posterior cerebellar/flocculonodular lobe (posterior inferior cerebellar artery/anterior inferior cerebellar artery territory) and connected to the ipsilesional vestibular nucleus (VN) and bilateral medial longitudinal fascicle (MLF) through the inferior cerebellar peduncle. title: Differential Trajectories of Brain Atrophy in Multiple Sclerosis, MOGAD, and AQP4 + NMOSD: The Role of Disease Activity in MOGAD.
abstract: Background and objectives Multiple sclerosis (MS), myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD), and aquaporin-4 antibody-positive neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (AQP4 + NMOSD) are inflammatory demyelinating disorders with distinct mechanisms of tissue injury. MS is characterized by diffuse neurodegeneration, whereas damage in antibody-mediated diseases is considered attack related. In MOGAD, the relationship between disease activity and brain atrophy remains unclear. We aimed to compare longitudinal trajectories of global and regional brain atrophy across MS, MOGAD, and AQP4 + NMOSD and investigate whether atrophy in MOGAD is associated with disease course and lesion dynamics. Methods In this retrospective multicenter Magnetic Resonance Imaging in Multiple Sclerosis (MAGNIMS) study, patients fulfilling the following criteria were enrolled: (1) age 18 years or older, (2) MS/MOGAD/AQP4 + NMOSD diagnosis, (3) ≥2 same-scanner brain MRIs ≥6 months apart and ≥3 months postattack, (4) concurrent Expanded Disability Status Scale, and (5) disease course information. White matter lesions were segmented using the Lesion Segmentation Toolbox. Longitudinal brain volumes were quantified on lesion-filled T1-weighted images using Sequence Adaptive Multimodal SEGmentation (SAMSEG) with a within-subject template approach. In MOGAD, lesion dynamics were classified as stable/new lesions/lesion resolution. Linear mixed-effects models adjusted for age, sex, baseline volume, and center estimated atrophy rates. Results Overall, 489 participants from 15 centers were included (98 MS [mean age 39.79 years, 68.37% female], 72 MOGAD [42.14 years, 66.67%], 41 AQP4 + NMOSD [51.25 years, 87.80%], and 278 healthy controls [42.94 years, 61.87%]). The mean follow-up was MS: 2.44 ± 1.55 years, MOGAD: 2.57 ± 1.85, and AQP4 + NMOSD: 3.22 ± 2.42. Compared with controls, MS showed accelerated global brain atrophy (β = -2.027 cm 3 per year, 95% CI -3.430 to -0.623). MOGAD demonstrated white matter volume loss (β = -0.989, 95% CI -1.889 to -0.090) and ventricular enlargement (lateral: β = 0.219, 95% CI 0.089-0.350; third ventricle: β = 0.009, 95% CI 0.003-0.015). AQP4 + NMOSD showed pallidal volume reduction (β = -0.008, 95% CI -0.014 to -0.001). Within MOGAD, relapsing patients (62.5%) exhibited greater third ventricular expansion than MS (β = 0.009, 95% CI 0.001-0.017). MOGAD with new lesions (22.22%) had greater ventricular enlargement than controls (lateral: β = 0.359, 95% CI 0.147-0.572; third ventricle: β = 0.016, 95% CI 0.006-0.025), MS, and AQP4 + NMOSD. Discussion Each inflammatory demyelinating disease exhibits a characteristic pattern of brain atrophy. In MOGAD, neuroaxonal loss seems associated with inflammatory activity and lesion accrual, supporting an event-driven pattern of tissue injury rather than diffuse neurodegeneration. Limitations include small NMOSD sample, heterogeneous follow-up, and potential scanner-related variability.

title: Resting-State Functional MRI and Clinical Outcomes After Acute Disorders of Consciousness: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Background and objectives Accurate assessment and prognostication of patients with acute disorders of consciousness (DoC) after severe brain injury remain a substantial clinical challenge. Resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) measures spontaneous, temporally correlated brain activity in the absence of external stimulation and provides objective insight into the integrity of large-scale neural networks that support brain function. Emerging evidence suggests that assessing neural integrity using rs-fMRI may improve outcome prediction in patients with acute DoC. This review summarizes the current evidence of rs-fMRI as an assessment tool during the acute phase of severe brain injury. Methods Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, we conducted a systematic literature search using MEDLINE and Embase databases from January 2006 to March 2026. Eligible studies included peer-reviewed empirical investigations of adult patients with acute DoC (<28 days postinjury) that examined associations between rs-fMRI measures and clinical outcomes. The systematic review protocol was registered in the PROSPERO International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420251085923). Results Of 396 studies screened, 30 met eligibility criteria. Across these studies, a total of 800 patients (mean age = 48, 69% male) were scanned at a weighted average of 9.31 days after intensive care unit admission. Ten studies included patients exclusively with traumatic brain injury, 8 with cardiac arrest, 2 with encephalopathy, and 10 included mixed etiologies. The most frequently assessed resting-state networks were the default mode (n = 20) and executive control networks (n = 11), followed by visual (n = 6), salience (n = 6), sensorimotor (n = 6), and auditory (n = 5) networks. Across studies, significant associations between rs-fMRI measures and outcome were consistently reported, despite heterogeneity in methodology. The most commonly reported patient outcomes were functional or neurologic status, assessed at hospital discharge or between 3 and 12 months postinjury. Discussion Current evidence consistently demonstrates that rs-fMRI acquired during the acute phase of brain injury is associated with neurologic and functional outcomes in patients with DoC. In addition, rs-fMRI may help identify patients more likely to recover consciousness and achieve favorable functional outcomes by characterizing the integrity of large-scale brain networks. However, substantial heterogeneity and small sample sizes limit comparability across studies. Standardized acquisition and analysis frameworks, along with larger prospective studies, are needed to validate the clinical utility of rs-fMRI and support translation into an assessment tool after brain injury.

title: Diagnostic Performance of the Infrascanner 2000™ for Detecting Intracranial Hemorrhage in Traumatic Brain Injury Patients in Pakistan.
abstract: Background and objectives Intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality after traumatic brain injury (TBI). Computed tomography (CT) is often unavailable in low-resource settings, delaying diagnosis. The Infrascanner 2000™, a handheld near-infrared device, has been proposed as a rapid, noninvasive ICH screening tool. The objective of this study was to determine the diagnostic accuracy of the Infrascanner 2000™ for detecting ICH in TBI patients, compared with noncontrast CT, at 2 tertiary care hospitals in Peshawar, Pakistan. Methods In this prospective observational study, 141 patients with mild, moderate, or severe TBI presenting to the emergency department of Neurosurgery at Northwest General Hospital and Lady Reading Hospital, Peshawar, Pakistan, underwent Infrascanner examination (inter-rater kappa 0.82), followed by noncontrast CT as the reference standard. Sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, likelihood ratios, balanced accuracy, and overall accuracy were calculated. Balanced accuracy (mean of sensitivity and specificity) replaced area under the curve, as the device yields a single binary operating point. Results followed Standard for Reporting Diagnostic Accuracy Studies guidelines. Results CT confirmed hemorrhage in 125 of 141 patients (88.6%). The Infrascanner showed sensitivity of 91.2%, specificity of 50.0%, positive predictive value of 93.4%, negative predictive value of 42.1%, and overall accuracy of 86.5% (positive likelihood ratio 1.82; negative likelihood ratio 0.18). Balanced accuracy was 0.706 (95% CI: 0.626-0.786), a single operating point rather than a conventional receiver operating characteristic-derived area under the curve. True positives were predominantly superficial hematomas; false negatives may reflect small or deep lesions. False positives could reflect extracranial soft-tissue injury, though this was not formally graded. Conclusion The Infrascanner showed good sensitivity but modest specificity for ICH detection in this two-center Pakistani cohort, consistent with published series. It may serve as a rapid triage adjunct where CT access is delayed but should not replace CT imaging. Further multicenter studies, including prehospital settings, are warranted.

title: Safety and Efficacy of Repeat Surgery for Recurrent Craniopharyngiomas: A RAPID Consortium Collaboration.
abstract: Background and objectives Craniopharyngiomas (CPs) recur in 20% to 50% of cases after initial management. To date, there are no large multi-institutional series investigating outcomes in patients receiving surgery for recurrent CP. Here, we leverage the Registry of Adenomas of the Pituitary and Related Disorders to analyze outcomes after surgical treatment of recurrent CP. Methods Demographic, clinical, radiographic, surgical, and outcome variables were analyzed for 483 patients receiving surgery for primary or recurrent CP across 16 US-based academic skull-base centers comprising the Registry of Adenomas of the Pituitary and Related Disorders consortium from 2000 to 2024. Results Among the 483 patients, 360 (74.5%) had primary CP and 123 (25.5%) had recurrent CP. The recurrent cohort was younger at initial diagnosis (Padj < .01) and recurrence (Padj = .02). Adamantinomatous CPs were more common in the recurrent cohort but not significantly so, and 33.3% of cases had prior radiation therapy. Recurrent cases had more frequent preoperative endocrine dysfunction and hormone replacement (Padj < .01). Patients with recurrent CP had less frequent suprasellar tumor extension (Padj = .04) and more frequent preinfundibular/transinfundibular over retroinfundibular localization (Padj = .02). There were no differences in operative approach; endoscopic endonasal surgery was the most common, and procedures achieved similar distributions of gross and subtotal resection in both cohorts (Padj = .30) with similar low frequencies of unplanned reoperation and surgical complications. New postoperative arginine vasopressin deficiency (in patients without preoperative arginine vasopressin deficiency) was more common in the primary cohort (Padj = .04), but long-term follow-up demonstrated similar frequencies of endocrine dysfunction in both cohorts and comparably low rates (<25%) of future recurrence within an average follow-up period of 1.57 years (Padj= .17). Conclusion This study provides the largest comparative evaluation of patients undergoing surgery for recurrent vs primary CP. Despite prior treatment, patients with recurrent CP achieved comparable resection outcomes with similar rates of neuroendocrine dysfunction. These findings indicate surgical resection remains a safe and efficacious option for recurrent CP, especially as emerging targeted therapies become available.

title: White Matter Functional Disconnection Predicts Long-Term Disability and Early Mortality in Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
abstract: Background and objectives Spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) has the highest short-term mortality among stroke subtypes, and progress in treatment has been hindered by the limited accuracy of current prognostic tools. We investigated whether white matter functional disconnection severity, estimated using a normative lesion network mapping framework integrating direct electrical stimulation and resting-state functional MRI data from previously published independent Data sets, improves prediction of 6-month functional outcome measured with the modified Rankin Scale (mRS). Methods We analyzed 97 patients with spontaneous ICH. Ordinal logistic regression models were used to evaluate the association between domain-specific disconnection severity and 6-month mRS, and to compare traditional functional outcome in patients with primary intracerebral hemorrhage and ICH scores with connectivity-enriched models incorporating disconnection measures. Results White matter functional disconnectivity was significantly associated with 6-month functional outcome (mRS; P < .001; Nagelkerke's R2 = 0.507). Integrating disconnection severity into the functional outcome in patients with primary intracerebral hemorrhage and ICH scores improved predictive performance in both cases (Nagelkerke's R2 = 0.615 vs 0.389 and 0.651 vs 0.434, respectively), with the connectivity-enriched ICH score achieving the strongest overall fit across all models tested. Exploratory analyses showed associations between domain-specific disconnection severity, residual functional deficits, and early mortality. Conclusion Assessment of white matter functional disconnection severity seems to be a promising approach for predicting long-term disability after ICH, although prospective validation in larger multicenter cohorts is required before clinical implementation. The findings suggest that different brain networks exhibit variable vulnerability to injury and differential potential for functional recovery.

title: Styloidogenic Jugular Venous Compression Syndrome: A Rare Vascular Variant of Eagle Syndrome.
abstract: Styloidogenic jugular venous compression syndrome, a recently recognized vascular variant of Eagle syndrome, a rare condition caused by the elongation of the styloid process or calcification of the stylohyoid ligament, occurs when the internal jugular vein is compressed between the styloid process and C1 transverse process, leading to a spectrum of neurovascular and cervicofacial symptoms. A 46-year-old male pilot presented with right-sided pulsatile tinnitus, vertigo, and episodic near-syncope that progressively worsened over 4 years despite multiple interventions. Computed tomography and MRI revealed an elongated right styloid process (approximately 35 mm) compressing the internal jugular vein against the C1 transverse process. The patient underwent a right-sided styloidectomy with partial resection of the C1 transverse process by a transcervical approach. The facial and spinal accessory nerves were preserved, and postoperative recovery was uneventful. By postoperative day 2, the patient reported near-complete resolution of tinnitus and pain, with sustained improvement at 1-month follow-up. Styloidogenic jugular venous compression syndrome should be considered for patients with pulsatile tinnitus or symptoms of impaired cerebral venous outflow. Computed tomography venography is considered the diagnostic gold standard. Surgical decompression through styloidectomy with C1 resection can provide effective and durable symptom relief. Early diagnosis and surgical management can result in excellent outcomes.

title: A Semispinalis Cervicis-Sparing Intermuscular Approach for C2-3 Posterior Fixation.
abstract: Background and importance Preservation of the semispinalis cervicis insertion at the C2 spinous process is important for maintaining cervical extensor function and postoperative alignment. However, muscle-preserving approaches for posterior fixation at the C2-3 level remain technically challenging. Clinical presentation A 66-year-old man with a traumatic hangman's fracture underwent posterior C2-3 fixation using a semispinalis cervicis-sparing intermuscular approach. A natural connective tissue plane between the semispinalis capitis and semispinalis cervicis was developed, allowing exposure of C2 and C3 without detaching the semispinalis cervicis insertion. Instrumentation was successfully performed under intraoperative computed tomography-based navigation. Postoperative pain was minimal, and stable fixation was achieved without complications. Conclusion This case demonstrates that the semispinalis cervicis-sparing intermuscular approach provides a feasible muscle-preserving corridor for C2-3 fixation and may represent a useful alternative in selected patients.

title: Internal Jugular Compression Syndrome Because of Compression Between the Styloid Process and C1 Transverse Process: Clinical Presentation, Diagnosis, and Management.
abstract: Background and objectives Internal jugular vein (IJV) compression at the skull base represents a rare cause of cerebral venous outflow obstruction and may mimic Eagle's syndrome. Unlike classic Eagle's syndrome, this condition results from venous compression between the hypertrophic C1 transverse process and the styloid process, producing symptoms such as pulsatile tinnitus, headache, and cognitive disturbances. We describe our experience highlighting the diagnostic protocol and management strategies. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 5 patients with symptomatic IJV compression syndrome. Demographics, clinical presentation, and treatment outcomes were analyzed. Diagnostic evaluation included computed tomography venography, duplex ultrasonography with head rotation, and cerebral angiography. Four (80%) patients underwent microsurgical decompression of the IJV through a posterolateral suboccipital approach with resection of the hypertrophic C1 transverse process and decompression of the V2-V3 vertebral artery. One patient was managed conservatively. Results The mean age was 57 years (3 females, 2 males). The mean symptom duration was 7.2 years. Presenting symptoms included pulsatile tinnitus, headache, dizziness, syncope, ear pain, and cognitive complaints. Two patients (40%) had undergone previous treatment without symptom relief. Postoperatively, 3 patients (75%) experienced complete resolution of symptoms and one demonstrated partial symptom improvement with persistent tinnitus attributable to neurovascular compression of cranial nerve VIII. Imaging confirmed restoration of IJV patency in all cases. One patient had spontaneous symptom resolution because of extensive venous collaterals. One patient developed intraoperative vertebral artery dissection because of atherosclerosis which was managed by endarterectomy and reconstruction with Hemashield patch. Conclusion IJV compression syndrome caused by the hypertrophic C1 transverse process is a distinct clinical condition that should be considered in patients with refractory pulsatile tinnitus or suspected venous intracranial hypertension. Computed tomography venography of head and neck along with head rotation is critical for diagnosis. Microsurgical decompression through a posterolateral far-lateral approach provides effective symptom relief and durable restoration of venous outflow.

title: Mid- to Long-Term Visual Outcomes After Surgical Treatment of Cavernous Sinus Meningioma.
abstract: Background and objectives Cavernous sinus meningiomas (CSMs) are surgically challenging due to their proximity to the internal carotid artery and multiple cranial nerves, and long-term visual trajectories after treatment remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to define mid- to long-term outcomes, with an emphasis on temporal patterns of visual change, in patients undergoing surgical treatment for CSMs. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 30 patients with CSM who underwent initial surgical treatment between April 2004 and October 2024. Clinical, radiological, and pathological data were reviewed, including surgical approach, extent of resection, optic canal decompression, complications, adjuvant radiotherapy, tumor control, visual outcomes, and Karnofsky Performance Status score. Extent of resection was calculated volumetrically using contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging. Visual outcomes were evaluated at 4 to 6 months postoperatively and at final follow-up. Results The median age was 56 years, and 76.7% were women. Radical intracavernous resection was not attempted. Optic canal decompression was performed in 20 patients. World Health Organization grade 1 tumors accounted for 92.6% of cases. Median follow-up was 81.0 months, and the mean number of surgeries was 1.7 per patient. Early visual improvement was observed in 7 of 11 patients (63.6%) with preoperative deficits. Four patients (13.3%) developed severe visual deterioration to perception of hand motion or worse, with a mean time to event of 94 months; all had received radiotherapy. Tumor irradiation with radiosurgery or radiotherapy provided durable tumor control in selected cases but was associated with higher rates of progression, reflecting selection bias. The mean final Karnofsky Performance Status score was 81.0. Conclusion These findings suggest the possibility of a biphasic visual trajectory after surgical management of CSM. Optic canal decompression may facilitate early visual improvement, although delayed visual deterioration can occur despite prolonged disease control, as observed in a limited number of patients. A function-preserving, multimodal strategy may optimize long-term outcomes.

title: Development and Validation of a Human Cadaveric Model for Lobar Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
abstract: Background and objectives To develop and validate an anatomically accurate human cadaveric intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) model that replicates the radiographic and mechanical properties of spontaneous lobar ICH, enabling training and testing of minimally invasive surgical evacuation techniques. Methods Human-derived thrombi were created using mixtures of banked human packed red blood cells, fresh-frozen plasma, and iodinated contrast. Thrombi with physiologic viscoelastic properties were identified through rheometric analysis benchmarked against patient-derived intraoperative ICH specimens. Fresh, never-frozen cadaveric head-and-neck specimens were obtained via the institutional willed body program. After partial embalming, transorbital surgical corridors enabled clot placement in the frontal, temporal, and parietal lobes, while an infratentorial midline mini-craniotomy was used to insert occipital lobe clots. Results Human-derived clots composed of 95% fresh-frozen plasma most closely mimicked the mechanical properties of real ICH specimens. Transorbital and occipital approaches allowed for precise, reproducible hematoma placement. Flat-panel computed tomography imaging provided sufficient radiodensity contrast to delineate the clot from the surrounding brain parenchyma. Conclusion We report the first human cadaveric lobar ICH model using rheologically validated, surgically implanted human-derived clots. This model provides a reproducible platform for device evaluation, procedural development, and training in minimally invasive surgical evacuation of ICH.

title: SurgiCorr: A Physics-Based Computational Framework for Patient-Specific Surgical Corridor Planning in Brain Tumor Surgery.
abstract: Background and objectives Transcortical corridor selection is guided by anatomic intuition and neuronavigation, with no quantitative tool to estimate retraction injury to brain tissue. Such injury depends on corridor-specific tissue properties, opening width, and hold duration, variables existing systems do not model. We present SurgiCorr, a preoperative framework that generates patient-specific corridor candidates, simulates each biomechanically, and ranks them by a composite risk score (CRS) integrating strain, viscoelastic dose, imaging burden, and ventricular proximity. Methods MRI volumes were resampled to isotropic resolution, segmented into 5 tissue classes, and meshed with per-element material properties. A surgeon-defined cortical entry patch was sampled to generate candidate corridors, each evaluated by parallel finite element analysis at 4 opening widths (4, 6, 8, and 12 mm). Four risk metrics were computed per corridor: volumetric cumulative strain injury (mm3), strain damage index, damage escalation metric (mm-1), and viscoelastic damage dose. These were combined with fluid-attenuated inversion recovery burden and ventricular proximity into a normalized CRS. Results In a pediatric supratentorial tumor and an adult with multiple deep-seated metastases, the pipeline generated 176 and 68 candidate corridors, and completed 704 and 272 finite element modeling solves in 68/9 and 28/3 minutes (central processing unit/graphics processing unit), respectively. CRS spanned 0.025 to 0.819 and 0.134 to 0.694 across the 2 cases (case means 0.395 and 0.379), respectively, with the highest-quartile corridors flagged AVOID in each. Viscoelastic damage dose separated the lowest- from the highest-risk corridor by 2.2- and 1.4-fold, respectively. Cortical heatmap produced spatially coherent risk zones. All risk labels are relative to the candidate distribution for the individual patient and do not imply an absolute threshold of mechanical safety. Conclusion SurgiCorr demonstrates the feasibility of physics-based preoperative corridor planning that quantifies retraction injury as a patient-specific, time-integrated biomechanical dose. Prospective clinical validation against surgical outcomes is required before deployment.

title: Validation of Magnetic Resonance Brain Thermometry and Bioheat Modeling of Brain Temperature Using Direct Measurements With an Implanted Fiber Optic Probe.
abstract: Background and objectives Brain temperature is a promising marker of prognosis after injury. Although magnetic resonance (MR) thermometry and biophysical modeling can approximate absolute temperature, limited validation has been performed with direct measurements in a large animal model. The goal of this pilot study was to compare brain temperature measured using MR chemical shift thermometry (CST) and biophysical modeling with that measured using a fiber optic probe in a porcine model. Methods MR data were acquired from a Yorkshire pig using a 3 T whole body MR scanner, with simultaneous monitoring of brain and body temperature using a fiber optic probe surgically implanted in the left thalamus and a rectal temperature probe, respectively. MR spectroscopy was acquired for CST. T1-weighted images and MR angiography and venography were acquired for biophysical modeling. Temperature was calculated using the chemical shift difference between water and N-acetylaspartate. Using MR input data of tissue and vessel structures, along with bioheat equations, whole brain temperatures were predicted. Brain temperatures measured using CST, biophysical modeling, and direct measurements from the fiber optic probe, along with rectal temperatures, were compared. Results Brain temperature measured using CST was 39.9°C, whereas that measured using the implanted probe was 40.6°C in the left thalamus. Modeled brain temperature, averaged across all voxels in the left thalamus, was 40.1 ± 0.2°C. The difference between brain temperatures measured using CST and modeled temperature was -0.2°C. Brain temperatures from all 3 methods were equal to or higher than the mean rectal temperature during CST (39.9°C, range = 39.6-40.2°C). The difference between brain temperatures measured using the implanted probe and CST was 0.7°C, whereas the difference between probe-measured and modeled temperature was 0.5°C, on the same order as CST (±0.8°C) and probe accuracy (±0.3°C). Conclusion Brain temperature quantification using CST and biophysical modeling showed strong agreement with ground truth measurements using a fiber optic probe, providing initial validation of both methods to quantify absolute brain temperature.

title: Impact of Neoadjuvant Immunotherapy Combined with Chemotherapy on Surgical Margin Strategy in Central Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer.
abstract: Background The CheckMate 816 trial showed that neoadjuvant immunotherapy combined with chemotherapy improved pathological complete response and tumor downstaging compared with chemotherapy alone. Whether this permits less extensive resection, such as reduced margins, without compromising survival remains unclear. Methods We included 142 patients with central-type non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who received neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy at three hospitals between 2017 and 2022. All were initially considered candidates for sleeve lobectomy (SLT) based on pretreatment findings. After treatment, patients with residual disease confined to the segmental bronchus and/or distal pulmonary parenchyma were considered eligible for lobectomy (LT). Patients underwent SLT or LT according to pretreatment or post-treatment tumor extent, respectively. Negative margins were confirmed by intraoperative frozen-section pathology. Propensity score weighting (PSW) was used to balance baseline characteristics. Results Of the 142 enrolled patients, 86 had a radiographic response, with bronchoscopy revealing tumor regression to the segmental bronchus or more proximal airways. Ultimately, 82 patients underwent surgery, seven of whom were lost to follow-up during the follow-up period. Among 75 patients, 30 (40.0%) underwent SLT and 45 (60.0%) converted to LT. Grade II-V complications occurred in one case (2.22%) in the LT group and seven cases (23.3%) in the SLT group (relative risk 0.09; 95% confidence interval 0.01-0.57; p < 0.05). After PSW, baseline characteristics were balanced between groups (p > 0.05). PSW-adjusted event-free survival showed no significant difference between groups (hazard ratio 0.53; 95% confidence interval 0.13-2.22; p > 0.05). Conclusion For central-type NSCLC initially planned for SLT, conversion to LT is feasible when adequate negative margins are confirmed after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy, potentially avoiding more extensive surgery.

title: A Novel Tumor Burden Index to Predict the Prognosis in Stage IA Lung Adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Background This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic utility of a novel tumor burden index (TBI) for patients with pathologic stage IA lung adenocarcinoma after complete resection. Methods This study retrospectively analyzed 994 patients with stage IA lung adenocarcinoma who underwent preoperative chest computed tomography (CT) and curative resection. The TBI was derived from radiologic evaluation. Survival outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier estimates and Cox proportional hazards models. Results During a median follow-up period of 60.6 months, 13.6% of the patients experienced recurrence. Multivariable analysis identified TBI, predominant histologic subtype, surgery extent, spread through air spaces (STAS), and consolidation-to-tumor ratio (CTR) as independent predictors of recurrence-free survival (RFS). Optimal TBI cutoffs of 1.6 and 8.0 stratified patients into three distinct prognostic groups with significantly different RFS and overall survival rates. The TBI demonstrated superior prognostic discrimination compared with tumor diameter or volume. Subgroup analysis showed that for patients with low TBI, sublobar resection achieved RFS comparable with lobectomy, whereas anatomic resection provided outcomes superior to those of wedge resection in the intermediate- and high-TBI groups (segmentectomy vs. wedge resection: hazard ratio [HR], 0.36; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.14-0.89; P = 0.027; lobectomy vs. wedge resection: HR, 0.34; 95% CI 0.17-0.67; P = 0.002). Conclusions The novel TBI is a robust prognostic marker in stage IA lung adenocarcinoma and may inform personalized surgical strategy based on individualized risk assessment.

title: Recommendations for the Multimodal Management of Malignant Bowel Obstructions: Results of a North American Multidisciplinary Delphi Consensus.
abstract: Background Malignant bowel obstruction (MBO) is a challenging clinical problem requiring teams to balance complex oncologic disease, limited treatment options, and patient prognosis and values as they approach end of life. Presently, there is limited high-quality evidence to guide decision-making for MBO patients. Objective A multidisciplinary modified Delphi process was undertaken to create guidance and support clinical decision-making in the medical and surgical care of this patient population. Methods Multidisciplinary experts from all specialties regularly caring for MBO in Canada and the United States were invited for participation, including Acute Care Surgery, Surgical Oncology, Gynecologic Oncology, Gastroenterology, Radiology, Medical Oncology, and Palliative Care. Statements were evaluated through two rounds of surveys and a consensus meeting, with an a priori threshold of 80% agreement for approval. Results Forty-nine final evidence-informed statements were included following expert consensus review pertaining to Patient Assessment, Medical Management, Surgical Management, and Palliative Management, in addition to a unifying definition of MBO. Consensus statements address aspects of complex MBO care, including but not limited to, optimal preoperative evaluation and multidisciplinary review; timing and use of steroids, motility, and antisecretory agents; contraindications to surgery; key facets of consent and perioperative decision making; framework for the nuanced use of gastrostomies and IV fluids in the end-of-life setting. Conclusions This Modified Delphi consensus provides multidisciplinary evidence-based recommendations for the care of patients with this challenging problem. These expert approved statements provide much-needed clinical guidance to support best care balanced with patient values and avoidance of undue harm.

title: Full-Field Optical Coherence Tomography for Immediate Analysis of Prostate Biopsy Cores: A New Step toward Real-Time Cancer Diagnosis.
abstract: Background Surgical treatment of prostate cancer (PCa) is becoming increasingly personalized, requiring precise intraprostatic tumor mapping, offered by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and fusion biopsies. Thus, a real-time histological assessment tool could be useful to improve intraoperative management of oncological margins. Full-field optical coherence tomography (FFOCT) enables real-time tissue analysis. The objective of our study was to assess the accuracy of urologists' diagnosis of PCa on FFOCT images from prostate biopsy cores. Patients and methods A total of 91 patients undergoing prostatic biopsies were included. All cores were imaged for the FFOCT analysis (991 cores). FFOCT images were analyzed by two urologists and two urology residents. The FFOCT analysis included the presence of PCa and clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa), i.e., International Society of Urological Pathology (ISUP) ≥ 2. Results were compared with the histological analysis. Results All 991 cores were analyzed. Among them, 236 cores (24%) were positive for PCa and 37 cores (3.7%) for csPCa. For csPCa detection, sensitivity and specificity were 41.4% and 88.1% respectively, negative predictive value was 97.5%, and global accuracy was 86.4%. Interreader reproducibility was moderate (κ = 0.46; 95% CI 0.37-0.48). Clustering-adjusted and patient-level analyses yielded similar results. Conclusions Our results demonstrate that FFOCT is feasible, reproducible, and can be interpreted directly by urologists. The high negative predictive value observed for clinically significant prostate cancer suggests a potential role for real-time prostate tissue assessment. Further prospective studies are required to validate these findings and explore future clinical applications.
